# `useI18nHead`

`useI18nHead()` changes the SEO tags the module generates, for one page only. Use it when a page knows better than the router: a CMS article that exists in some locales only, a canonical URL from an API, extra `og:` tags. You get the generated tags with your overrides merged on top.

## Signature

```ts
useI18nHead(input?: MaybeRefOrGetter<I18nHeadInput | null>): { pageHead: any; resetPageHead: () => void }
```

Register page-level overrides for i18n SEO head tags.
Merged on top of `useLocaleHead` output by the `02.meta` plugin.

Prefer a getter (`() => ({ … })`) when values come from `$t` / `t` so they
re-resolve on locale change. A plain object is evaluated once and stays frozen.

::field-group
:field{name="input" type="MaybeRefOrGetter<I18nHeadInput | null>"}
::

It works with [`meta: true`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#meta) (the default): the module's meta plugin merges the input over the [`useLocaleHead`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/composables/useLocaleHead) output on every head render. With `meta: false` nothing reads it.

The override is reset when the route name changes. A page that sets `disableMeta` gets no i18n tags at all, overrides included.

## Input

`I18nHeadInput` (from `@i18n-micro/types`):

| Key                    | Type                     | Effect                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `htmlAttrs`            | `Record<string, string>` | Merged into the `<html>` attributes (`lang`, `dir`).                                                                                                                           |
| `meta`                 | `I18nHeadMeta[]`         | Added after the generated tags; replaces a tag with the same `id`, `property` or `name`.                                                                                       |
| `link`                 | `I18nHeadLink[]`         | Added after the generated links; replaces a link with the same `id`, or `rel` + `hreflang`.                                                                                    |
| `replace.canonical`    | `string | false`         | Replace the canonical `href`, or remove the link.                                                                                                                              |
| `replace.hreflang`     | `I18nHeadLink[] | false` | Replace or remove **every** `rel="alternate"` link, `x-default` included.                                                                                                      |
| `replace.xDefault`     | `I18nHeadLink | false`   | Replace or remove the `x-default` link.                                                                                                                                        |
| `replace.ogLocale`     | `string | false`         | Replace or remove `og:locale`.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `replace.ogUrl`        | `string | false`         | Replace or remove `og:url`.                                                                                                                                                    |
| `replace.ogAlternates` | `string[] | false`       | Rebuild `og:locale:alternate` from these locale codes (via `og` / `iso`), skipping the current locale, unknown codes and codes without an `og` or `iso` value, or remove them. |
| `disable`              | `I18nHeadDisableGroup[]` | Drop generated groups: `'hreflang'` (not `x-default`), `'x-default'`, `'canonical'`, `'og'` (`og:locale` + `og:url`), `'og-alternates'`, `'html'`.                             |

Order of application: `disable`, then `replace`, then `htmlAttrs`, `meta`, `link`.

## Example

An article that exists in some locales only, with alternate URLs from the API:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const route = useRoute()
const { t } = useI18n()
const { data: article } = await useFetch<{ title: string; urls: Record<string, string> }>(`/api/articles/${route.params.slug}`)

useI18nHead(() => {
  if (!article.value) return null
  const codes = Object.keys(article.value.urls)
  return {
    meta: [{ property: 'og:title', content: article.value.title || t('blog.title') }],
    replace: {
      hreflang: codes.map((code) => ({ rel: 'alternate', hreflang: code, href: article.value!.urls[code]! })),
      ogAlternates: codes,
    },
  }
})
</script>
```

Pass a getter, as here, when values come from `t()` or async data: it re-runs on locale change. A plain object is read once.

  :::card

  ---
  What the module generates and how to configure it
  :::

  :::card

  icon: i-lucide-braces

  ---

  :::

# `useI18nLocale`

`useI18nLocale()` gives access to the locale the app has chosen: the `i18n-locale` state and the locale cookie. Use it in a plugin that detects the locale itself (domain, user profile, header) instead of writing `useState('i18n-locale')` or the cookie by hand. Its validity checks use the enabled locales, runtime overrides included.

## Signature

```ts
useI18nLocale(): { getEffectiveLocale: (route: unknown, getLocaleFromRoute: GetLocaleFromRoute) => string; getLocale: () => string | null; getPreferredLocale: () => string | null; hashCookie: CookieRef; isValidLocale: (locale: string | null | undefined) => locale is string; locale: any; localeCookie: CookieRef; resolveInitialLocale: (options: ResolveInitialLocaleOptions) => string; setLocale: (locale: string | null) => void; syncLocale: (locale: string | null) => void; validLocales: string[] }
```

Centralized entry point for i18n locale management.
Combines useState('i18n-locale'), locale cookie, and sync utilities.

## Returned values

| Member                                          | Type                                               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`                                        | `Ref<string | null>`                               | The `useState('i18n-locale')` ref.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `localeCookie`                                  | `Ref<string | null>`                               | The [`localeCookie`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#localecookie) cookie; a plain `{ value: null }` when the option is `null`.                                           |
| `hashCookie`                                    | `Ref<string | null>`                               | The `hash-locale` cookie under hash routing; `{ value: null }` otherwise.                                                                                                                           |
| `validLocales`                                  | `string[]`                                         | Codes of the enabled locales.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `setLocale(locale)`                             | `(locale: string | null) => void`                  | Write the state and the cookies. Does not validate and does not load translations.                                                                                                                  |
| `syncLocale(locale)`                            | `(locale: string | null) => void`                  | Write the cookies only.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `getLocale()`                                   | `() => string | null`                              | State, then the preference cookie (hash cookie under hash routing). Not validated.                                                                                                                  |
| `getPreferredLocale()`                          | `() => string | null`                              | The first **valid** of state and preference cookie, or `null`.                                                                                                                                      |
| `getEffectiveLocale(route, getLocaleFromRoute)` | `(route, fn) => string`                            | The state under hash routing when set; otherwise `getLocaleFromRoute(route)`.                                                                                                                       |
| `resolveInitialLocale(options)`                 | `(options: ResolveInitialLocaleOptions) => string` | `options.urlLocale`, then a valid state, then `options.serverLocale`, then the route's locale. Stores the result in the state when the state is not valid; on the client it also writes the cookie. |
| `isValidLocale(locale)`                         | `(locale) => locale is string`                     | Whether `locale` is in `validLocales`.                                                                                                                                                              |

The cookies last one year, with `path: '/'` and `sameSite: 'lax'`.

## Example

```ts
// plugins/locale-from-domain.server.ts
export default defineNuxtPlugin({
  name: 'locale-from-domain',
  enforce: 'pre',
  setup() {
    const { setLocale, isValidLocale } = useI18nLocale()
    const host = useRequestURL().hostname // e.g. de.example.com
    const code = host.split('.')[0]
    if (isValidLocale(code)) setLocale(code)
  },
})
```

The module's loader plugin reads the state when it starts, so a plugin that sets it must run first (`enforce: 'pre'`). How the state competes with the URL, the cookie and `Accept-Language`: [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection). Full walkthrough: [Custom detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-auto-detect).

`setLocale()` does not switch the translations on screen. To change the locale of the current page, call [`$switchLocale()`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods#switchlocale).

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Custom detection" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-auto-detect"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Locale detection" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-braces" title="useI18n" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/composables/useI18n"}
::


# `useLocaleHead`

`useLocaleHead()` builds the i18n head tags for the current route: `lang` and `dir` on `<html>`, a canonical link, `hreflang` alternates with `x-default`, `og:url`, `og:locale` and `og:locale:alternate`. Use it when you set [`meta: false`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#meta) and manage `useHead` yourself; with `meta: true` the module already registers these tags, and per-page changes go through [`useI18nHead`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/composables/useI18nHead).

## Signature

```ts
useLocaleHead(options: UseLocaleHeadOptions): { build: () => LocaleHead; metaObject: Ref<{ htmlAttrs: { dir?: "ltr" | "rtl" | "auto"; lang?: string; [key: string]: string | undefined }; link: ({ href: string; rel: "canonical"; [key: string]: string | undefined } | { href: string; hreflang: string; rel: "alternate"; [key: string]: string | undefined })[]; meta: { content: string; property: string; [key: string]: string }[] }, LocaleHead | { htmlAttrs: { dir?: "ltr" | "rtl" | "auto"; lang?: string; [key: string]: string | undefined }; link: ({ href: string; rel: "canonical"; [key: string]: string | undefined } | { href: string; hreflang: string; rel: "alternate"; [key: string]: string | undefined })[]; meta: { content: string; property: string; [key: string]: string }[] }>; updateMeta: () => void }
```

The SEO head tags for the current route: `hreflang` alternates for every locale plus
`x-default`, a canonical link, `og:locale`, and `lang`/`dir` on `<html>`.

Only needed when `meta` is disabled or the defaults need adjusting — with `meta: true`
the module registers the same tags itself.

::field-group
  :::field{required name="options" type="UseLocaleHeadOptions"}
  :::
::

**Returns** — `metaObject`, a ref holding the head object ready to pass to `useHead`; `updateMeta` refreshes it; `build` computes the head object from the current route (reactive when read in a getter, e.g. `useHead(() => build())`)

```ts
const { metaObject } = useLocaleHead({ addSeoAttributes: true })
useHead(metaObject)
```

## Options

| Option                | Default | Description                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `addDirAttribute`     | `true`  | Set `dir` on `<html>` from the locale's `dir` (`'auto'` when it has none).                                                            |
| `identifierAttribute` | `'id'`  | Attribute that keys each tag (`i18n-can`, `i18n-og`, `i18n-alternate-<hreflang>`, …), so updates replace tags instead of adding them. |
| `addSeoAttributes`    | `true`  | Emit canonical, `hreflang` and `og:` tags. `false` keeps only `htmlAttrs`.                                                            |
| `baseUrl`             | `'/'`   | Origin joined to every URL. Keep `'/'` for relative URLs; pass `'https://example.com'` for absolute ones.                             |
| `autoUpdate`          | `true`  | Rebuild `metaObject` when the route or the `i18n-locale` state changes.                                                               |

## What it emits

- Nothing on a route with no match (404) or with `disableMeta` for the active locale.
- Canonical and `og:url`: `$switchLocalePath(<active locale>)`, query reduced to [`canonicalQueryWhitelist`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#canonicalquerywhitelist), [`trailingSlash`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#trailingslash) applied.
- `hreflang`: one link per enabled locale the page exists in, `hreflang = iso || code`, skipping locales with `seo: false`; with `hreflangBaseLanguage: true` the first regional locale of a language also emits its bare-language tag. None under `no_prefix`.
- `x-default`: the default locale's URL, unless the strategy is `no_prefix`, the default locale has `seo: false`, or the page does not exist in it.
- `og:locale` / `og:locale:alternate`: from the locale's `og`, or its `iso` converted (`en-US` → `en_US`); skipped with a dev warning when neither works.

## Example

```ts
// app.vue, with i18n.meta: false
const { metaObject } = useLocaleHead({ baseUrl: 'https://example.com' })
useHead(metaObject)
```

`build()` returns the same object without the ref: `useHead(() => build())` stays reactive without a watcher.

  :::card
  ---

  title: SEO
  to: https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo
  ---
  Base URL resolution, `metaBaseUrl`, per-locale `seo` / `og`
  :::

  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-lucide-braces

  :::

# Architecture

This page follows a translation from the JSON file in `locales/` to `$t()` on screen, and names the file behind each step. Read it before you change the build, the server loader, the payload route or the client storage. App authors do not need it: the supported knobs are listed under [Public surface](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#public-surface), and the [Guide](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations) explains them.

## Overview

![Locale JSON files are built into a payload tree, stored in public/ on Node or in server assets on Edge, read by a server loader, then used by $t on the server and fetched for $t in the browser](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/diagrams/translation-pipeline.svg)

## Build

| Step                                                                                                                                                                     | Source                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Layers are read in order (extended layers first, the project last); `additionalTranslationDirs` before `translationDir`                                                  | `src/module.ts` (`rootDirs`)                                                            |
| `premerged` (default): root + page + fallback chain merged into one `{page}/{locale}/data.json` per page and locale, in `.nuxt/i18n-merged`                              | `src/build/build.ts` (`preMergeLocales`)                                                |
| `source`: a compact copy of the source files in `.nuxt/i18n-source`, merged per request at runtime                                                                       | `src/build/build.ts` (`buildTranslationSourceLayers`), `@i18n-micro/utils/merge-source` |
| Fallback chain: global `fallbackLocale`, then each locale's `fallbackLocale` link, then the locale                                                                       | `@i18n-micro/utils/merge-source` (`buildFallbackLocaleChain`)                           |
| `dateBuild`: a hash of the translation files unless set                                                                                                                  | `src/module.ts` (`resolveDateBuild`), `src/build/payload-stats.ts`                      |
| Templates: `#build/i18n.strategy.mjs` (public config + `createI18nStrategy`), `i18n.config.mjs` (private config, Nitro alias `#i18n-internal/config`), `i18n.plural.mjs` | `src/module.ts` (`registerI18nTemplates`), `src/plural-template.ts`                     |

Where the tree goes depends on the Nitro preset, decided in `nitro:init`. A preset that serves `public/` from disk (`node-server`) gets the tree copied to `public/<apiBaseUrl>/` and reads it with `readFile` (`src/runtime/server/payload-source.fs.ts`). Edge, function and `serveStatic: "inline"` presets embed it as Nitro `serverAssets` under `assets:i18n` (`payload-source.assets.ts`). Both readers reject paths that leave the payload root.

## Server

- **Middleware** `src/runtime/server/middleware/i18n.global.ts` runs on every request except internals (`/api`, `/_nuxt`, `/__*`, the payload route, static files). It detects the request locale once (`detectRequestLocale` in `server/utils/locale-detector.ts`) and stores `event.context.i18n = { locale, translations, load, config }`. `translations` is the `index` chunk when `serverTranslationPreload` is on.
- **Loader** `server/utils/server-loader.ts` (`loadTranslationsFromServer(locale, page)`): in dev it reads the live files on every call; with `apiBaseServerHost` it fetches the payload from that host; otherwise it reads through `#i18n-internal/payload-source` (one file in `premerged`, a runtime merge in `source`). A premerged page without its own folder shares the root entry, so made-up page names cannot add entries. With `cacheStorage`, `server/internal/shared-cache.ts` sits between the process cache and the source, unless the dictionaries are embedded and no host is set.
- **Server cache** `server/internal/server-translation-cache.ts`: one LRU `CacheControl` per process on `globalThis[Symbol.for('__NUXT_I18N_SERVER_CACHE_CC__')]`, at most `cacheMaxSize` entries (1000 when unset), `cacheTtl` from write. Entries hold the data and its pre-serialized JSON; concurrent loads of one key share one read. It is emptied on restart and, in dev, whenever a translation file changes (`translation-watcher.ts`).
- **Route** `server/routes/i18n.ts` serves `/{apiBaseUrl}/:page/:locale/data.json` from the loader's pre-serialized JSON, 404 for a disabled or unknown locale. Outside dev, when `httpCacheDuration` is above 0, it sets `public, max-age=<httpCacheDuration>, immutable` only when the request's `?v=` equals `dateBuild`; otherwise `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. At `httpCacheDuration: 0` it sends no `Cache-Control` header.

## Client and SSR runtime

- **Loader plugin** `src/runtime/plugins/01.plugin.ts` resolves the initial locale, configures storage, loads the first chunk and registers the helpers. During SSR the chunk comes from `event.context.i18n.load` (no HTTP); dictionaries are never written into the HTML payload. The server adds a `<link rel="preload" as="fetch">` for the chunk the browser will fetch while hydrating.
- **`TranslationStorage`** `src/runtime/utils/storage.ts`: a module-level instance whose `CacheControl` lives on `globalThis[Symbol.for('__NUXT_I18N_STORAGE_CC__')]`, keyed `locale:routeName`. On the server a chunk's root is frozen in place, because every request shares it; the browser stores the object it fetched. Bounded by `cacheMaxSize` (1000 on the server when unset, unbounded in the browser), expired by `cacheTtl`.
- **`NuxtI18n`** `src/runtime/utils/nuxt-i18n.ts` (extends `BaseI18n` from `@i18n-micro/core`): one per app. It holds the chunk map (`storage.translations`, FIFO-evicted with `cacheMaxSize`), the active dictionary, and the outgoing dictionary.
- **Navigation** does not merge. `applySwitchContext` installs the new chunk as the active dictionary; on a same-locale navigation the old one stays as a fallback layer so the leaving page still renders its keys. `finishTransition` drops it when the leaving page's element leaves the document, watched from the commit, or on `page:finish` for a page with no element. A parent still in `to.matched` keeps it until the next navigation.
- **Patches merge**: `$mergeTranslations`, `$loadPageTranslations` and `i18n:register` deep-merge into the stored chunk and, when it is active, into the dictionary. Stored trees are never edited in place.
- **`NuxtTranslationLoader`** dedupes in-flight loads per key and keeps a switch generation, so a slow load cannot overwrite a newer navigation. `reload()` (`$clearCache`, dev HMR) clears both caches and re-applies the current chunk without blanking the screen.
- **Dev HMR**: a Vite plugin in `src/module.ts` swallows updates of translation files and sends `i18n-micro:update`; the client plugin from `src/hmr-plugin.ts` calls `$clearCache()`. The dev server reads live files, so nothing on the server needs invalidating.

## Public surface

Everything above is internal and may change in any release. Apps may rely on:

| Need                                 | Use                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Reload translations in the browser   | [`$clearCache()`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods#clearcache)                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| Add or patch translations at runtime | [`$mergeTranslations`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods#mergetranslations), [`$loadPageTranslations`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods#loadpagetranslations), [`i18n:register`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/events) |
| Bound or expire the caches           | [`cacheMaxSize`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#cachemaxsize), [`cacheTtl`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#cachettl)                                                                                             |
| HTTP caching of payloads             | [`httpCacheDuration`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#httpcacheduration), [`dateBuild`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#datebuild)                                                                                 |
| Where payloads are written           | [`translationPayloads`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#translationpayloads), [Deployment](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment)                                                                                          |
| Translations in a Nitro handler      | [Server routes](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/server-side-translations)                                                                                                                                                                                 |

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-git-pull-request" title="Contributing" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/"}

# Contributing

This page takes you from a fresh clone to a pull request. Read it before your first change: the build order and the package versioning rules are easy to get wrong. The other pages in this section cover the architecture, the test suites, the maintenance commands and the release checks.

## Prerequisites

- **Node.js 22** — CI runs 22; Vitest needs ≥ 22.12.
- **pnpm 9.14.2** — the version in `packageManager`; `corepack enable` picks it up. Do not use npm or yarn in the workspace.

No database, Docker or external service is needed: integration and e2e tests start their own Nuxt servers.

## Setup

Fork the repository, then run these steps **in this order** (the same order as `.github/workflows/ci.yml`):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/<you>/nuxt-i18n-micro.git
cd nuxt-i18n-micro
pnpm install
pnpm --filter "./packages/**" --filter "!./packages/*/playground" run build
pnpm run dev:prepare
pnpm --filter "./packages/*/playground" run build
```

- `dev:prepare` loads `src/module.ts`, which imports `@i18n-micro/*` from their `dist/`, so the packages must be built first. It also writes `.nuxt/tsconfig.json`, which the root `tsconfig.json` extends.
- The package playground build generates the `virtual:i18n-micro/config` declaration that the Astro playground needs. Skip it and `pnpm run test:unit` / `pnpm run typecheck` fail with `Cannot find module 'virtual:i18n-micro/config'`.

Then start the playground at `http://localhost:3000` (`/` redirects to `/en`):

```bash
pnpm run dev
```

Warnings about `localeCookie` and large translation payloads at startup are expected.

## Where to change what

| Goal                                                    | Location                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Module options, build hooks                             | `src/module.ts`                                                          |
| Nuxt runtime (plugins, composables, middleware, server) | `src/runtime/`                                                           |
| Shared types                                            | `packages/types/src/`                                                    |
| Framework-agnostic helpers                              | `packages/utils/src/` (subpath exports)                                  |
| Translation, plural, formatting                         | `packages/core/src/`                                                     |
| Route generation / runtime paths                        | `packages/route-strategy/` / `packages/path-strategy/`                   |
| Framework bindings                                      | `packages/vue`, `react`, `preact`, `solid`, `astro`, `node`, `vitepress` |
| Docs                                                    | `docs/` — never `docs/news/` unless a maintainer asks                    |
| E2E tests and fixtures                                  | `test/`, `test/fixtures/`                                                |

Work in this order: types, utils, core, then the Nuxt runtime or framework package, then docs and tests. Reuse `@i18n-micro/utils` and core instead of copying logic into a framework package. [Architecture](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/architecture) explains how the pieces fit.

## Checks

| Command                               | What it does                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `pnpm run lint` / `pnpm run lint:fix` | Oxlint                                                                         |
| `pnpm run format`                     | Oxfmt                                                                          |
| `pnpm run typecheck`                  | Root, playground, scripts, packages, package playgrounds                       |
| `pnpm run test:unit`                  | Fast unit tests, no builds                                                     |
| `pnpm run test`                       | Everything: unit, integration, packages, e2e                                   |
| `pnpm run test:e2e`                   | Browser journeys (`pnpm exec playwright install chromium` once first)          |
| `pnpm run docs:generate`              | Regenerate the generated docs regions after changing JSDoc, options or exports |
| `pnpm run docs:dev`                   | Docs site with hot reload                                                      |

Run at least `lint`, `typecheck` and `test:unit` before you push; run the full `pnpm run test` when you touch runtime or routing. Test layout and how to add a test: [Testing the module](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/testing). Every maintenance command: [Maintenance commands](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/maintenance-commands).

## Changing a package

Packages under `packages/*` are versioned by hand; the release scripts bump only the root. `pnpm publish -r` silently skips a version that is already on npm, so a missing bump leaves the package stale.

1. Bump every changed package once per pull request (not per commit): `pnpm run bump --level patch --packages <names>`. Use a patch unless a maintainer decides on minor or major.
2. Rebuild it so `dist/` matches the source: `pnpm --filter @i18n-micro/<name> build`.
3. Commit source and version together. `dist/` is gitignored; `prepack` rebuilds it for a release.

CI runs `pnpm run check:versions` against the merge base; changes to tests, docs and playgrounds do not count. **Never** edit the root `version` or `CHANGELOG.md` by hand: only the release scripts change them. [Publishing](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/maintenance-commands#publishing) lists the commands.

## Commits and pull requests

- Conventional Commits: `feat(scope): …`, `fix(scope): …`, `docs(scope): …`, `test(scope): …`.
- Follow-ups are new commits; do not amend or force-push a branch under review.
- Target `main` of `s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro`, fill in the pull request template, link the issue.
- Update docs when you change a public API or an exports map; add or adjust tests next to the change.
- Bugs and feature requests go through the [issue templates](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/issues/new/choose){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}; include a reproduction.

# Maintenance commands

These commands check the repository itself, not apps that use the module. Run them when you change exports, docs, dependencies or fixtures, and before a release. Each catches a drift that builds and tests do not notice.

All of them live in the `scripts/` workspace package and run through one CLI; `--help` prints every flag:

```bash
pnpm -C scripts cli <command> --help
```

## Commands

| Command                                                                    | Root script                                  | Catches                                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`docs-generate`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#docs-generate)   | `docs:generate`, `docs:generate:check`       | Generated docs regions out of date with the code                                                                             |
| [`api-surface`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#api-surface)       | `api:surface`, `api:surface:update`          | An export removed or retyped                                                                                                 |
| [`docs-audit`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#docs-audit)         | `audit:docs`                                 | Undocumented options, dead nav/sidebar entries and links                                                                     |
| [`deps-audit`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#deps-audit)         | `audit:deps`                                 | Versions outside the catalog, imports never declared                                                                         |
| [`fixtures-audit`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#fixtures-audit) | `audit:fixtures`                             | Unreferenced fixtures, committed build output                                                                                |
| [`payload-budget`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#payload-budget) | `budget:payload`, `budget:payload:update`    | `__NUXT_DATA__` or client assets growing                                                                                     |
| `check-versions`                                                           | `check:versions`                             | A changed package without a version bump (`--npm`: version already published)                                                |
| `verify-packages`                                                          | `verify:packages`, `verify:packages:publint` | Broken `exports` / `files` in a package                                                                                      |
| `compare-published`                                                        | `compare:published`                          | The packed packages against the versions on npm                                                                              |
| `consumer-types`                                                           | `check:consumer`                             | Published `.d.ts` that break a user: Are The Types Wrong, then `tsc` with `skipLibCheck: false` under `bundler` and `node16` |
| `oldest-versions`                                                          | `check:oldest`                               | A peer range that fails at its floor: Nuxt 3.18, VitePress 1.0, Vue 3.3, vue-router 4.5.1                                    |
| `http-fuzz`                                                                | `test:fuzz`                                  | Off-origin redirects, header injection, reflected HTML, traversal, crashes under hostile HTTP. For release checks, not CI    |
| `ensure-release-source`                                                    | `release:source`                             | Root `version` or `CHANGELOG.md` changed outside `cli release`                                                               |
| [`preflight`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#preflight)           | `preflight`                                  | All release gates in one run                                                                                                 |

`release` and `bump` are covered in [Publishing](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#publishing). `performance`, `preset-smoke` and the `smoke-*` commands are covered in [Release smoke checks](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/release-smoke) and [Benchmark methodology](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/performance-methodology).

## docs-generate

Writes the generated parts of the docs from the code. `docs:dev` and `docs:build` run it first; CI and `preflight` run `--check`, which fails when a page would change.

| Output                                                                                                         | Read from                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Module options](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options) tables and `option:<path>` regions | `ModuleOptions` in `packages/types/src/index.ts` (TypeScript AST)                            |
| [Helpers](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods) index and `method:<name>` regions                | `PluginsInjections`, `NuxtAppOnlyInjections` in `src/runtime/plugins/01.plugin.ts` (TypeDoc) |
| Composable signatures (`symbol:<name>`)                                                                        | `src/runtime/composables/*.ts` (TypeDoc)                                                     |
| Component props, slots, events (`component:<tag>`)                                                             | `src/runtime/components/*.vue` (vue-docgen-api)                                              |
| [Package APIs](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages) index and `docs/api/packages/*.md`         | `scripts/api-surface/*.api.txt`                                                              |
| Payload budget table in [Performance](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance)                | `scripts/payload-budget.json`                                                                |

A region is marked in a hand-written page and replaced on every run:

```md
<!-- generated:method:$t — do not edit; run `pnpm run docs:generate` -->
<!-- /generated:method:$t -->
```

A fixed page that lacks its region makes the command exit with an error; an optional region (an `option:*` or `method:*` block) is filled only where a page has one. To change generated text, edit the JSDoc (or `@slot` comment) in the source and rerun. Tests require a comment on every prop, slot, helper and composable.

## api-surface

Compares the exported API of every package with the committed snapshots in `scripts/api-surface/*.api.txt`: one line per export and per class member. It reads `src` through the TypeScript program, so no build is needed. Removals and signature changes fail; additions are reported.

```bash
pnpm run api:surface
pnpm run api:surface:update   # accept the current surface
pnpm -C scripts cli api-surface --package core
```

After an accepted change run `api:surface:update`, then `docs:generate`, in that order: the package pages read the snapshots.

## docs-audit

Fails on an option of `ModuleOptions` that appears nowhere in `docs/`, a nav or sidebar entry pointing at a missing page, and a link to a missing page. Warns on a page no nav or sidebar reaches. Dynamic routes (`[param].md`) and `cleanUrls` are resolved the way VitePress does.

```bash
pnpm run audit:docs
pnpm -C scripts cli docs-audit --warnings-as-errors
```

## deps-audit

Fails when a dependency is pinned outside the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog or a package imports something it does not declare (`undeclared-import`). Warns on imports satisfied only by a devDependency, `import type` of an undeclared package, unused catalog entries, and peers without a matching devDependency. Comments and template literals are ignored when scanning.

```bash
pnpm run audit:deps
pnpm -C scripts cli deps-audit --warnings-as-errors
```

## fixtures-audit

Lists fixtures under `test/fixtures/` that nothing in `test/`, `.github/`, `package.json` or the Vitest configs references, and build output (`.nuxt`, `.output`, `.output-shared`, `.nuxt-test`, `test-results`) inside a fixture. It never deletes. `--strict` fails only on **committed** build output. `pnpm run clean:test` removes local build output except `.output`.

```bash
pnpm run audit:fixtures
pnpm -C scripts cli fixtures-audit --strict
```

## payload-budget

Builds an app (default: the playground), serves it, and measures `__NUXT_DATA__` per route and the client assets against `scripts/payload-budget.json`. The playground's dictionary is deliberately huge, so the numbers are a fixed point for comparison, not what a real app ships.

```bash
pnpm run budget:payload
pnpm -C scripts cli payload-budget --skip-build   # reuse .output
pnpm run budget:payload:update                    # record with --tolerance headroom (default 10 %)
```

## preflight

Runs the preflight gates, publishes nothing, and reports all results at once (the `release:*` scripts stop at the first failure). `release:check` also runs prepack, format, lint, typecheck, compare-published and tests, so preflight alone is not a full release check. Gates in order: `deps-audit`, `verify-packages --publint`, `api-surface`, `docs-audit`, `docs-generate --check`, `fixtures-audit --strict`, `check-versions`, `ensure-release-source`, `ensure-npm-auth` (with `--npm`), `payload-budget` (with `--budget`).

```bash
pnpm run preflight
pnpm -C scripts cli preflight --npm       # registry checks and npm auth too
pnpm -C scripts cli preflight --offline   # skip network gates
pnpm -C scripts cli preflight --budget    # also build and check the payload budget
```

Before pushing a change set, maintainers run: `prepack`, `format`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `check:versions -- --npm`, `release:source`, `compare:published`, plus `test` when runtime or routing changed. `release:check` chains most of these. `ensure-release-source` is part of `release:check`, `preflight` and every release command.

## Publishing

You pick every version level, and you start every publish. No command reads a level from commit messages, and no CI workflow publishes to npm.

| What        | Patch                                            | Minor                                            | Major                                            |
| ----------- | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| Root module | `pnpm run release:patch`                         | `pnpm run release:minor`                         | `pnpm run release:major`                         |
| Packages    | `pnpm run bump --level patch --packages <names>` | `pnpm run bump --level minor --packages <names>` | `pnpm run bump --level major --packages <names>` |

Tests run by default. When CI already passed, add `--ci-passed` to any release command: see [Skip the local tests](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#skip-the-local-tests).

### Root module

`release:patch`, `release:minor` and `release:major` run `pnpm -C scripts cli publish --bump <level>`, which does, in order:

1. `release:auth`: fails when you are not logged in to npm.
2. `prepack`: builds the packages, the module and the client.
3. `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck`, `check:versions -- --npm`, `release:source`, `compare:published`.
4. `test`.
5. `pnpm -C scripts cli release --bump <level>`: changelogen writes the root `version` and `CHANGELOG.md`, commits `chore(release): vX.Y.Z` and tags it. `--bump` is required.
6. `pnpm publish -r`, then `git push --follow-tags`.

`pnpm publish -r` also ships every package whose version is not on npm yet, so bump and commit the packages first.

### Packages

`bump` edits only `version` in the named `packages/*/package.json`. It does not commit, tag or publish. `--packages` takes short or scoped names separated by commas, or `all`.

```bash
pnpm run bump --level minor --packages core,vue
pnpm run check:versions                          # names the dependents that still need a bump
pnpm run bump --level patch --packages runtime,react
git commit -am "chore(packages): bump versions"
pnpm run release:packages                        # the steps above, without the root bump
```

`release:packages` leaves the root alone: its version is already on npm, so `pnpm publish -r` skips it, and no tag is created. To see what would ship without publishing, run `pnpm publish -r --dry-run`.

`check:versions` fails on a changed package that was not bumped, and on a dependent of a bumped package; it never picks the level.

### Skip the local tests

`--ci-passed` works on every release command and on `release:check`. It skips step 4 and nothing else: the build, `dist`, version and packaging checks still run.

```bash
pnpm run release:minor --ci-passed      # root
pnpm run release:packages --ci-passed   # packages only
```

The flag asks `gh run list --commit` about `ci.yml` on `HEAD` and prints why it skipped the tests. It refuses when a run failed or is still running, when no run passed, and when the working tree has uncommitted changes. If `gh` is missing, not logged in or cannot reach GitHub, it says so and stops; add `--force` to confirm by hand that CI passed:

```bash
pnpm run release:minor --ci-passed --force
```

`--force` does not override a failed run. In that case run the release without `--ci-passed`, which runs the tests here.

To publish without the tests and without asking CI, for example when the change since the last green run cannot affect them, use `--skip-tests`. It is your call: nothing checks it. The build, `dist`, version and packaging checks still run.

```bash
pnpm run release:major --skip-tests
```

### CI

| Workflow              | Starts on                                                               | Publishes                                                       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `ci.yml`              | Push to `main`, pull requests                                           | Nothing                                                         |
| `release-smoke.yml`   | Manual; `presets: true` builds every preset on the checkout             | Nothing to npm. The manual `deploy` input deploys the smoke app |
| `docs.yml`            | Push to `main` that changes `docs/`, a published GitHub release, manual | The docs site only                                              |
| `oldest-versions.yml` | Manual                                                                  | Nothing                                                         |
| `mutation.yml`        | Manual                                                                  | Nothing. A report to read, not a gate                           |

# Benchmark methodology

`pnpm test:performance` builds the same generated app without i18n, with `@nuxtjs/i18n` and with this module, then load-tests each build. Run it when a change may affect build time, memory or throughput. Results for the current release are on [Benchmarks](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance-results); this page explains what they measure and how to reproduce them.

## What is measured

| Layer    | Artifact                                                                                 |
| -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| App      | Generated fixture, `nuxi build`, Nitro `node-server` output (`.output/server/index.mjs`) |
| Module   | Root `dist/module.mjs` from `nuxt-module-build build`; the suite fails on a jiti stub    |
| Packages | `@i18n-micro/*/dist`, built before the suite                                             |
| Load     | Artillery through `@untestutils/perf`                                                    |

Vite SPA output, `nuxi preview` and dev servers are not measured. The defaults are 4 locales, a 10,000-key target (`--keys 10000`, which the fixture rounds up to a tree of 16,807 leaf keys per locale: branch 7, depth 5) and 3 consecutive runs (means reported), with paths for `prefix_except_default`.

## Load profiles

| `--load`          | Window                                          | Use               |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------- |
| `short` (default) | Warm 2 s at 10/s, main 10 s at 40/s, max 40 VUs | Day to day and CI |
| `mid`             | Warm 6 s at 6/s, main 30 s at 60/s, uncapped    | Between the two   |
| `full`            | Warm 6 s at 6/s, main 60 s at 60/s, uncapped    | Published numbers |

Absolute RPS scales with the window and the machine. In an A/B of all three profiles the ranking of the three apps never changed, so `short` is the default and `full` is kept for the published page.

## Cool-downs

| `--cool`         | After build | Between runs | Between targets |
| ---------------- | ----------- | ------------ | --------------- |
| `fast` (default) | 200 ms      | 500 ms       | 500 ms          |
| `strict`         | 2 s         | 3 s          | 5 s             |

`fast` preserves the ranking; `strict` reproduces the older pauses.

## Commands

```bash
# day to day: --load short --cool fast --runs 3
pnpm test:performance

# one target, or build times only
pnpm -C scripts cli performance --only micro
pnpm -C scripts cli performance --skip-load

# regenerate docs/guide/performance-results.md
pnpm -C scripts cli performance --load full --cool fast --runs 3 --only all
```

`--only` takes `plain`, `i18n`, `micro` or `all`. The results page is written only with `--load full --only all`.

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Benchmarks" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance-results"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Performance" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance"}

# Release smoke checks

The test suites run against the source; these checks install the module the way a user does and test the running app. Run them before a release (packed from the checkout) and after one (from npm), and whenever you touch payload output for serverless or Edge presets. The app is [`test/deploy-smoke`](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/tree/main/test/deploy-smoke){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## Sources

| Source | Installs                                    | Catches                                                                                                            |
| ------ | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `git`  | Tarballs packed from the checkout           | Packaging problems before publishing: missing files, unresolved `workspace:` / `catalog:`, undeclared dependencies |
| `npm`  | `nuxt-i18n-micro@latest` or a named version | A bad or missing publish, version mismatch between the module and `@i18n-micro/*`                                  |

`smoke-pack` packs every workspace package with `pnpm pack` (only pnpm rewrites `workspace:` and `catalog:`) and points each tarball's `@i18n-micro/*` dependencies at its siblings, because the local versions are not on npm yet.

## What is checked

`smoke-verify --url <base>` (HTTP, so it runs against a local server or a deployment):

- `/`, `/de`, `/fr`, `/de/about` render their own translations; plurals resolve; no raw keys in the HTML;
- `/_locales/index/de/data.json` returns the chunk and is cacheable (not `no-store`);
- `hreflang` alternates with `x-default`, `canonical`, `og:locale`, and `<html lang>` matching the locale.

`smoke-browser --url <base>` (Playwright) adds hydration, client navigation between pages and locales with no raw key visible mid-transition, and no uncaught page errors.

## Run locally

```bash
pnpm run prepack
pnpm -C scripts cli smoke-pack --app test/deploy-smoke
cd test/deploy-smoke
printf 'packages:\n  - .\n' > pnpm-workspace.yaml
pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
pnpm exec nuxt build
PORT=3000 node .output/server/index.mjs &
cd ../..
pnpm -C scripts cli smoke-verify --url http://127.0.0.1:3000
pnpm -C scripts cli smoke-browser --url http://127.0.0.1:3000
```

For a published version, skip `smoke-pack` and set the dependency to `nuxt-i18n-micro@<version>` before installing.

## Serverless presets locally

The unit tests and the `node-server` fixtures do not catch SSR that cannot read `public/` on a function or Edge preset. `preset-smoke` packs, installs, builds `test/deploy-smoke` with a real preset, runs it with the runner that matches the artifact, and calls `smoke-verify`:

```bash
pnpm run prepack                       # once
pnpm run test:presets                  # vercel, cloudflare_pages, netlify
pnpm -C scripts cli preset-smoke --preset vercel                         # one preset
pnpm -C scripts cli preset-smoke --preset vercel --public-assets false   # SSR from serverAssets only
pnpm -C scripts cli preset-smoke --preset vercel --skip-pack --skip-install   # faster reruns
```

`--browser` also runs `smoke-browser`; `--skip-build` reuses the preset output.

| Preset             | Runner                                                                                                                                                |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `vercel`           | Imports `.vercel/output/functions/__fallback.func/index.mjs` as a Node listener (as Nitro's own preset tests do; nitropack 2 has no `preview` for it) |
| `cloudflare_pages` | `wrangler pages dev dist`                                                                                                                             |
| `netlify`          | Imports `.netlify/functions-internal/server/main.mjs` behind a local HTTP server                                                                      |

`vercel dev`, emulators and swapping to a Node adapter are not used: they run a different artifact.

## CI workflow

`.github/workflows/release-smoke.yml` runs **manually** (Actions → *release smoke* → *Run workflow*), after a publish has reached npm. Inputs: `source` (`both`, `git`, `npm`), `version` (default `latest`), `deploy`.

With `deploy` it deploys the **published** package to Cloudflare Pages and Vercel, waits for the deployment, and runs `smoke-verify` and `smoke-browser` against the live URL. Use dedicated projects: every run replaces the deployment.

| Name                                 | Kind     | Where to get it                                                                                        |
| ------------------------------------ | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `CLOUDFLARE_PROJECT_NAME`            | variable | A direct-upload Pages project (*Workers & Pages* → *Create* → *Pages* → *Upload assets*)               |
| `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`              | secret   | The ID in the dashboard URL, or *Account details*                                                      |
| `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`               | secret   | Custom token with one permission: Account · Cloudflare Pages · Edit; no IP filter                      |
| `VERCEL_ORG_ID`, `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` | secret   | `pnpm dlx vercel link` in `test/deploy-smoke` writes them to `.vercel/project.json` (do not commit it) |
| `VERCEL_TOKEN`                       | secret   | A token scoped to the account or team that owns the project                                            |

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-git-pull-request" title="Maintenance commands" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/maintenance-commands"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Deployment" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment"}
