# Testing the module

The repository's tests split into fast unit tests, build-heavy integration suites and browser journeys, all against a few shared Nuxt fixtures. Read this before you add a test or a fixture. You learn which command to run, where a new check belongs, and how builds stay safe to run in parallel.

To test your own app, see [Testing your app](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/testing).

## Commands

```bash
pnpm run test:unit         # no builds, no browser
pnpm run test:integration  # suites that build or generate a fixture
pnpm run test:strategies   # static generate of every strategy
pnpm run test:e2e          # browser journeys
pnpm run test:packages     # one project per packages/*
pnpm run test              # all of the above
```

Run `pnpm exec playwright install chromium` once before e2e.

| Project       | Contents                                                                  | Config                         |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `unit`        | pure unit tests, no Nuxt build                                            | `vitest.unit.config.ts`        |
| `integration` | suites that run `nuxi build` / `generate` or `@nuxt/test-utils` `setup()` | `vitest.integration.config.ts` |
| `e2e`         | journeys in `test/journeys/*.spec.ts` against real servers                | `vitest.e2e.config.ts`         |
| packages      | one per `packages/*`                                                      | `packages/*/vitest.config.ts`  |

`INTEGRATION_TESTS` in `test/setup/heavy-tests.ts` is the one list of heavy suites: the integration config includes it and the unit config excludes it.

## Fixtures

All fixtures are apps under `test/fixtures/`:

| Fixture               | Covers                                                                                      |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `basic`               | the public API; `basic/layer` is the only nested app, because `extends` needs a second root |
| `strategy`            | the four strategies, detection and global URL shapes                                        |
| `seo`                 | head tags                                                                                   |
| `integrations`        | `@nuxt/content` and `@nuxtjs/seo`                                                           |
| `translation-watcher` | dev HMR                                                                                     |

The benchmark apps are not fixtures: they live in `scripts/perf-fixtures`.

A new check goes into an existing fixture as a page. A build creates an empty `locales/pages/<page>/<locale>.json` for every page without one; commit those files. A file that appears mid-run changes the fixture hash, and the forks then reject the recipe (`bound to conflicting identities`).

## Variants are recipes

`test/recipes.ts` names one build per variant of a fixture. A variant is one recipe line, never a copied directory:

```ts
'strategy-prefix': app('strategy-prefix', 'strategy', { STRATEGY: 'prefix', LOCALE_COOKIE: 'user-locale' }),
'basic-n3': app('basic-n3', 'basic', { BASIC_VARIANT: 'n3' }),
'strategy-baseurl': app('strategy-baseurl', 'strategy', { STRATEGY: 'prefix' }, { app: { baseURL: '/examples' } }),
```

- The third argument is env, read by the fixture's `nuxt.config.ts` (`BASIC_VARIANT`, `SEO_VARIANT`, `STRATEGY`, `TRANSLATION_PAYLOADS`).
- The fourth is a `nuxtConfig` override, for a global URL shape. It is a defu merge, so arrays concatenate: never pass `locales` that way, switch them by env.
- A suite that builds a fixture itself (`setup()`, `nuxi build` / `generate`) sets the same env as the recipe.

Builds are hashed by fixture directory and `src/`, cached in `test/.untestutils/builds` (CI caches that directory) and started once per run.

## Parallel builds

- **Own build dir per suite.** `isolatedBuild(fixture, name)` points `NUXT_TEST_BUILD_DIR` at `test/.fixture-builds/<fixture>/<name>/`, outside the fixture: a build written into it would change the recipe hash mid-run.
- **OS-assigned ports.** Take ports from `getFreePort()` (`test/helpers/port.ts`) and stop servers with `stopChild()` (`test/helpers/subprocess.ts`), which kills the whole process group. Never free a port by killing whatever owns it: with parallel workers that can kill a sibling suite's server.
- **No writes inside the repo tree.** Specs that edit locale files or start a server from the build output run on a temp copy from `tmpFixture()` in `test/helpers/tmp-fixture.ts`.

Each strategy has one file, `test/strategies-<strategy>.test.ts`, so Vitest runs all four at once. They share `test/helpers/strategy-suite.ts`: `nuxi generate` into an isolated build, then the output is read from disk. It is one chain (a single `test`), so a strategy costs one build. The server side of the same routes is checked by `test/journeys/strategies-*.spec.ts` on the recipe's server build.

## Journeys

Browser e2e runs through [untestutils](https://github.com/s00d/untestutils){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} and a real Playwright browser.

- One spec walks one real flow on one recipe: visit, browse, switch locale, reload, detection, head. Each step has a `// step n: action → assert` comment.
- One harness per file: `test.override({ harness: '<recipe>' })` at the top of the `describe`. A second harness in the same file would reach the first one's server, so split it into its own file.
- No `waitForTimeout`, no `networkidle`, no optional `if` assertions. Statuses come from `request.get(path)`, with `{ maxRedirects: 0 }` where the redirect itself is checked. Arm console collectors before the first `goto`.
- Specs import `test` from `test/helpers/guarded-test.ts`. It fails a test on any document response >= 500, uncaught page error, console error or hydration warning, even when the assertions pass. A test that expects one calls `guard.allow(/pattern/)`; `test.override({ guardAllow: [/pattern/] })` allows a pattern for a whole `describe`.
- Retries cover infrastructure only (`retryInfra`, CI): a failing assertion fails.

## Routing goldens

`test/routing-characterization` runs every app in `scenarios.ts` under every strategy and records what each URL reads as and where each navigation lands. The harness calls the code the module calls (`mergeDefineI18nRouteMeta`, `extractDefineI18nRouteData`, `RouteGenerator`), so do not copy module logic into it: a copy cannot fail.

- Pages are not only what the file scanner makes: `modulePages` are pushed as in `pages:extend`, with or without a name, and `noPages` runs Nuxt's stub router with no records (`pages: false`).
- Input is frozen, so a package that writes to pages or routes throws in the golden. Every page is tagged with its file, and a record that loses `meta` is listed under the invariant breaks.
- A golden diff is either an intended fix or a bug. Read all of it before you regenerate.

## Mutation testing

`pnpm run test:mutation` runs [Stryker](https://stryker-mutator.io/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} on one package. It changes the source (`<` to `<=`, a branch removed, a string emptied) and reruns the tests that cover the change; a surviving mutant is a behaviour no test pins.

```bash
MUTATE_PACKAGE=core pnpm run test:mutation                      # score; JSON report in test-results/mutation/
MUTATE_PACKAGE=core MUTATE_ALL_KILLERS=1 pnpm run test:mutation # record every test that kills each mutant
```

With `MUTATE_ALL_KILLERS=1` the report lists every killing test per mutant, so a test whose mutants are all killed by others can be deleted. Package tests are kept to a small set that still kills every mutant any test kills. New tests are scenarios (set up like a real app, act, assert, act again), not one-line checks.

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-git-pull-request" title="Contributing" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-git-pull-request" title="Maintenance commands" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/maintenance-commands"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Testing your app" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/testing"}
::


# CLI

`@i18n-micro/cli` manages the locale files of a Nuxt project. It reads `locales`, `defaultLocale`, `translationDir` and your layers from `nuxt.config`, so it needs no configuration of its own.

![A terminal running i18n-micro check, which lists a missing, an undefined and four unused keys and fails, then extract, which adds the undefined key, then clean --dryRun, which lists the four keys it would remove](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/cli/demo.gif){height="640" width="1200"}

| Command     | Use it to                                            |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `check`     | Fail a build on anything wrong with the locale files |
| `translate` | Fill missing keys through a translation service      |
| `clean`     | Remove keys nothing uses                             |
| `rename`    | Move a key, or a whole namespace, everywhere at once |

```bash
npm install -D @i18n-micro/cli
npx i18n-micro --help
```

Run it from the app root, or point at it with `--cwd`. Every flag of every command is on the [command reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/cli).

::tip
**Moving from nuxt-i18n-micro-cli?** `@i18n-micro/cli` replaces it; the bins `i18n-micro` and `i18n-micro-cli` stay. See the [table of old commands](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#moving-from-nuxt-i18n-micro-cli).
::

## Use it in CI

```bash
i18n-micro check
```

`check` is the gate. It reports:

| Check          | Means                                                                   |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `missing`      | A key of the default locale is absent from a locale                     |
| `empty`        | A value is `''`. The app shows a blank, not the fallback                |
| `extra`        | A locale has a key the default locale does not                          |
| `placeholders` | `{name}` was lost or added, or a plural lost its forms                  |
| `undefined`    | The code uses a key the default locale does not have                    |
| `unused`       | Nothing in the project uses a key                                       |
| `duplicates`   | The same text under different keys. Off by default: pass `--duplicates` |

- `--only missing,placeholders` runs some checks; a check named in `--only` that could not run fails.
- `--json` gives a report for tooling.
- `--ignore` skips source files.
- While keys are computed at runtime, `unused` is skipped and the report says why.

Every command exits with one of three codes, so a pipeline can tell a problem with your translations from a problem with the tool:

| Exit code | Meaning                                                                   |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `0`       | Nothing to report                                                         |
| `1`       | Findings                                                                  |
| `2`       | The command could not run: a usage error, a broken file, a failed request |

Other commands worth a CI step:

```bash
i18n-micro format --check      # fails if a file is not formatted
i18n-micro lint                # stray spaces, empty values, your own regex rules
i18n-micro stats --baseRef main
```

## Keep locales in step

| Command   | What it does                                                                                                                      |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `extract` | Lists the keys the code uses that have no text yet. A default text, as in `$t('key', {}, 'Welcome')`, goes to the default locale. |
| `sync`    | Removes keys the default locale does not have. Try `--dryRun` first.                                                              |
| `clean`   | Removes keys nothing uses. Try `--dryRun` first.                                                                                  |
| `search`  | Finds keys and values, and shows where each key is used.                                                                          |
| `stats`   | Completion per locale; `--baseRef main` compares with a git ref.                                                                  |

`sync` stops like `clean` does when it would remove a key it cannot prove unused, and also when the default locale has nothing to compare with. With nothing to remove it never stops, so `$t(item.label)` alone is no reason for `--force`.

::note
`extract` and `sync` never write `''` for a key without a translation. The key stays absent, so `fallbackLocale` applies at runtime and `check` reports it. An empty string would be a defined value and show a blank.
::

### What the commands read

`check`, `extract`, `sync`, `clean`, `search` and `rename` read source code across the whole project, not a fixed list of folders:

- **Read:** templates and scripts through a parser, `.html` and Pug as text, every layer, and folders outside the root that an alias or `components` points at.
- **Skipped:** `node_modules`, build output and the locale files. Add your own with `--ignore 'legacy/**,*.stories.ts'`.
- **Test code** counts as usage, so `clean` and `check --only unused` keep a key only a test reads. It never adds a key: `extract` skips such keys, and `check` does not report them as undefined.

Test code means the root folders `tests`, `test`, `__tests__`, `e2e`, `cypress` and `playwright`, plus `.spec` and `.test` JavaScript and TypeScript files (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs` and the like) anywhere. Only the root folders are exempt from the doubts below: `pages/tests/[id].vue` is a page like any other, and so are `public/` and minified files, whose code is not part of the app.

The commands recognise:

- `$t`, `$ts`, `$tc`, `$has` and `$_t(route)`;
- `t()` from `useI18n()` and `useTranslationServerMiddleware()`;
- `<i18n-t keypath>` in templates and JSX, and `<i18n-group prefix>`;
- aliases such as `const { t: tr } = useI18n()`.

### How `clean` decides

`clean` would rather leave a dead key than remove a live one. A key stays when any of this is true:

- a call uses it, or a key below or above it;
- a string in the code equals it: `const key = 'menu.home'`, `<Item label="menu.home" />`;
- a JSON, YAML or Markdown file in the project contains it;
- a computed key has a static start that covers it: ``$t(`status.${state}`)`` keeps everything under `status.`;
- a layer defines it.

`clean` stops without changing anything when it cannot know, and lists why:

- a key is fully computed, as in `$t(name)`, `<i18n-t :keypath="name" />` or `<i18n-t v-bind="props" />`;
- `$t` is passed around as a value, as in `items.map($t)`;
- a function called `t` gets a computed argument and comes from a parameter, an import or a call: it may be a wrapper around the real one. A function the same file defines does not count, because a wrapper would have its own call inside;
- a source file does not parse;
- no file uses any key at all, which usually means it is looking in the wrong place;
- a locale file is a symlink out of the project, so another app may read it.

::steps{level="4"}
#### Preview

Run `i18n-micro clean --dryRun` and review what it lists.

#### Protect keys

Keep keys that only look unused with `--exclude '^errors\.'`.

#### Remove

Run it again with `--force`.
::

## Translate missing keys

```bash
i18n-micro translate --dryRun                     # keys and characters per locale, nothing sent
export I18N_TRANSLATE_TOKEN=...                   # or put it in .env
i18n-micro translate --service deepl --locale de,fr
```

- `translate` fills keys that are missing or empty; `--replace` translates everything again.
- Placeholders and plural forms are protected. A translation that lost a placeholder is not written: the key is listed and the command exits `1`.
- Every batch is saved before the next request goes out, so a failure costs only the request that failed.

| `--service`      | Service                                                              | `--token`                                                               | Useful `--options`                          |
| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `ai`             | Vercel AI Gateway, OpenAI, Anthropic or any OpenAI-compatible server | API key, or `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` | `provider`, `model`, `baseUrl`, `maxTokens` |
| `azure`          | Azure Translator                                                     | Subscription key                                                        | `region`                                    |
| `deepl`          | DeepL, Free keys included                                            | Auth key                                                                | `formality`, `glossaryId`, `context`        |
| `google`         | Google Cloud Translation v2                                          | API key                                                                 | `model`                                     |
| `libretranslate` | LibreTranslate                                                       | Optional                                                                | `baseUrl`                                   |
| `yandexcloud`    | Yandex Cloud Translate                                               | API key, or IAM token with `authScheme:Bearer`                          | `folderId`, `model`                         |

Options are `key:value` pairs: `--options provider:openai,model:gpt-4o-mini`. All services also take `baseUrl`, `retries`, `retryDelayMs` and `timeoutMs`. A translation request may already be billed, so it is repeated only after a `429` or `503`, and not when the service asks to wait more than a minute.

::warning
Flags are visible in shell history and process lists, so pass the token through the environment variable. The CLI masks what it knows to be secret wherever it prints it, `--debug` included: tokens, provider keys, Basic credentials, and the query and credentials of a URL you configured. A server that reformats a key before echoing it is out of its reach, so treat logs of a failed run with care.
::

The `ai` service follows a glossary. When `.i18n-glossary.json` exists it is used without a flag; `--glossaryFile` picks another file.

```json [.i18n-glossary.json]
{ "entries": [{ "source": "Cart", "target": "Warenkorb", "to": "de" }] }
```

## Turn hardcoded text into keys

```bash
i18n-micro text-to-i18n --dryRun   # list what would change
i18n-micro text-to-i18n            # rewrite the templates
```

```vue
<!-- before -->
<h1>Welcome to our site</h1>
<!-- after -->
<h1>{{ $t('pages.index.welcome-to-our') }}</h1>
```

Only `.vue` templates of the project itself are rewritten, not those of a layer or an alias target. Every rewritten file is parsed again before it is written. These are listed and keep their text:

- text in `.ts` files and scripts, because `$t` is not in scope everywhere;
- text next to markup or an interpolation, such as `<p>Hello <b>world</b> today</p>`: half a sentence cannot be translated on its own;
- a generated key that would collide with another, as a parent page and its child can;
- a known key that cannot go between quotes.

::warning
Commit first, and review the diff.
::

## Rename a key

```bash
i18n-micro rename --from common.save --to actions.save
i18n-micro rename --from settings --to account.settings   # a whole namespace
```

`rename` edits the syntax tree, so comments and unrelated strings stay as they are, and aliases and `:keypath` are followed. A layer's own file is never changed. It warns about what it cannot rewrite, and leaves it alone:

- a computed key under the old name;
- each plain string equal to it;
- a Pug template;
- a source in a layer or in a folder outside the project.

`--to` has to be a key that can be written in code: no quotes, no backslash, no empty segment, no `__proto__`.

## Exchange files with translators

```bash
i18n-micro export --format csv
i18n-micro import --format csv --dryRun
```

**`export`** writes every key of every locale, untranslated ones included, with the default-locale text as the source: a `Source` column in CSV, a `#.` comment in PO.

- Without `--dir`, PO goes to `pots` and CSV to `csv_exports`.
- It records what it wrote in `.i18n-export.json`, in the output folder. It stops when a file has changed since then and holds translations the locale files do not have, fuzzy PO entries included; `--force` overwrites them. Ordinary edits of the locale files do not stop it.

**`import`** merges, skips empty cells, and skips PO entries marked `fuzzy`.

- A key that would overwrite a value, or a value over a whole group of keys, is listed and left out, and the command exits `1`.
- It stops with exit `2` on a catalog in an unexpected location, a page's catalog the last export did not write, a quote out of place in a CSV, or a page entry under `disablePageLocales`.

For a translation platform, use its own CLI: the [Crowdin](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/crowdin) setup syncs the JSON files, page files included.

## Sync with your own endpoint

`sync-remote` exchanges the global locale files with an HTTP endpoint you run. Page files stay local, and the command says so. Describe the endpoint in `.i18n-remote.json`:

```json [.i18n-remote.json]
{ "url": "https://translations.example.com", "path": "translations" }
```

The endpoint answers `GET` and `PUT` with a `{ locale: messages }` object. Authenticate with `auth: { username, password }`, or put a bearer token in `I18N_REMOTE_TOKEN`.

|            | Pull                                                                                             | Push                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| What moves | Fills what you do not have and keeps keys only you have                                          | Sends the project's own keys, not those of a layer, and leaves your blanks out                                                                                                                          |
| Conflicts  | A key that differs on both sides: nothing is written, exit `1`; `--force` takes the remote value | A PUT replaces the document, so a push first reads the endpoint and stops with exit `1` when it holds text you do not have; `--force` overwrites it. An endpoint that answers `404` has nothing to lose |
| `--dryRun` | Reads from the endpoint, lists the changes, writes nothing                                       | Says what would be sent, without contacting the endpoint                                                                                                                                                |

A locale you have not configured is skipped, and a blank remote value clears nothing.

## Moving from nuxt-i18n-micro-cli

| Old command                                                                                                                 | Now                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `validate`                                                                                                                  | `check`                                                                                    |
| `diff`                                                                                                                      | `check --only missing`                                                                     |
| `check-duplicates`                                                                                                          | `check --only duplicates`                                                                  |
| `export-csv`, `import-csv`                                                                                                  | `export --format csv`, `import --format csv`                                               |
| `--potsDir`, `--csvDir`                                                                                                     | `--dir`                                                                                    |
| `estimate`                                                                                                                  | `translate --dryRun`                                                                       |
| `glossary`                                                                                                                  | Edit `.i18n-glossary.json`; `translate` reads it by itself                                 |
| `backup`, `restore`                                                                                                         | Git, which already keeps your locale files                                                 |
| `init`                                                                                                                      | `nuxi init`, then add `nuxt-i18n-micro` to `modules`                                       |
| `split`                                                                                                                     | Removed: the module does not read split files                                              |
| `optimize`                                                                                                                  | `check --only duplicates`                                                                  |
| `replace-values`                                                                                                            | Your editor or `sed`                                                                       |
| `stats --full`                                                                                                              | `stats`; [DevTools](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/devtools) has the details |
| `search --hardcodedOnly`                                                                                                    | `text-to-i18n --dryRun`                                                                    |
| `search --preferUnused`, `--onlyVue`                                                                                        | Removed                                                                                    |
| `lint` rules `no-html-tags`, `no-special-chars`, `no-mixed-case`, `no-missing-punctuation`, `no-inconsistent-pluralization` | Removed: they flagged normal text. Write a `customRegexRules` entry if you need one        |
| `text-to-i18n --extractOnlyDirs`, `--extractOnlyPatterns`, `--verbose`                                                      | Removed: code is never rewritten                                                           |
| `--logLevel verbose`                                                                                                        | Removed: it did nothing                                                                    |

**Removed services:** `googlefree`, `yandex` (use `yandexcloud`), `ibm`, `lingvatranslate`, `modernmt`, `lilt`, `unbabel`, `reverso`, `baidu`, `papago`, `tencent`, `systran`, `mymemory`.

**Removed `sync-remote` types:** `github`, `gitlab`, `crowdin`, `lokalise`, `tolgee`, `weblate`. Use the platform's own CLI, or `custom`, which needs no `type` any more.

### Changed behaviour

- `extract` and `sync` no longer write `''`. Keys stay absent, and `check` reports them. `extract` writes a key only when the code gives its text.
- `extract` writes page keys to `locales/pages/<route name>/`, where the module reads them, and scans `app/` on Nuxt 4. Move anything from directories such as `pages/_about` and `pages/blog_`, and delete a stray `locales/pages/<locale>.json`.
- `translationDir` from `nuxt.config` is respected; before, every command silently used `locales`.
- Without `defaultLocale`, the default is `en`, as in the module, and `DEFAULT_LOCALE` is honoured. It used to be the first locale.
- `check` and `sync` use the default locale as the reference and check page files. `"a.b"` and `a: { b }` count as one key.
- `clean` keeps a key used anywhere, in any scope, and stops when usage cannot be proven. `--include` and `--exclude` choose what may be removed.
- `sync` stops the same way, and when the default locale has no keys to compare with. `--force` overrides it. It also stops when `DEFAULT_LOCALE` chose another reference than `nuxt.config`.
- Single-dash long flags and stray arguments are errors: `clean -dryRun` no longer runs `clean`.
- A read-only file, or a file that is not UTF-8, cannot be saved: the command stops before it changes anything. Reading such a file is fine. A repeated key, a key called `__proto__` and an integer above 2^53 stop a command, because a save would lose them.
- A flag that needs a value and is followed by another flag is an error; write `--flag=--value` for a value that starts with a dash. A boolean flag takes only `true` or `false`.
- `export` stops rather than overwrite translations that were never imported.
- Exit codes are `0`, `1` and `2`; failures used to be `1`, and `diff` and `check-duplicates` always `0`.
- `lint --fix` no longer leaves `.bak` files.
- A save keeps a file's indentation, line endings, final newline, symlink and hard link, and leaves files it did not change alone.
- A mistyped or removed flag is now an error, not silently ignored.
- Paths such as `--dir` are relative to the project, not to the shell.
- `ai` no longer loads `@ai-sdk/*` packages: use `provider` `gateway`, `openai` or `anthropic`, or `baseUrl` for an OpenAI-compatible server.

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="DevTools" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/devtools"}
::


# Crowdin

[Crowdin](https://crowdin.com/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} is a translation platform: you upload the default locale's files, translators work in Crowdin, and you download the other locales back. The module reads plain JSON files, so the Crowdin CLI only needs a `crowdin.yml` that maps `locales/` and `locales/pages/` correctly. No module setting changes.

## Configure crowdin.yml

```yml
# crowdin.yml
project_id_env: CROWDIN_PROJECT_ID
api_token_env: CROWDIN_PERSONAL_TOKEN
base_path: ./locales
preserve_hierarchy: true

files:
  - source: /en.json
    translation: /%two_letters_code%.json
  - source: /pages/**/en.json
    translation: /pages/**/%two_letters_code%.json
```

- `en` is your default locale; its files are the sources.
- `project_id_env` / `api_token_env` read the ID and token from environment variables, so no secret is committed.
- `preserve_hierarchy: true` keeps `pages/<page>/` folders as they are.
- The translated file name must equal the locale `code` in `nuxt.config.ts`. `%two_letters_code%` fits codes like `de`; for codes like `pt-BR` use `%locale%`, or map Crowdin's codes to yours with `languages_mapping`.

## Upload and download

```bash
npm install -g @crowdin/cli

export CROWDIN_PROJECT_ID=123456
export CROWDIN_PERSONAL_TOKEN=...   # from Crowdin account settings

crowdin upload sources   # push locales/en.json and locales/pages/**/en.json
crowdin download         # write locales/de.json, locales/pages/**/de.json, ...
```

Run both in CI to keep files current. Downloaded files land in your repository like hand-edited ones; the next build or dev reload picks them up.

## Before uploading

Clean the sources first so translators do not work on dead keys: [`i18n-micro clean`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/cli#clean) removes unused keys, [`i18n-micro check`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/cli#check) reports gaps after a download. The CLI has no Crowdin integration of its own: this page is the supported way.

# Custom locale detection

The built-in detection reads the URL, a cookie and `Accept-Language`. When the locale depends on something else — the domain, a geo header set by your CDN, a user profile — set it yourself in a plugin that runs before the i18n plugin. The module then loads that locale's translations and uses it for redirects exactly as if it had detected it. The rules that decide when a chosen locale wins over the URL are on [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection); this page shows how to plug your own source in.

## Set the locale in a server plugin

```ts
// plugins/i18n-locale.server.ts
export default defineNuxtPlugin({
  name: 'i18n-custom-locale',
  enforce: 'pre',
  order: -10, // before the i18n plugin (order -5)
  setup() {
    const { setLocale } = useI18nLocale()
    const host = (useRequestHeaders(['host']).host ?? '').split(':')[0]! // without the port

    if (host.endsWith('.de')) setLocale('de')
    else if (host.endsWith('.fr')) setLocale('fr')
  },
})
```

`setLocale(code)` writes the locale state (`useState('i18n-locale')`) and, when a locale cookie is configured, the cookie. Use it instead of writing `useState` or `useCookie` yourself. Pass only enabled locale codes.

Keep the plugin `.server.ts` when it reads request headers: they do not exist in the browser. A `.client.ts` plugin is the place for browser-only sources such as `localStorage`.

## Turn off the built-in Accept-Language step

Your plugin and `Accept-Language` can disagree. To let only your code (plus the URL and cookie) decide, switch the header off:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    autoDetectLanguage: false,
  },
})
```

[`autoDetectLanguage`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#autodetectlanguage) only controls the header step. The URL and a valid cookie still count.

## What happens next

The effect of `setLocale` depends on the [strategy](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/strategy):

| Strategy                          | Effect of `setLocale('de')` in the plugin                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no_prefix`                       | The page renders in German; the URL does not change.                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `prefix`, `prefix_except_default` | On an unprefixed path where [`autoDetectPath`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#autodetectpath) allows redirects (by default only `/`), the server answers `302` to the German URL. A URL with a locale prefix keeps it. |
| `prefix_and_default`              | No redirect: the unprefixed URL is a valid default-locale page.                                                                                                                                                                                   |

Under the prefix strategies a locale in the URL is the user's choice and your plugin does not override it. `autoDetectPath: '*'` is the exception: the server then moves prefixed URLs by cookie and `Accept-Language` and ignores the state, but `setLocale()` also writes the cookie when one is configured, so from the next request your plugin's choice can redirect a prefixed URL. Keep `'/'` or use `'no_prefix'` when explicit locale URLs must win. Use your plugin to choose where a visitor lands, not to rewrite links they followed.

## Respect a locale the user picked

Once a user switches language, the switch writes the cookie. Skip your own detection when there is already a valid preference:

```ts
// plugins/i18n-locale.server.ts
import { detectLocaleFromAcceptLanguage } from '@i18n-micro/utils/accept-language'

export default defineNuxtPlugin({
  name: 'i18n-custom-locale',
  enforce: 'pre',
  order: -10,
  setup() {
    const { getPreferredLocale, setLocale, validLocales } = useI18nLocale()
    if (getPreferredLocale()) return // valid state or cookie: keep it

    const country = useRequestHeaders(['x-country'])['x-country']
    if (country === 'JP') return setLocale('ja')

    const header = useRequestHeaders(['accept-language'])['accept-language']
    setLocale(detectLocaleFromAcceptLanguage(header, validLocales))
  },
})
```

`getPreferredLocale()` returns the state or cookie only when it is an enabled locale, so a stale cookie does not stop detection. `detectLocaleFromAcceptLanguage` is the q-value-aware matcher the module uses itself (install `@i18n-micro/utils` to import it); `setLocale(null)` does nothing.

## One domain per locale

If each domain should serve its own locales, you do not need a plugin: give each locale a `baseUrl`, set `baseDefault: true` on each domain's default locale, and build once (a static site still runs `nuxi generate` per domain). See [Layers and domains](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/layers#multiple-domains).

# Localized paths

By default every locale serves a page at the same path: `/en/about`, `/de/about`. Localized paths let each locale use its own words, such as `/de/ueber-uns`, while the page file stays the same. You set them in the page with `$defineI18nRoute`, or for many pages at once in `nuxt.config.ts`.

## In the page

```vue
<!-- pages/about.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
const { $defineI18nRoute } = useNuxtApp()

$defineI18nRoute({
  localeRoutes: {
    de: '/ueber-uns',
    fr: '/a-propos',
  },
})
</script>
```

With `prefix_except_default` and `defaultLocale: 'en'` the page answers at `/about`, `/de/ueber-uns` and `/fr/a-propos`. A locale without an entry keeps the default path. Write paths without the locale code: the prefix is added by the [strategy](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/strategy), and a path that starts with the locale code logs a warning. What else the call accepts is on [Page config](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/per-component-translations).

## In nuxt.config

[`globalLocaleRoutes`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#globallocaleroutes) does the same for any page, keyed by its path (or by its route name, when written without a leading slash):

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    globalLocaleRoutes: {
      '/about': { de: '/ueber-uns' },
      '/about/team': { de: '/ueber-uns/team' },
      '/admin': false, // not localized: one /admin route, no locale prefix
    },
  },
})
```

When a page sets `localeRoutes` and `globalLocaleRoutes` has the same key, the config entry wins.

## Dynamic params

Write params in any Nuxt form: `[id]`, `[[page]]`, `[...slug]`, or `:id()`. The param names must match the page file.

```ts
// pages/products/[...slug].vue
$defineI18nRoute({
  localeRoutes: {
    en: '/our-products/[...slug]',
    de: '/unsere-produkte/[...slug]',
  },
})
```

Nested pages take an absolute child path (`/ueber-uns/team`) or a path relative to the parent's localized path (`team`).

## Linking to localized pages

Links resolve to the localized path of the target locale, whether you pass a route name or a plain path:

```vue
<template>
  <i18n-link :to="{ name: 'about' }">About</i18n-link>
  <i18n-link to="/about">About</i18n-link>
  <!-- de: both render /de/ueber-uns -->
  <NuxtLink :to="$localePath('/about', 'de')">Deutsch</NuxtLink>
</template>
```

Route names come from the file path (`pages/about/team.vue` is `about-team`) unless you set one with `definePageMeta({ name })`.

## Per-locale slugs

When the slug itself differs per locale (`/our-products/red-shoe` vs `/de/unsere-produkte/roter-schuh`), tell the language switcher which params to use with `$setI18nRouteParams` once the data is loaded:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const { $setI18nRouteParams } = useNuxtApp()
const route = useRoute()

const { data: product } = await useFetch(`/api/products/${route.params.slug}`)

if (product.value) {
  $setI18nRouteParams({
    en: { slug: product.value.slugEn },
    de: { slug: product.value.slugDe },
  })
}
</script>
```

`$switchLocalePath('de')` and `<i18n-switcher>` then link to `/de/unsere-produkte/roter-schuh`. Keys are locale codes, values are params by name (as in the page file).

A switcher in the layout renders before the page's async setup gets here, so when the render ends the module rewrites the links of `<i18n-switcher>`, in `app.vue` and in the page alike. The server HTML, a visitor without JavaScript and the first client render then agree. Set the params during SSR for this: with `lazy` or `server: false` the links change only after hydration. Nuxt's SSR streaming sends the HTML before the params are known, so under it the links in the first HTML keep the URL's own params.

Only the switcher's own links are rewritten. A hand-written `$switchLocalePath` link must render after the params are set, so put it in the page that sets them, also after an `await`. In a layout it renders first: its server HTML keeps the URL's params, and hydration warns about a mismatch. Use `<i18n-switcher>` there, with its slots and `custom*Style` props for the look.

The params belong to the page that set them:

- They are dropped when a navigation to another path commits, so each page sets its own. A cancelled navigation leaves them in place.
- Take `$setI18nRouteParams` from `useNuxtApp()` or `useI18n()` in `setup`, also when you call it later in a `useAsyncData` handler. Taken there, the function knows its page: if the visitor has left, a late call does nothing.
- With `keepalive`, a page gets the params it set back when the visitor returns. `useI18nHead` does the same.

## Routes added in pages\:extend

Routes you push in the `pages:extend` hook have no page file to read `$defineI18nRoute` from, and several of them often share one wrapper component. A route pushed without a `name` gets the name Nuxt would give its path (`/a/:id()` becomes `a-id`), so language links reach it, unless another route already has that name; then give it an explicit `name`. Keep one list and split it into pages and `globalLocaleRoutes` keyed by route name with `splitLocaleRoutes` from `@i18n-micro/utils/split-locale-routes` (add the package to your dependencies):

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
import { splitLocaleRoutes } from '@i18n-micro/utils/split-locale-routes'

const dynamic = splitLocaleRoutes([
  { name: 'products-tag', path: '/products/:tag', file: '~/pages/_dynamic.vue', paths: { de: '/produkte/:tag' } },
  { name: 'internal', path: '/internal', file: '~/pages/_dynamic.vue', paths: false }, // not localized
])

export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  hooks: {
    'pages:extend'(pages) {
      pages.push(...dynamic.pages)
    },
  },
  i18n: {
    globalLocaleRoutes: dynamic.globalLocaleRoutes,
  },
})
```

Do not put localized paths in `route.meta`: they would ship in the client route table.

# Deployment

The module works with any Nitro preset without extra config: it picks where translation files live from the preset you build for. Defaults are right for most apps; read the section for your platform. This page explains:

- what ends up in `.output/` and which headers the payloads get;
- what to change for static hosting, large catalogs, a sub-path, a proxy or a CDN.

::note
Deployed and checked on real hosts: Cloudflare Workers and Pages, Vercel and Vercel Edge, Netlify and Netlify Edge, Cloud Run and Deno Deploy, each with what [Platforms](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#platforms) lists. The other presets were built and run locally.
::

## How translations are delivered

At build time the module turns `locales/` (all layers merged) into **payloads**: one JSON file per page and locale. Two consumers read them:

- **SSR** loads the payload of the rendered page in-process — no HTTP request, and the dictionary is not embedded in the HTML.
- **The browser** fetches `/_locales/<page>/<locale>/data.json?v=<dateBuild>` on hydration and on navigation.

`_locales` is [`apiBaseUrl`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#apibaseurl). The built-in server route answers that URL; the static copy in `public/` answers it without a server.

## Node server

```bash
npx nuxi build
node .output/server/index.mjs
```

With `node-server` (the default preset), `node-cluster`, `bun`, `deno-server` or any other preset that serves `public/` from disk, with `public/` next to the `server/` folder:

- payloads are copied to `.output/public/_locales/<page>/<locale>/data.json`;
- SSR reads them from that folder with `fs` (nothing is bundled into the server);
- the browser gets them as static files, or from the server route.

Deploy the whole `.output/` directory. The module needs Node 20 or newer, and Nuxt has its own minimum: Nuxt 4.5 declares `^22.19.0 || ^24.11.0 || >=26.0.0`.

A process under steady load can hold much more memory than its live heap. See [Memory on a Node server](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance#memory-on-a-node-server) before you set a container limit.

With another layout, the module embeds the payloads as described in the next section. That covers:

- a custom `nitro.output.publicDir`, which the build reads once;
- `serveStatic: true` on a preset that keeps static files elsewhere.

::warning
If a build reads `public/` and the folder does not reach the server, as with `aws-lambda` and `serveStatic: true`, the server logs one error and pages show raw keys. Set `nitro.serveStatic: false` to embed the payloads.
::

## Serverless and Edge

These presets cannot read `public/` at runtime:

- function presets that ship `public/` to a CDN or do not serve it: `vercel`, `netlify`, `aws-lambda`, `aws-amplify`, `azure-swa`, `firebase`, `stormkit`, `zeabur`, `node-listener`;
- Edge presets without a file system: `cloudflare-module`, `cloudflare-pages`, `vercel-edge`, `netlify-edge`, `deno_deploy`;
- `serveStatic: 'inline'`, such as `winterjs`.

There the module embeds the payloads into the server bundle as Nitro server assets (`assets:i18n`) and still writes the public copy for the browser.

Embedding the full page × locale matrix makes the bundle large. Past the limit of an Edge platform the build warns and names it, see [Bundle limits](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#bundle-limits-on-edge). For big catalogs switch to `source` mode, which embeds the compact source files and merges root, page and fallback translations at runtime:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    translationPayloads: {
      mode: 'source',
    },
  },
})
```

In `source` mode the browser always fetches payloads from the server route, which merges them on request (any public copy holds the compact source tree that only the server reads). That needs a running server, so do not use `source` for a pure static site.

### Bundle limits on Edge

| Platform           | Limit                                                                                  |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Cloudflare Workers | 64 MiB uncompressed, on Free and Paid. No compressed limit. 1 s startup, 128 MB memory |
| Vercel Edge        | 1 MB gzip on Hobby, 2 MB on Pro, 4 MB on Enterprise                                    |
| Netlify Edge       | 20 MB compressed                                                                       |

The build sums the dictionaries it embeds and warns only past the lowest limit of the platform. It counts dictionaries alone, so the app comes on top. For example, 120 pages × 4 locales with a 60 KB root file embed:

| Mode        | Embedded | Fits                                        |
| ----------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `premerged` | 34.9 MiB | Cloudflare; not Vercel Edge or Netlify Edge |
| `source`    | 5.7 MiB  | Still 3 MB gzip on Vercel Edge              |

A catalog that size on Vercel Edge needs a [payload host](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#app-baseurl-and-payload-hosts).

`source` pays a merge per page and locale in each isolate, about 1 ms in that example and 7 ms of CPU in a cold one. It grows with the size of the fallback chain: about 43 ms for 4 MB of chain files. Netlify Edge allows 50 ms of CPU per request and Cloudflare's Free plan 10 ms.

### Dates on Edge runtimes

`$td` uses the runtime's `Intl`, and its ICU data can differ from the browser's. On Netlify Edge a formatted date can contain U+202F (narrow no-break space) where Chrome has a normal space, so Vue logs one hydration mismatch and the text corrects itself on hydration. Plain Nuxt with plain `Intl` does the same there; Deno Deploy does not.

::tip
`<i18n-t>` with `date` or `relativeDate` already allows the mismatch. For `$td` in a template, put `data-allow-mismatch="text"` on the element.
::

## Static site (nuxi generate)

```bash
npx nuxi generate
```

`nuxi build --preset <static preset>` does the same.

- The default `premerged` mode writes every payload into `.output/public/_locales/`, so any static host can serve them.
- Pages are prerendered for each locale: under `prefix` the module seeds every localized root (`/en`, `/de`), and `/` is kept as a redirect stub.
- Leave [`prerenderRoutes`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#translationpayloads) off: the public copy already contains the payload files.
- With `source` mode or `publicAssets: false` there is nothing for the browser to read, and the build warns.

::note
There is no server to read a cookie or `Accept-Language`, so a saved locale does not redirect `/` on the first load. Under `no_prefix` the HTML holds the default locale, and a saved cookie is not applied on load: `$switchLocale` still works in the open page.
::

For Cloudflare Pages see [Cloudflare Pages](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#cloudflare-pages).

For a build with [locale domains](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/layers#multiple-domains), run generate once per domain, with `NUXT_I18N_DOMAIN` as the host of the run. Each tree then holds that domain's pages and payloads. Nitro has no variable for the output folder, so read your own from the config:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  nitro: { output: { publicDir: process.env.PUBLIC_DIR } },
})
```

```bash
NUXT_I18N_DOMAIN=example.de PUBLIC_DIR=sites/example.de npx nuxi generate
NUXT_I18N_DOMAIN=example.com PUBLIC_DIR=sites/example.com npx nuxi generate
```

- Keep the folders outside `.output`: each run empties it.
- Absolute links to the other domains are not crawled.
- Without the variable, a build with a `baseUrl` locale warns and generates the build config, where those locales are links and get no pages.
- On a Node server the same variable pins the process to one domain, whatever `Host` says.

A static host applies its own headers to these files; set caching in the host's config. The module's `/_locales/*` rule does reach Cloudflare Pages through `_headers` and Vercel through `config.json`, as `public, max-age=60`. To ship `.gz` / `.br` siblings, turn on `nitro.compressPublicAssets`: the module compresses the payload copy with the same settings.

## Cache headers and dateBuild

| Request                                                                                  | `Cache-Control`                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Node server or route, `?v=` equal to the current `dateBuild`, a non-empty dictionary     | `private, max-age=<httpCacheDuration>, immutable`                                                                       |
| Node server or route, without `?v=`, with an old one, or an empty dictionary             | `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`                                                                                    |
| A host's copy of `public/`, any `?v=`                                                    | `public, max-age=60` ([`httpCacheControl`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#httpcachecontrol)) |
| `source` mode, `cacheTtl`, or `apiBaseServerHost`: a dictionary can change with no build | the `httpCacheControl` header, always                                                                                   |
| Server route, the dictionary could not be read                                           | `503`, `no-store`                                                                                                       |
| dev server                                                                               | none                                                                                                                    |

Why the table looks like this:

- The URL with the current `v` is pinned like a hashed asset, and only what sees the query can say so: the server route, and a Node server, which sets the header on its static files.
- It is `private`, so a CDN that ignores the query cannot answer the next `v` from this response.
- A host's static files take a path-wide header from a `/_locales/**` route rule, which cannot see the query, so it stays short; a repeat load still blocks on nothing.
- An old `v` stays servable, as cached HTML names it.

`httpCacheControl: false` keeps every static file on `max-age=0, must-revalidate`. [`httpCacheDuration`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#httpcacheduration) defaults to one year; `0` sends no header. `$clearCache()` revalidates whatever it loads next.

Safari requests a preloaded payload again when it may not reuse the response: with `no-cache` and an `ETag` the second request is a `304`, with neither a cache header nor a validator it is a second full download. A `max-age` above `0` gives one request. Only `httpCacheDuration: 0` on a host that adds no validator pays this.

[`dateBuild`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#datebuild) is the `?v=` value. By default it is a hash of your translation files, so it changes only when translations change, and browsers keep their cached payloads across deploys that did not touch them. It also moves with the fallback chain.

- Set it yourself to pin a value.
- Set `0` or `''` to drop `?v=` entirely; payloads are then never `immutable`.

::tip
After replacing a dictionary in place on a Node server, restart with `NUXT_I18N_DATE_BUILD=<new value>`: nothing else moves `v` without a rebuild.
::

### Root and delta files

`premerged` writes one root per locale, `__root/<locale>/data.json`, and in each page's file only what differs from it.

- The page file marks the root it was made against with a `__i18n_root` key.
- The browser fetches both, the page shows nothing until both are in, and SSR merges them once per chunk.
- A file with no mark is a whole dictionary and stands alone: dev, `source` mode, the server route, and a host still holding older files all answer one, with no setting.

So anyone reading `_locales/*/data.json` directly reads a delta. Set `translationPayloads.rootDelta: false` to keep whole files.

A tab open across a deploy that asks for a new delta sees that it was made against another root, and fetches that root before showing it.

### When a dictionary cannot be read

A failed fetch from a host (anything but a 404), an unreadable or corrupt file, or a 200 that is not a JSON object reaches no cache, and the next request reads again:

- a page render logs a warning, shows raw keys for that dictionary and answers `503` with `Cache-Control: no-store`, the same in every CDN header (`CDN-Cache-Control`, `Cloudflare-CDN-Cache-Control`, `Netlify-CDN-Cache-Control`, `Vercel-CDN-Cache-Control`, `Surrogate-Control`, over any from a route rule) and `Retry-After: 60`;
- `/_locales/...` answers `503` with `no-store`;
- `useTranslationServerMiddleware` gives a `t` that answers the key or the default value.

What happens during the outage:

- **Visitors:** the body of that 503 is the page itself. On hydration the browser reads the dictionary again, and the text appears once the host is back, with Vue's one console error about a hydration mismatch, as the server's HTML had the keys.
- **Crawlers** are told to come back later.
- **Caches:** an `swr` or `cache` route rule stores nothing with a status of 400 or more, and a CDN gets `no-store`, so no cache keeps the raw keys and the first request after recovery renders the real text.
- **Pages already cached** by a rule stay as they are: the revalidation fails and stores nothing. On Vercel a failed `isr` revalidation keeps the last page the same way.

This covers every chunk a render loads, a failed page chunk with its root at hand included, and a chunk merged later in the render. A page with a healthy dictionary, a redirect and an error page keep their status. A [component island](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/server-side-translations) is the exception: it stays a 200, as a 503 would take it out of the page, so a page whose own dictionary loads can be kept with an island's raw keys. Requests during an outage each reach the host, with no timeout of the module's own beyond the 60 seconds for response headers.

A 404 from the host means it has no such file, which is not a failure. A page render shows the root dictionary, as the browser does, and `/_locales/...` answers the same 404. No cache keeps either, so a file that appears is read on the next request, at the cost of one request to the host per render of such a page. With no root file either the dictionary is empty, and a [prerender](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/upgrade#server-build-and-deployment) fails.

The server keeps loaded payloads in an in-process LRU cache of up to `cacheMaxSize` entries (1000 by default) that reloads an entry after `cacheTtl` when set; [Performance tuning](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance) covers both, and [`cacheStorage`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance#shared-cache-for-several-instances) adds a cache shared by instances. Do not add a Nitro `cache` route rule on `/_locales/**` on top: it keys by full URL, query included, and stores a third copy.

## App baseURL and payload hosts

**`app.baseURL`** needs nothing else. With `app.baseURL: '/shop/'` the browser fetches `/shop/_locales/...`; the copy stays in `.output/public/_locales/`, which Nitro serves under the base (a static host must mount the output at `/shop/`). Locale prefixes and [excluded paths](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/excluding-static-files) are matched without the base.

**`app.cdnURL`** moves the payloads too, when they are files in `public/`: the browser fetches and preloads `<cdnURL>/_locales/...`.

- The CDN must hold `_locales/` beside `_nuxt/`, at that path.
- It must allow your site's origin (CORS), as the file arrives by `fetch`.
- A dictionary only the server route answers (`source` mode, no public copy) stays on the app's origin.

A runtime `NUXT_APP_BASE_URL` on `cloudflare-module` needs Node compatibility (`nodejs_compat`). With `nitro.cloudflare.nodeCompat` off, which Nitro also falls to on an old date with no flag, it does not see the variable and serves `/`, plain Nuxt included, while a locale redirect still goes to the base. Set `app.baseURL` at build there.

To serve payloads from another origin, point the client and server at it and turn the local outputs off:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    apiBaseClientHost: 'https://cdn.example.com',
    apiBaseServerHost: 'https://cdn.example.com',
    translationPayloads: {
      serverHandler: false,
      publicAssets: false,
      serverAssets: false,
    },
  },
})
```

- On Node, `serverAssets` writes the same copy for the server's own reads, and that file answers `/_locales`: it must be off too, also if you keep the server route for the browser, which it would never reach.
- The host must serve the same `<apiBaseUrl>/<page>/<locale>/data.json` layout.
- The build warns when every local output is off and a host is missing.

**With [`baseUrl` on locales](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/layers#multiple-domains)** one build has one payload host, shared by every domain:

- **CORS.** The host must allow the origin of each domain, not only one.
- **A CDN that pulls from the app.** On a known host, `/_locales/...` answers only the locales that host serves. So if the CDN forwards one site's `Host` (say `example.com`), it gets a 404 for every locale of `example.de`, and may cache it. To avoid that:
  - upload `.output/public/_locales/` to the CDN; with one `nuxt generate` per domain, upload every output to the same path, since a locale on two domains has the same file;
  - or forward a `Host` that is not one of the locales' `baseUrl`, such as the CDN's own: the route then answers every locale.
- **A host per domain.** One build can't set one. Build once per domain instead, with `NUXT_I18N_DOMAIN` and `NUXT_I18N_APP_BASE_CLIENT_HOST` for each.

The same values can come from `NUXT_I18N_APP_BASE_URL`, `NUXT_I18N_APP_BASE_CLIENT_HOST` and `NUXT_I18N_APP_BASE_SERVER_HOST` at build time. `NUXT_I18N_APP_BASE_SERVER_HOST` also works at runtime and wins over the build value. An empty variable (`NUXT_I18N_APP_BASE_CLIENT_HOST=` in a `.env`) counts as unset, as does an empty option. See [`apiBaseServerHost`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#apibaseserverhost) for the details.

## Platforms

Only what the module or its output needs. Accounts, regions and CLI logins are in the platform's docs.

### Cloudflare Workers

Preset `cloudflare_module`. `wrangler deploy` bundles Nitro's output a second time with esbuild, and after that a raw `defineAsyncComponent(() => import('./X.vue'))` renders empty on the server. Nuxt's default error page is one, so a 404 has an empty body and the browser logs a hydration mismatch. The client then renders the page and the status stays 404, but without JavaScript the page is blank. This is [nuxt#33270](https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/issues/33270){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}: plain Nuxt without the module does the same. Page routes are not affected.

Turn the second bundle off:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  nitro: {
    preset: 'cloudflare_module',
    cloudflare: {
      deployConfig: true, // `wrangler` below applies only with it
      wrangler: {
        no_bundle: true,
        find_additional_modules: true,
        rules: [{ type: 'ESModule', globs: ['**/*.mjs'] }],
      },
    },
  },
})
```

```bash
npx nuxi build
cd .output/server && npx wrangler deploy -c wrangler.json
```

Set `compatibilityDate` to `2024-09-19` or later: an older one picks the legacy preset, which writes no `wrangler.json` and gives no error. The 404 then renders, and the upload gets smaller: 190 KiB gzip against 246 KiB on the test app. Your own `error.vue` is the other way out, but it covers only the error page.

The module itself does not need `nodejs_compat`. For the limits see [Bundle limits](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#bundle-limits-on-edge).

### Cloudflare Pages

Use the `cloudflare-pages-static` preset. `nuxi generate --preset cloudflare-pages` is a server build with no `index.html`.

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  nitro: {
    preset: 'cloudflare-pages-static',
    prerender: { autoSubfolderIndex: false },
  },
})
```

```bash
npx nuxi generate
npx wrangler pages project create my-site --production-branch main --force
npx wrangler pages deploy dist --project-name my-site --branch main
```

- **Output.** The preset writes to `dist/`, not `.output/public`.
- **`--force`.** Without it a new wrangler (4.156 here) hands `pages project create` over to Workers. With it you get a classic Pages project. It is needed once, for the create.
- **`autoSubfolderIndex: false`.** Pages answers `/de` with a 308 to `/de/` while canonical and `hreflang` name `/de`, so they point at a redirect. With this option the file is `de.html`, and the redirect is gone.
- **`NUXT_E1005` in the console on a 404** is a normal 404. Nuxt reports it that way because `404.html` starts on the client, before the app is mounted. The page works, and plain Nuxt prints the same line.

### Vercel and Vercel Edge

Presets `vercel` and `vercel_edge`, with no change to the app. The tags work without `metaBaseUrl`, from the platform's forwarded headers. Vercel Edge has a small bundle limit: see [Bundle limits](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#bundle-limits-on-edge). For a shared cache use the [`upstash` driver](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance#upstash-on-vercel-and-vercel-edge).

### Netlify

Presets `netlify` and `netlify_edge`.

```bash
npx nuxi build --preset netlify
npx netlify deploy --prod --no-build --dir dist --functions .netlify/functions-internal
```

- **Leave `nitro.output` unset.** The preset writes `.netlify/` and `dist/` itself.
- **Keep a `package.json` in the folder you deploy from.** Without one the CLI looks at the parent folder and deploys no function, with no error.
- **Netlify Edge** deploys with `--dir dist` alone. See [Dates on Edge runtimes](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#dates-on-edge-runtimes).

### Cloud Run

Use the default `node-server` build. `gcloud run deploy --source` needs a `Dockerfile` in the output folder when docker is not running locally:

```dockerfile
# .output/Dockerfile
FROM node:22-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY . .
ENV NODE_ENV=production
CMD ["node", "server/index.mjs"]
```

```bash
cd .output && gcloud run deploy my-app --source .
```

The tags work without `metaBaseUrl`, from the platform's forwarded headers.

### Deno Deploy

Preset `deno_deploy`. `deno deploy` replaces `deployctl`. Create a dynamic app with the entrypoint `server/index.ts`, and deploy from the output folder.

### Firebase

| Product          | Setup                                                                               |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| App Hosting      | Runs the Node build: use the default preset or `firebase-app-hosting`, and Node 20+ |
| Cloud Functions  | The `firebase` preset embeds the payloads and needs `firebase-functions`            |
| Hosting (static) | Serves `.output/public` as files, so `/_locales/**` gets Hosting's headers          |

On static Hosting, if JSON comes back with the wrong `Content-Type` or caching, add a `headers` entry for `/_locales/**` in `firebase.json`. Nuxt `routeRules` headers do not apply to files Hosting serves itself; the payload route sets its own `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control` on responses that do reach the server.

### AWS Amplify

`aws-amplify` keeps static files beside its compute folder, not next to the server, so the payloads are embedded like on a function platform.

### Several instances of one build

One artifact can run with a different default or disabled locale per instance through environment variables: see [Runtime overrides](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/runtime-overrides). A locale disabled only at runtime still has its static files in `public/`; disable it at build time if those must not be reachable.

Instances that load dictionaries from a remote host can share them in Redis, Upstash, Cloudflare KV or D1, Deno KV or another Nitro storage, so the backend gets one request instead of one per instance. It is a cache, not a source of translations: see [Shared cache for several instances](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance#shared-cache-for-several-instances).

## Behind a proxy or CDN

The app has to learn the public host and the scheme from the request.

| The proxy sends                              | Plain build                                                                            | Build with `baseUrl` on locales                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The real `Host`                              | Nothing to set                                                                         | Nothing to set                                                                                             |
| The origin's `Host`, plus `X-Forwarded-Host` | Nothing to set                                                                         | [`trustForwardedHost: true`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#trustforwardedhost) |
| Neither                                      | [`metaBaseUrl`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#metabaseurl) | No setting helps: every request looks like the origin's host, so change the proxy                          |

- **Routes under `swr` or `cache`.** The table does not hold there: see [Caching HTML](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#caching-html). Set `metaBaseUrl` or `site.url`.
- **`X-Forwarded-Proto`.** Send it, or canonical URLs read `http://` behind an HTTPS proxy. `metaBaseUrl` also fixes this.
- **In a domain build** the domain picks the base URL of the tags. `metaTrustForwardedHost` does not choose the domain there, only `trustForwardedHost` does.
- **Redirects are relative and the locale cookie has no `Domain`,** so both stay on the public host.

::warning
**Pin `metaBaseUrl` when the origin stays reachable** — On a plain build without `metaBaseUrl` or `site.url`, canonical, `hreflang` and `og:url` take their host from the request. [`metaTrustForwardedHost`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#metatrustforwardedhost) is on by default, so a direct request with `X-Forwarded-Host: evil.example` gets `https://evil.example` in those tags, and a cache in front spreads that page. A platform host such as `*.workers.dev` is exactly such an origin. `metaBaseUrl` closes this for `Host` too. A known host of a domain build keeps its own `baseUrl`. With `trustForwardedHost: true` a direct client can pick the page of another domain, so turn that on only behind a proxy that overwrites the header.
::

## Caching HTML

Most URLs are safe to cache, because they name their locale. These depend on the visitor:

| Setup                          | URLs                                              |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Default, `autoDetectPath: '/'` | `/`                                               |
| `prefix`                       | `/` and every unprefixed URL, which only redirect |
| `autoDetectPath: '*'`          | Every URL                                         |
| `no_prefix`                    | Every page                                        |

- **`Vary`.** Those responses carry `Vary` with `Cookie` when [`localeCookie`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#localecookie) is set and `Accept-Language` when `autoDetectLanguage` is on. A cache that honours it keeps the answers apart.
- **A cache that ignores `Vary`,** such as "cache everything by URL", must skip those URLs. Otherwise one visitor's `302 /de` reaches the next visitor, and a stored default page drops the redirect for everyone. On `/` you can also set `redirects: false`. Nitro's route cache keys on the path and its `varies` list, so keep `/` out of `swr` and `cache` rules as well.
- **`Set-Cookie`.** With `localeCookie` set, every server-rendered page under a prefix carries `Set-Cookie`, and a correct CDN will not store it. For cached HTML leave `localeCookie` off, or strip the header at the edge.
- **`swr` and `cache` rules need `metaBaseUrl` or `site.url`.** Nitro renders such a route with only the headers in `cache.varies`, so `Host`, `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Proto` are gone and the request URL reads `http://localhost`. Without a fixed origin, canonical, `hreflang` and `og:url` on those routes point at `http://localhost`, on every platform. Plain Nuxt's `useRequestURL()` reads the same there. Taking the host from the visitor instead would put one visitor's `X-Forwarded-Host` into the page every visitor gets. A domain build is not affected: its tags use the `baseUrl` of the locales. :br If one build serves several hosts and no single origin fits, let the rule see the headers and keep one copy per value: `'/blog/**': { swr: 60, cache: { varies: ['host', 'x-forwarded-host', 'x-forwarded-proto'] } }`. Every distinct value is a new cache entry, so a client that sends made-up headers fills the cache: put the origin behind a proxy that sets them.
- **`swr` and `cache` rules on a domain build.** The module adds `host` to `cache.varies` of every such rule, and `x-forwarded-host` with `trustForwardedHost`, so one domain does not serve another its page. A rule with `cache: false` stays as written. `isr` is the platform's cache: check that it keys on the host. With the host in the key, a client that sends made-up hosts adds cache entries.

For the payload files see [Cache headers and dateBuild](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#cache-headers-and-datebuild).

# DevTools

In `nuxt dev` the module adds two debugging aids: an **i18n Micro** tab in Nuxt DevTools for browsing and editing translation files, and a Vue DevTools inspector for the live locale and loaded dictionaries. Both exist only in development and add nothing to production builds. The Nuxt tab needs only Nuxt DevTools enabled; the Vue inspector also needs the Vue DevTools browser extension.

## Nuxt DevTools tab

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  devtools: { enabled: true }, // the tab is registered only when DevTools are on
})
```

Open Nuxt DevTools (`Shift + Alt + D`) and pick **i18n Micro**. The tab shows:

- every JSON file under `locales/` (root and `pages/`) of every layer, plus root files from `additionalTranslationDirs`;
- an editor per file; **Save** writes the file back to disk, and the dev server reloads the translations;
- **Export** / **Import** of a file as JSON, and **Stats** with key counts and translation coverage;
- a config view of the resolved module options;
- **Translate**, which fills missing keys with a machine-translation engine you configure in the tab's settings.

Saving writes only existing `.json` files inside your translation directories. When a file exists in several layers, the project's copy is written.

::tabs
  :::tabs-item{label="Editor"}
  ![The i18n Micro tab: the file tree on the left, keys with the default-locale text and an input per key on the right](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/devtools/02-translations-editor-dark.webp){height="852" width="1392"}
  :::

  :::tabs-item{label="Missing only"}

## Vue DevTools inspector

With the Vue DevTools browser extension, the module registers an i18n inspector (current locale, route chunk, loaded keys) and a timeline with locale switches, chunk loads and missing keys.

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    debug: true, // also log every $t / $ts / $tc call on the timeline
    // vueDevtools: false, // turn the inspector off, keep the Nuxt tab
  },
})
```

[`vueDevtools`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options) defaults to `true`. `debug: true` is verbose; keep it for short sessions.

## Outside Nuxt

The same UI is published as [`@i18n-micro/devtools-ui`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/devtools-ui-package) for Vite apps built on the framework packages; see that page for the setup.
