# Excluding paths

Some paths must never get a locale prefix or a locale redirect: an admin area, a health check, a generated feed. `excludePatterns` marks them, and a built-in list already covers Nuxt internals and common static files. An excluded page keeps exactly the path you wrote and still renders with `$t`.

## Exclude a path

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    excludePatterns: [
      '/admin', // /admin and everything below it
      '/preview-*', // glob over the whole path
    ],
  },
})
```

With this config `pages/admin/index.vue` answers only at `/admin`; there is no `/de/admin`, and `/admin` is never redirected to `/de/admin`.

## Pattern syntax

Patterns are matched against the path without `app.baseURL`:

| Pattern        | Matches                      | Does not match                |
| -------------- | ---------------------------- | ----------------------------- |
| `'/admin'`     | `/admin`, `/admin/users`     | `/administrator`, `/de/admin` |
| `'/preview-*'` | `/preview-1`, `/preview-a/b` | `/de/preview-1`               |
| `'/file-?'`    | `/file-a`                    | `/file-ab`                    |
| `/^\/v\d+\//`  | `/v2/docs`                   | `/docs`                       |

A string without `*` or `?` matches the path and whole segments below it. With `*` (any run of characters, slashes included) or `?` (one character) it must match the whole path. Always start strings with `/`.

## What is excluded already

These never get locale routes or redirects, without any config:

- `/api` and `/_nuxt`, and everything below them;
- the translations route, `/_locales` by default ([`apiBaseUrl`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#apibaseurl));
- any path with a segment starting with `__` (`/__nuxt_content`, `/en/__og-image__`);
- `/sitemap*.xml`, `/robots.txt`, `/favicon.ico`, `/apple-touch-icon*.png`, `/manifest.json`, `/sw.js`, `/workbox-*.js`;
- any path whose last segment ends in a static-file extension: `xml txt ico json js css png jpg jpeg gif svg webp avif pdf wasm map mp4 webm mp3 zip gz woff woff2 ttf eot`. Dotted page slugs like `/user/john.doe` and `.html` paths stay pages.

## What an exclusion does

- **Routes:** no localized variants are generated; the page is kept as written.
- **Redirects and 404s:** the server redirect plugin and the client redirect middleware skip the path.
- **Prerender:** matching paths are removed from the prerender route list.

It does not stop the i18n server middleware from detecting a locale for the request, and it does not stop the page from using translations. To keep a page localized but out of SEO tags, use `disableMeta` ([Page config](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/per-component-translations#turn-off-seo-tags)). To keep one page unlocalized from `nuxt.config.ts` by path, `globalLocaleRoutes: { '/admin': false }` ([Localized paths](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-locale-routes#in-nuxtconfig)) does the same for routing.

# FAQ

Short answers to the problems people hit most, for questions the topic pages do not answer head-on. Each answer links the page that owns the topic. If yours is not here, search the docs or open an [issue](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/issues){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## Translations

### `$t` fails in a plugin or a utility function

Composables need the Nuxt context. Outside `setup`, take the helper from the app, or run in its context after an `await`:

```ts
const nuxtApp = useNuxtApp()
const title = nuxtApp.$t('errors.unknown')
await nuxtApp.runWithContext(() => nuxtApp.$t('errors.unknown'))
```

In services that have no app at all, pass keys and translate them in the component.

### A key shows as raw text on one page only

The key is in another page's file. A page sees only the root file and its own `locales/pages/<route-name>/` file; move shared keys to the root file. See [Translation files](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations).

### Keys flash while a page transition runs

They should not: the leaving page's keys resolve until the transition ends. If they still flash, the key lives only in a page file that neither page owns (for example in a layout); move it to the root file.

### Translations are missing during SSR on Vercel, Netlify or Edge

The server function cannot read `public/` there, so payloads are embedded in the server bundle. That is the default; check that `translationPayloads.serverAssets` is not turned off. If the log says `public/ is not deployed next to the server`, set `nitro.serveStatic: false`. See [Deployment](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment).

### How do I put a link inside a translated sentence?

Use `<i18n-t>`: each named slot fills the `{placeholder}` of the same name.

```vue
<!-- "share": "Share your {link} with friends" -->
<i18n-t keypath="share">
  <template #link>
    <i18n-link :to="{ name: 'referral' }">{{ $t('referralLink') }}</i18n-link>
  </template>
</i18n-t>
```

See [`<i18n-t>`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/components/i18n-t). vue-i18n's linked messages and modifiers are not supported; compose in the template like this.

## Locales and URLs

### `/en/about` is a 404

With the default `prefix_except_default`, the default locale has no prefix: `/about` is English. Use `prefix` or `prefix_and_default` if you want `/en/...`. See [Routing strategies](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/strategy).

### Visitors are not redirected on deep links

By default only `/` follows the browser language or the cookie, so shared links keep their language. Set `autoDetectPath: 'no_prefix'` or `'*'`. See [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection#autodetectpath).

### The chosen language is forgotten after a reload

The locale cookie is off for the prefix strategies. Set `localeCookie: 'user-locale'`. See [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection#the-cookie).

### Can I switch locale without changing the URL?

Only with `strategy: 'no_prefix'`, where `$switchLocale('de')` reloads the dictionary on the same path. Under the prefix strategies the locale is part of the URL, so switching navigates. For a link instead of a call, use `$switchLocalePath('de')`.

### The page scrolls to the top when I switch locale

That is Nuxt's `scrollBehavior` for any navigation. Set `definePageMeta({ scrollToTop: false })` and restore the position yourself. The playground's [`SwitchLocalePreserve.vue`](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/blob/main/playground/components/SwitchLocalePreserve.vue){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} is a copyable wrapper ([demo page](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/blob/main/playground/pages/scroll-test.vue){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}).

## Build and integrations

### `nuxt-seo:defaults depends on nuxt-site-config:i18n but they are not registered`

An old `nuxt-site-config` only knows `@nuxtjs/i18n`. Upgrade `@nuxtjs/seo` to 3 or newer and list `nuxt-i18n-micro` before it in `modules`. See [SEO](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo).

### Build error about `@unhead/vue` on Cloudflare

Install `@unhead/vue` in the app so the prerender step finds it. The module itself does not need `nodejs_compat`: add `compatibility_flags = ["nodejs_compat"]` to `wrangler.toml` only if something else in the app does.

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Getting started" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/getting-started"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Translation files" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Locale detection" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Deployment" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment"}
::


# Getting started

This page takes a Nuxt app from no i18n to a translated page with a language switcher. You need it once, at the start of a project. You end up with localized URLs (`/about`, `/de/about`), one JSON file per locale and page, and `$t` in your templates.

## Install

The module needs Nuxt 3.18 or newer (Nuxt 4 works too) and Node 20 or newer.

::code-group
```bash [npm]
npm install nuxt-i18n-micro
```

```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add nuxt-i18n-micro
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add nuxt-i18n-micro
```

```bash [bun]
bun add nuxt-i18n-micro
```
::

## Configure the locales

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US', displayName: 'English' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE', displayName: 'Deutsch' },
      { code: 'fr', iso: 'fr-FR', displayName: 'Français' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
  },
})
```

That is all the configuration a first app needs. The defaults give you:

- `strategy: 'prefix_except_default'`: the default locale has no prefix (`/about`), the others do (`/de/about`). See [Routing strategies](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/strategy).
- `translationDir: 'locales'`: translation files live in `locales/` at the project root, also with the Nuxt 4 `app/` layout.
- `meta: true`: `hreflang`, canonical and `og:locale` tags, plus `lang` and `dir` on `<html>`. See [SEO](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo).
- A visitor who opens `/` is sent to the language their browser asks for (`Accept-Language`). See [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection).

`iso` is the language tag used in SEO tags; `code` is what appears in the URL. Every option is listed in [Module options](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options).

## Add translation files

Start the dev server with `nuxt dev`. When Nuxt resolves the pages, the module creates an empty `{}` file for every locale and page that has none (turn this off with [`disableWatcher`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#disablewatcher)):

```text
locales/
├── en.json            # root: keys every page can use
├── de.json
├── fr.json
└── pages/
    ├── index/         # pages/index.vue
    │   ├── en.json
    │   ├── de.json
    │   └── fr.json
    └── about/         # pages/about.vue
        ├── en.json
        ├── de.json
        └── fr.json
```

Fill in the root file and a page file:

```json
// locales/en.json
{ "nav": { "home": "Home", "about": "About" } }
```

```json
// locales/pages/index/en.json
{ "welcome": "Welcome, {name}!", "items": "no items | one item | {count} items" }
```

A page sees the root keys and its own keys; its own file wins on a clash. Folder names follow the route name (`pages/articles/[id].vue` is `locales/pages/articles-id/`). [Translation files](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations) covers the layout, fallbacks and loading.

## Use `$t` on a page

```vue
<!-- pages/index.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
const { t, tc, getLocale } = useI18n()

const title = t('nav.home') // 'Home'
</script>

<template>
  <h1>{{ $t('welcome', { name: 'Ada' }) }}</h1>
  <!-- Welcome, Ada! -->
  <p>{{ $tc('items', 3) }}</p>
  <!-- 3 items -->
  <p>{{ getLocale() }}</p>
  <!-- en -->
</template>
```

- In templates every helper is available with a `$` (`$t`, `$tc`, `$localePath`, …).
- In `<script setup>`, `useI18n()` returns the same helpers, with and without the `$` (`t` and `$t` are one function). It is auto-imported.
- `{name}` placeholders are filled from the params object; `{0}`, `{1}` from an array (`$t('pair', ['Ann', 'Bob'])` with `"pair": "{0} and {1}"`). Plural forms are separated by `|`; the count picks the form (0, 1, then the last one for everything above).

All helpers are listed in [Methods](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods).

## Link between pages and switch locale

```vue
<!-- components/AppHeader.vue -->
<template>
  <nav>
    <i18n-link :to="{ name: 'index' }">{{ $t('nav.home') }}</i18n-link>
    <i18n-link :to="{ name: 'about' }">{{ $t('nav.about') }}</i18n-link>
    <i18n-switcher />
  </nav>
</template>
```

- [`<i18n-link>`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/components/i18n-link) is a `NuxtLink` that points at the page in the current locale: on `/de` the about link goes to `/de/about`.
- [`<i18n-switcher>`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/components/i18n-switcher) is a dropdown of the enabled locales; it keeps the visitor on the same page.
- For your own buttons call `$switchLocale('de')`, which navigates to the current page in German and remembers the choice. For a plain `NuxtLink`, use `$localePath({ name: 'about' })` or `$switchLocalePath('de')`.

## Check it

Run `nuxt dev` and open:

| URL         | Shows                                                                  |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/`         | English home (or a redirect to `/de` when your browser prefers German) |
| `/de`       | German home                                                            |
| `/de/about` | German about page                                                      |
| `/en/about` | 404: the default locale has no prefix under `prefix_except_default`    |

Edits to the JSON files apply in the open page without a reload.

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Routing strategies" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/strategy"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Locale detection" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Migrating from @nuxtjs/i18n" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/migration"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Upgrading" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/upgrade"}
::


# Layers and domains

A Nuxt layer can carry the i18n config and the `locales/` folder for several apps, and each app adds or overrides what it needs. This page shows that, and how one build serves several domains.

## Share config and translations

```ts
// base/nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE' },
      { code: 'fr', iso: 'fr-FR' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
  },
})
```

```ts
// shop/nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  extends: ['../base'], // a layer directory or package, not a nuxt.config file
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'es', iso: 'es-ES' }, // added
      { code: 'fr', disabled: true }, // the base layer's fr, switched off here
    ],
  },
})
```

- **Config:** scalar options in the app replace the layer's. `locales` arrays from all layers are combined, and entries with the same `code` merge into one with the app's fields winning, so an app can add a locale or set fields such as `disabled: true` on an inherited one.
- **Translations:** `locales/` of every layer are merged key by key, layer first and app last, so a key in `shop/locales/en.json` overrides the same key in `base/locales/en.json`. Page files (`locales/pages/<page>/`) merge the same way.
- **Pages:** `$defineI18nRoute` is read from the pages of every layer.

To merge folders that are not part of a layer, list them in [`additionalTranslationDirs`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#additionaltranslationdirs).

## Multiple domains

One build serves every domain. List each locale with its domain; `baseDefault` makes it the default of that host:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    strategy: 'prefix_except_default',
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US', baseUrl: 'https://example.com', baseDefault: true },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE', baseUrl: 'https://example.de', baseDefault: true },
      { code: 'nl', iso: 'nl-NL', baseUrl: 'https://example.de' },
      { code: 'fr', iso: 'fr-FR' },
    ],
  },
})
```

Point both domains at the same server. The request's host decides the rest:

- **Default:** the host's `baseDefault` locale. Without one, the build default if the host serves it, else the host's first locale.
- **Served locales:** the locales of that host, plus every locale with no `baseUrl`. On `example.de` that is `de`, `nl` and `fr`.
- **Locales of other domains** are link targets. `$localePath`, `$localeRoute`, `$switchLocalePath`, `<i18n-switcher>` and `hreflang` give absolute URLs on their `baseUrl`, and `$switchLocale` navigates there. On this host their URLs are a 404, and a cookie or `Accept-Language` cannot pick them.
- **A link to another domain** goes through `$localePath` or `<i18n-link>`: `<NuxtLink :to="$localePath('/contact', 'de')">`, `<i18n-link :to="$localeRoute('/contact', 'de')">`. The router takes no absolute object, so `<NuxtLink :to="$localeRoute(...)">` and `router.push($localeRoute(...))` stay on this origin. On `localhost` or a preview host every locale with a `baseUrl` is such a link, the current one too. In code use `navigateTo($localePath('/contact', 'de'), { external: true })`, or `$switchRoute`.
- **Any other host** gets the build config, with every `baseUrl` locale as a link target. Nothing from the request is echoed: canonical and `hreflang` use `metaBaseUrl`, else the build default's `baseUrl` (a default with no `baseUrl` needs `metaBaseUrl` or `site.url`, see [SEO](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo#set-the-public-origin)).
- **Payload files** in `public/` are static: any host returns any locale's file. Per-domain [generate](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#static-site-nuxi-generate) publishes only that domain's.

`example.de` under each strategy, with `de: '/kontakt'` as a custom path of `contact`:

| Strategy                | `/`                | Default locale's page                              | Other URLs                                                                    |
| ----------------------- | ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `prefix_except_default` | `de`               | `/kontakt`                                         | `/de/kontakt` and `/en/contact` are a 404, `/contact` redirects to `/kontakt` |
| `prefix_and_default`    | `de`               | `/kontakt` and `/de/kontakt`, links use `/kontakt` | `/en/contact` and `/contact` are a 404                                        |
| `prefix`                | redirects to `/de` | `/de/kontakt`                                      | `/kontakt` redirects to `/de/kontakt`, `/en/contact` is a 404                 |
| `no_prefix`             | `de`               | `/kontakt`                                         | a custom path of a locale on another domain is a 404                          |

Under `prefix` a link from another domain keeps the prefix, since the unprefixed URL would only redirect. Under `no_prefix` a link to another domain lands on that host's default locale: the URL cannot name a second one.

Things to know:

- **Behind a proxy** the host comes from `Host`. If the proxy puts the public host in `X-Forwarded-Host` instead, set [`trustForwardedHost`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#trustforwardedhost), and only when the proxy overwrites that header. A proxy that sends neither cannot serve a domain build. See [Behind a proxy or CDN](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#behind-a-proxy-or-cdn).
- **`app.baseURL`** belongs in `baseUrl` too: `baseUrl: 'https://example.de/shop'` with `app.baseURL: '/shop'`.
- **Hosts match exactly.** `www.example.de` is another host: redirect it at the edge, or set that `baseUrl` on the locale. Only one host per locale.
- **Caches must key on the host.** A CDN normally does. Nitro's route cache keys on the path, so in a domain build the module adds `host` to `cache.varies` of every `swr` and `cache` rule, and `x-forwarded-host` with `trustForwardedHost`. A rule with `cache: false` stays as written. `isr` is the platform's cache: check that it keys on the host.
- **Custom paths of two host defaults must not collide.** The unprefixed records share one router, so `/x` cannot be one page on `example.de` and another on `example.com`.
- **Prerendered pages:** a `prerender: true` route rule in `nuxt build` renders once, with no host, and the file answers every domain. Leave pages that differ per domain to the server, or [generate per domain](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#static-site-nuxi-generate).
- **`noPrefixRedirect`** goes by the locale of the host and the visitor, on every host.
- **`hashMode`:** the host picks the render as above, links to another domain carry the route in the hash (`https://example.com/#/contact`).
- **`ssr: false`:** the browser reads the domain from `location.host`, so a host with no server still resolves.
- **[Runtime overrides](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/runtime-overrides)** apply first. A runtime `disabledLocales` holds on every host, with one exception: under `prefix_except_default` and `prefix_and_default` the default of a host stays enabled on its host, as its pages are the unprefixed records. Under `prefix` and `no_prefix` the host falls to the next locale it serves. A runtime `defaultLocale` applies to unknown hosts only.

For a [static site](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#static-site-nuxi-generate), generate once per domain.

### One app per domain

A shared layer with one small app per domain still works, when the domains need different pages or modules. Each app sets its own `defaultLocale` on top of the same `locales` list. A locale on another domain is a 404 in that app, as above.

### Choosing the locale in code

For a single instance answering every domain with the request's own origin in SEO tags, see [SEO](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo#set-the-public-origin); to choose the locale from the host in code, see [Custom locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-auto-detect).

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Translation files" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Runtime overrides" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/runtime-overrides"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="SEO" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo"}

# Locale detection

Every request gets one locale, picked from the same list of sources in the same order on the server and in the browser. Read this when you decide how first-time visitors land on a language, whether their choice is remembered, and what your server API sees. You get the precedence, the redirect each strategy makes, and the options that turn each source on or off.

::tip
**Prerequisites** — [Routing strategies](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/strategy)
::

## The precedence

The first source that names an **enabled** locale wins. An invalid or malformed value (an unknown code, a broken cookie) is skipped and the next source counts.

| # | Source                                                                                     | Counts when                                                                                                                                       |
| - | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 1 | URL prefix (`/de/about`)                                                                   | prefix strategies. Under `prefix_except_default` and `prefix_and_default` an unprefixed URL is the default locale                                 |
| 2 | `?locale=de`                                                                               | pages: `no_prefix` only. Server API helpers: always, and before the URL                                                                           |
| 3 | Locale state set by the app (`useI18nLocale().setLocale()`)                                | the URL has no locale                                                                                                                             |
| 4 | Cookie                                                                                     | [`localeCookie`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#localecookie) is set (`'user-locale'` automatically under `no_prefix`) |
| 5 | `Accept-Language` header                                                                   | [`autoDetectLanguage`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#autodetectlanguage) is `true` (default)                          |
| 6 | [`defaultLocale`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#defaultlocale) | always                                                                                                                                            |

So under a prefix strategy the URL decides what a page shows; the preference sources (3–5) only decide where a visitor is **redirected**, and only on the paths `autoDetectPath` allows. Under `no_prefix` there is nothing to redirect, and the preference sources decide what the page shows.

![Decision flow: a locale prefix in the URL renders that locale. Without one, no_prefix renders from the preference sources, prefix_and_default renders the default locale, and prefix or prefix_except_default redirect by preference when autoDetectPath allows the path](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/diagrams/locale-detection.svg)

## Redirects per strategy

Redirects are a `302`, made on the server before the page renders, and by a route middleware for client navigations. Query and hash are kept. With [`redirects: false`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#redirects) none happen; wrong prefixes are still a 404.

Visitor prefers `de` (cookie or header), `defaultLocale: 'en'`, default `autoDetectPath: '/'`:

| Request     | `prefix_except_default` | `prefix`      | `prefix_and_default` | `no_prefix`      |
| ----------- | ----------------------- | ------------- | -------------------- | ---------------- |
| `/`         | → `/de`                 | → `/de`       | `/` in `en`          | `/` in `de`      |
| `/about`    | `/about` in `en`        | → `/de/about` | `/about` in `en`     | `/about` in `de` |
| `/fr/about` | `/fr/about`             | `/fr/about`   | `/fr/about`          | —                |
| `/en/about` | 404                     | `/en/about`   | `/en/about`          | —                |

`prefix_and_default` never redirects: an unprefixed URL belongs to the default locale, and other locales live under their prefix. A visitor who prefers `en` is not redirected from `/` under `prefix_except_default`. Targets have no trailing slash (`/de`, not `/de/`) and follow custom paths (`/about` → `/de/ueber-uns`).

Wherever the cookie or the header decides (the redirect from `/`, every page under `no_prefix`), the response carries `Vary: Cookie, Accept-Language`, so a CDN keeps the answers apart.

### `autoDetectPath`

Where the preference sources may move a visitor:

| Value           | Preference counts on                                                                                |
| --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `'/'` (default) | `/` only. Deep links stay in the language of the URL                                                |
| `'no_prefix'`   | every path without a locale prefix (`/about` → `/de/about`)                                         |
| `'/welcome'`    | that exact path (a trailing slash is ignored)                                                       |
| `'*'`           | every path, prefixed ones too: `/about` and `/fr/about` → `/de/about` when the visitor prefers `de` |

- On paths it does not allow, an unprefixed URL is treated as the default locale.
- `prefix` is the exception: it has no unprefixed pages, so `/about` always goes to the visitor's locale (`/de/about` with cookie `de`, `/en/about` with no preference).
- With `'*'` the server ignores the app's state, and a prefixed URL no longer records its own locale in the cookie; the cookie changes when the visitor switches with `$switchLocale`.

::warning
With `'*'`, shared links open in the reader's language, which can surprise. Prefer `'/'` or `'no_prefix'` unless that is what you want.
::

## Accept-Language

The header is read as RFC 9110 defines it and matched against the locale **codes** in your config:

- Entries are tried by `q` value, highest first (`fr;q=0.1, de;q=0.9` → `de`). `q=0` means "not this language"; an entry with a malformed `q` is ignored. `*` matches nothing.
- `_` is read as `-` (`en_US` = `en-US`).
- Per entry: the exact code, then shorter forms (`de-AT` → `de`), then a regional locale of the same language (`en` → `en-US`). Exact and shorter forms do not depend on the order of `locales`; among several regional matches, the first in `locales` wins.
- Scripts are never crossed: `zh-TW` and `zh-HK` imply Traditional, `zh-CN` Simplified, so `zh-CN` never matches a `zh-Hant` locale.
- Disabled locales never match.

```ts
// locales: [{ code: 'en' }, { code: 'de' }, { code: 'zh-Hant' }]
// 'de-CH,de;q=0.9,en;q=0.8'  → 'de'
// 'en-GB'                    → 'en'
// 'zh-TW'                    → 'zh-Hant'
// 'zh-CN'                    → no match, next source
```

Turn header detection off with `autoDetectLanguage: false`; the cookie and the state still count.

## The cookie

- **Off by default** for the prefix strategies (`localeCookie: null`). Redirects then work from the header alone, and the choice is not remembered across visits. Set `localeCookie: 'user-locale'` to remember it.
- Under `no_prefix` it is `'user-locale'` unless you set another name. `localeCookie: null` turns it off there too.
- It is written when the visitor switches (`$switchLocale`, `<i18n-switcher>`, `useI18nLocale().setLocale()`), and on a server render of a page under a prefix (`/fr/about` stores `fr`; not under `autoDetectPath: '*'` with redirects on, where the URL can still move). A client navigation to a page stores that page's locale too, also on an unprefixed page of the default locale; a first load of that URL does not. Under `no_prefix` and in hash mode a navigation stores only a change. A 404 stores nothing, unless `$switchLocale` lands on it.
- It lasts one year (`path=/`, `SameSite=Lax`), with no `Domain` and no `Secure`. [`localeCookieOptions`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#localecookieoptions) changes them, e.g. `{ domain: '.example.com' }` to share the choice across subdomains, or `{ sameSite: 'none', secure: true }` for an app in an iframe (browsers drop `SameSite=None` without `Secure`).
- Under `hashMode` the preference lives in the `hash-locale` cookie instead; server and client read the same one. The server renders that locale and, outside `prefix`, never redirects; a locale in the hash (`/#/de`) wins over it and applies right after hydration. Under `prefix` there is no page on `/`, so `/` is rendered in the browser, which goes to `/#/de` by the cookie, then the browser language (`autoDetectLanguage`); any other document (`/about`, `/de`) redirects into the hash.

Read and set the preference with [`useI18nLocale`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/composables/useI18nLocale), not with `useCookie` or `useState` directly.

## Your own detection

To pick the locale yourself (a user setting, a subdomain), call `useI18nLocale().setLocale(code)` in a plugin that runs before the module's plugin. It becomes source 3, the app's state. [Custom locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-auto-detect) has the full recipe, including turning the built-in detection off.

## Server API routes

[`useLocaleServerMiddleware`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/server-side-translations) and `useTranslationServerMiddleware` use their own order, because an API URL is rarely localized:

1. `?locale=`
2. a `[locale]` route param, or a locale prefix in the path
3. cookie (when `localeCookie` is set)
4. `Accept-Language` (when `autoDetectLanguage` is on)
5. `defaultLocale`

`localeCookie: null` and `autoDetectLanguage: false` switch sources 3 and 4 off here too.

## Runtime overrides

[Runtime overrides](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/runtime-overrides) change the list the sources are matched against:

- Runtime `disabledLocales` are removed from every step: a cookie or header naming one is skipped.
- A runtime `defaultLocale` is step 6 under `prefix` and `no_prefix`.
- Under `prefix_except_default` and `prefix_and_default` the default locale is fixed at build (its pages are the unprefixed routes). A runtime `defaultLocale`, or disabling the build default, is ignored with a warning.

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Custom locale detection" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-auto-detect"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Server routes and API" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/server-side-translations"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-braces" title="useI18nLocale" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/composables/useI18nLocale"}
::


# Migrating from @nuxtjs/i18n

This page maps a `@nuxtjs/i18n` app onto nuxt-i18n-micro: options, helpers and file layout. Use it when you swap the module in an existing app. You keep your URLs (the strategy names are the same) and move translations into JSON files per page.

::tip
**Upgrading nuxt-i18n-micro itself?** — See [Upgrading](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/upgrade).
::

## Swap the module

```bash
npm uninstall @nuxtjs/i18n
npm install nuxt-i18n-micro
```

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts — before
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['@nuxtjs/i18n'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', language: 'en-US', file: 'en.json' },
      { code: 'de', language: 'de-DE', file: 'de.json' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    strategy: 'prefix_except_default',
    langDir: 'locales',
    detectBrowserLanguage: { useCookie: true, cookieKey: 'i18n_redirected', redirectOn: 'root' },
  },
})
```

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts — after
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    strategy: 'prefix_except_default',
    translationDir: 'locales',
    localeCookie: 'i18n_redirected',
    autoDetectPath: '/',
  },
})
```

## Options

| `@nuxtjs/i18n`                                                               | nuxt-i18n-micro                                                                                                                            |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `locales[].code`                                                             | `locales[].code`                                                                                                                           |
| `locales[].language` (`iso` before v9)                                       | `locales[].iso`                                                                                                                            |
| `locales[].name`                                                             | `locales[].displayName`                                                                                                                    |
| `locales[].dir`                                                              | `locales[].dir`                                                                                                                            |
| `locales[].domain`                                                           | `locales[].baseUrl` (an origin with its scheme)                                                                                            |
| `locales[].domainDefault`                                                    | `locales[].baseDefault`                                                                                                                    |
| `differentDomains`, `multiDomainLocales`                                     | not needed: `baseUrl` alone routes by host, see [Layers and domains](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/layers#multiple-domains) |
| `locales[].file` / `files`, `langDir`, `lazy`                                | `translationDir`; files are found by name and always loaded per page                                                                       |
| `defaultLocale`, `strategy`                                                  | same names, same four values                                                                                                               |
| `baseUrl`                                                                    | `metaBaseUrl`                                                                                                                              |
| `customRoutes: 'config'` + `pages`                                           | `globalLocaleRoutes`                                                                                                                       |
| `detectBrowserLanguage: false`                                               | `redirects: false` (no redirects) or `autoDetectLanguage: false` (ignore the header)                                                       |
| `detectBrowserLanguage.useCookie` / `cookieKey`                              | `localeCookie: '<name>'` (`null` turns the cookie off)                                                                                     |
| `detectBrowserLanguage.redirectOn: 'root'`                                   | `autoDetectPath: '/'` (default)                                                                                                            |
| `detectBrowserLanguage.redirectOn: 'no prefix'`                              | `autoDetectPath: 'no_prefix'`                                                                                                              |
| `detectBrowserLanguage.redirectOn: 'all'`                                    | `autoDetectPath: '*'`                                                                                                                      |
| `vueI18n` config file (`fallbackLocale`, `numberFormats`, `datetimeFormats`) | `fallbackLocale`, `numberFormats`, `datetimeFormats` in `i18n`                                                                             |

There is no `alwaysRedirect`: with a cookie set, `/` follows it on every visit. The full list is [Module options](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options); detection rules are on [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection).

## Helpers and composables

| `@nuxtjs/i18n` / vue-i18n                                          | nuxt-i18n-micro (template / `useI18n()`)                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `const { t } = useI18n()`                                          | `const { t } = useI18n()`, `$t` in templates                                                                                                |
| `t('key', count)`, `tc`                                            | `$tc('key', count)`                                                                                                                         |
| `te('key')`                                                        | `$has('key')`                                                                                                                               |
| `n(value, 'currency')`, `d(date, 'short')`                         | `$tn(value, 'currency')`, `$td(date, 'short')`                                                                                              |
| —                                                                  | `$tdr(date)`: relative time ("in 3 days")                                                                                                   |
| `locale.value`                                                     | `$getLocale()`                                                                                                                              |
| `locales.value`                                                    | `$getLocales()`                                                                                                                             |
| `setLocale('de')`                                                  | `$switchLocale('de')`                                                                                                                       |
| `useLocalePath()('about')`                                         | `$localePath({ name: 'about' })`                                                                                                            |
| `useLocaleRoute()`                                                 | `$localeRoute()`                                                                                                                            |
| `useSwitchLocalePath()('de')`                                      | `$switchLocalePath('de')`                                                                                                                   |
| `useSetI18nParams()`                                               | `$setI18nRouteParams()`                                                                                                                     |
| `useLocaleHead()`                                                  | automatic with `meta: true`; [`useLocaleHead`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/composables/useLocaleHead) for custom heads           |
| `defineI18nRoute({ paths: { de: '/ueber-uns' }, locales: [...] })` | `$defineI18nRoute({ localeRoutes: { de: '/ueber-uns' }, locales: [...] })`                                                                  |
| `<NuxtLinkLocale to="about">`                                      | `<i18n-link :to="{ name: 'about' }">`                                                                                                       |
| `<i18n-t>`                                                         | `<i18n-t>` (slots fill `{name}` placeholders)                                                                                               |
| `$i18n` in server routes                                           | `useTranslationServerMiddleware(event)`, see [Server routes and API](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/server-side-translations) |

`useI18n()` is auto-imported. `$defineI18nRoute` must keep its `$`: the build reads that call. All helpers: [Methods](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods).

## Translation files

Move the keys of one big file per locale into a root file plus one file per page:

```text
locales/
├── en.json              # keys used on many pages (nav, footer)
├── de.json
└── pages/
    ├── index/en.json    # keys of pages/index.vue
    └── about/en.json    # keys of pages/about.vue
```

Keeping everything in the root files works too, and is the quickest first step. Set `disablePageLocales: true` until you split them. See [Translation files](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations).

### Message syntax

| vue-i18n                          | nuxt-i18n-micro                                                            |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `{name}` named interpolation      | same                                                                       |
| `car | cars` (2 forms: 1 → first) | forms are picked by count from 0: write `no cars | one car | {count} cars` |
| `@:other.key` linked messages     | not supported: repeat the text or compose in code                          |
| `@.upper:` modifiers              | not supported: format in code or use `<i18n-t>`                            |
| `{'@'}` literal escapes           | not needed: only `{word}` tokens are replaced                              |
| JS/TS message files               | JSON only                                                                  |

The plural rule is replaceable with the [`plural`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#plural) option.

## Check after the switch

- Every URL you had still resolves; the strategy names match, custom paths move to `globalLocaleRoutes` or `$defineI18nRoute`.
- `hreflang`, canonical and `og:locale` come out of the box with `meta: true`; remove hand-written ones.
- A JSON parse error logs the file path; a missing key logs a warning in the browser console in dev.

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Translation files" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Routing strategies" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/strategy"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Locale detection" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection"}
::


# Page config

`$defineI18nRoute` sets i18n options for one page from inside the page itself. Use it when a page exists only in some locales, needs its own localized path, carries a few translations of its own, or must not get hreflang/canonical tags. The module reads the call at build time and bakes it into the generated routes.

## Restrict a page to some locales

```vue
<!-- pages/product/index.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
const { $defineI18nRoute } = useNuxtApp()

$defineI18nRoute({
  locales: ['en', 'de'],
})
</script>
```

Only `/product` and `/de/product` are generated under the default `prefix_except_default` strategy; the page has no route in any other locale. The same can be set from `nuxt.config.ts` with [`routeLocales`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#routelocales).

`$defineI18nRoute` is a Nuxt app injection, not a compiler macro: always take it from `useNuxtApp()` and call it with the `$`. Only `$defineI18nRoute(` is recognized by the build step.

## Add inline translations

Pass an object instead of an array. Its keys are the allowed locales, its values are merged into the page's dictionary for the active locale.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const { $defineI18nRoute } = useNuxtApp()

$defineI18nRoute({
  locales: {
    en: { greeting: 'Hello' },
    de: { greeting: 'Hallo' },
    fr: {}, // allowed, no inline keys
  },
})
</script>

<template>
  <h1>{{ $t('greeting') }}</h1>
</template>
```

Inline translations ship inside the page component for every locale. Prefer [page translation files](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations) for anything larger than a few keys; keep inline keys for self-contained pages and components.

## Set localized paths

```ts
$defineI18nRoute({
  locales: ['en', 'de'],
  localeRoutes: {
    en: '/welcome',
    de: '/willkommen',
  },
})
```

With `prefix_except_default` and `defaultLocale: 'en'` this produces `/welcome` and `/de/willkommen`. A `path` inside an inline locale object does the same: `locales: { de: { path: '/willkommen' } }`. Dynamic params, nested routes and the config-level alternative are covered in [Localized paths](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-locale-routes).

## Keep a page out of localization

```ts
$defineI18nRoute(false)
```

The page gets one route, with no locale prefix and no locale variants, as with [`globalLocaleRoutes: { page: false }`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#globallocaleroutes). An entry for the page in `globalLocaleRoutes` still wins.

## Turn off SEO tags

```ts
$defineI18nRoute({
  disableMeta: true, // no hreflang, canonical or og:locale tags on this page
})

$defineI18nRoute({
  disableMeta: ['de'], // only the de version has no tags
})
```

The config-level alternative is [`routeDisableMeta`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#routedisablemeta). What the tags are is on the [SEO](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo) page.

## What the build can read

The build step finds the call in each page file and evaluates its argument without running your app. It works when the config is:

- a literal object (strings, arrays, nested objects, template literals, ternaries on `process.env.NODE_ENV`);
- built from constants declared in the same `<script setup>` (`const locales = ['en', 'de']`, spreads included);
- an array of objects with a `code` field (`[{ code: 'en' }, { code: 'de' }]`).

It cannot read values imported from another module, or anything that needs your app at runtime (composables, `await`, fetched data). In that case the build logs `Ignored the $defineI18nRoute() config in <file>` and the page keeps the default locales and routes.

At runtime the call only merges the inline translations for the current locale and re-merges them when the locale changes. `locales`, `localeRoutes` and `disableMeta` take effect only through the build, so changing them needs a rebuild (the dev server rebuilds on save).

## Related

::card-group

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Translation files" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="SEO" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-braces" title="$defineI18nRoute reference" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods"}
::


# Performance tuning

The defaults are tuned for a typical app: one JSON payload per page and locale, translations kept off the HTML, bounded caches on the server. This page lists the few settings worth changing when a catalog is large, the server is memory-constrained, or payloads come from another host. For measured numbers against `@nuxtjs/i18n` and plain Nuxt, see [Benchmarks](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance-results).

## What the defaults already do

- **One payload per page.** The build merges root, page and fallback-locale keys into `/_locales/<page>/<locale>/data.json`, so a page loads one file and `$t` is a single lookup.
- **No dictionary in the HTML.** SSR keeps translations in server memory; the browser fetches the payload instead of parsing it from `__NUXT_DATA__`.
- **Browser cache.** `?v=` changes only when translations do, so a browser keeps its payloads across deploys that did not touch them. A host's static copy is fresh for 60 seconds and revalidates after that: a repeat load waits for one `304`. The server route answers `immutable` for a year ([Deployment](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#cache-headers-and-datebuild)).
- **Bounded server memory.** The server caches at most 1000 payloads by default and drops the least recently used.

## Split translations by page

Keys used on one page belong in `locales/pages/<page>/<locale>.json`, not in the root files: root keys are part of every page's payload. See [Translation files](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations).

Two settings change this split:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    // pages that show the same keys share one payload: /de/products/123 loads the products payload
    routesLocaleLinks: { 'products-id': 'products' },
    // or: no page files at all, every page loads only the root dictionary
    // disablePageLocales: true,
  },
})
```

[`routesLocaleLinks`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#routeslocalelinks) cuts duplicate payloads for related routes. [`disablePageLocales`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#disablepagelocales) suits small apps where one dictionary per locale is simpler.

## Server caches

| Setting                                                                                  | Default | Effect                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [`cacheMaxSize`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#cachemaxsize) | `0`     | Max entries in the payload caches. `0` = no limit in the browser, 1000 on the server.                                                     |
| [`cacheTtl`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#cachettl)         | `0`     | Seconds before a cached entry is reloaded. `0` = never; set it when payloads come from `apiBaseServerHost` and change without a redeploy. |
| `serverTranslationPreload`                                                               | `false` | Load the `index` payload in the Nitro middleware for every page request, so server helpers and the home page reuse it.                    |

Lower `cacheMaxSize` on a small instance with many pages × locales. Locally edited translations never need a TTL: dev reads files live, production payloads change only with a deploy.

## Memory on a Node server

Under steady load a Node server can sit at about 12 times its live heap and stay there. On a stress test of 100k keys per page, a live heap of 90 MB ran at about 1.1 GB of RSS. This is not a leak. After one oversized GC cycle V8 raises its heap limit, and it keeps the freed pages in a pool for reuse while load lasts. About 8 seconds after load stops the pool empties and RSS falls to about 160 MB. `global.gc()` does not return this memory. Plain Nuxt without the module does the same, scaled to its smaller heap.

It costs headroom: with a memory limit below that level and no heap cap, the process can be killed. Set a cap that fits your limit and sits well above the live heap:

```bash
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=512 node .output/server/index.mjs
```

| 100k keys, 12 locales, 5 to 30 minutes of load | Default        | `--max-old-space-size=512` |
| ---------------------------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------- |
| RSS under load                                 | about 1,150 MB | 254-287 MB                 |
| Requests per second                            | 624            | 517-572                    |

So the cap trades 8 to 10 % of throughput for the memory. A catalog of ordinary size has a smaller heap and a smaller step. These runs were on macOS with Node 22, not in a container.

## Parse time and `dir`

`dir: 'auto'` on a locale makes the browser work out the direction from the content while it parses. In Chromium, DOMContentLoaded at 20,000 elements was about 1.1 s with `dir="auto"` and 0.1 s without it, and at 5,000 elements about 130 ms against 45 ms. Leave `dir` unset or set it to `ltr` or `rtl` ([Text direction](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/seo#text-direction)).

## Shared cache for several instances

With several instances of one build, [`cacheStorage`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#cachestorage) gives them one dictionary cache in any Nitro storage, on the connection your app configures in `nitro.storage`. The module adds no connector and no dependency.

**It is a cache, not a source.** Translations come from the embedded or public payloads, or from `apiBaseServerHost`. Only what came from the source is written, and keys carry the build, so a store you fill by hand is not read. To serve translations from KV or a database, put a small route that reads it at `apiBaseServerHost`.

**When it helps.** Only with a remote `apiBaseServerHost`. Three instances walking 39 dictionaries made 117 requests to the host without it and 48 with it. With files on disk a store hit is no faster than the file, and a first pass over 12 pages took 280-296 ms without the option and 308-325 ms with a filled Redis, so leave it unset. On a preset that embeds dictionaries it does nothing without a host, and the build says so.

A cold dictionary, one client, one walk each, so rough, and most of it is the distance to the host:

| Store                      | From the host | From the store |
| -------------------------- | ------------- | -------------- |
| Cloudflare KV              | about 300 ms  | about 110 ms   |
| D1                         | about 230 ms  | about 115 ms   |
| Deno KV                    | about 430 ms  | about 100 ms   |
| Upstash, Vercel serverless | about 445 ms  | about 245 ms   |
| Upstash, Vercel Edge       | about 505 ms  | about 235 ms   |

### Redis

Needs `ioredis` in your project.

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  nitro: {
    storage: {
      redis: { driver: 'redis', url: process.env.REDIS_URL },
    },
  },
  i18n: {
    cacheStorage: 'redis', // the mount name
    apiBaseServerHost: 'https://translations.internal',
    cacheTtl: 300,
  },
})
```

### Upstash on Vercel and Vercel Edge

Use the `upstash` driver on both: it talks REST, where the `redis` driver needs TCP. It needs `@upstash/redis` in your project, and reads `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` from the environment.

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  nitro: {
    storage: {
      upstash: { driver: 'upstash' },
    },
  },
  i18n: {
    cacheStorage: 'upstash',
    apiBaseServerHost: 'https://translations.example.com',
  },
})
```

### Cloudflare KV

Bind a namespace to the Worker as `I18N_KV` (`kv_namespaces` in its wrangler config).

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  nitro: {
    storage: {
      kv: { driver: 'cloudflare-kv-binding', binding: 'I18N_KV' },
    },
  },
  i18n: {
    cacheStorage: 'kv',
    apiBaseServerHost: 'https://translations.example.com',
  },
})
```

A host that is another Worker on the same account needs the `global_fetch_strictly_public` compatibility flag, or the fetch does not reach it.

### Cloudflare D1

`nitro.storage` cannot hold a database object, so a Nitro plugin mounts the driver. The mount is checked on first use, so that is early enough. Bind the database as `I18N_DB` (`d1_databases`) and have `unstorage` in your project.

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  nitro: {
    experimental: { database: true },
    database: {
      default: { connector: 'cloudflare-d1', options: { bindingName: 'I18N_DB' } },
    },
  },
  i18n: {
    cacheStorage: 'd1',
    apiBaseServerHost: 'https://translations.example.com',
  },
})
```

```ts
// server/plugins/i18n-storage.ts
import dbDriver from 'unstorage/drivers/db0'

export default defineNitroPlugin(() => {
  useStorage().mount('d1', dbDriver({ database: useDatabase() }))
})
```

The `db0` driver is marked experimental and ignores the TTL: rows of old builds stay until you delete them.

### Deno KV

On Deno Deploy, provision a database (`deno deploy database provision <name> --kind denokv`), assign it to the app (`deno deploy database assign`), and use the driver:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  nitro: {
    storage: {
      kv: { driver: 'deno-kv' },
    },
  },
  i18n: {
    cacheStorage: 'kv',
    apiBaseServerHost: 'https://translations.example.com',
  },
})
```

### How it behaves

A dictionary is looked up in the instance's own cache, then in the shared storage, then at its source. The instance's own cache stays, because `$t` is synchronous and needs the tree in memory: this separates who fetches from who serves, it does not save memory.

- **Who fetches.** With a remote host, one fetch from the backend per dictionary instead of one per instance. Instances that miss at the same moment each fetch it, because there is no lock.
- **Pages without their own dictionary** are not stored, so that made-up page names cannot add keys. Each instance fetches such a page from the host once, and on Workers, where isolates come and go, that is a steady trickle.
- **The host is down.** Pages with a stored dictionary work. A page with none renders from the stored root dictionary, its own keys raw, with [a `503` no cache keeps](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#when-a-dictionary-cannot-be-read), and `/_locales` answers `503` for it until the host is back. `useTranslationServerMiddleware` answers keys for a dictionary it cannot read.
- **The host** is `NUXT_I18N_APP_BASE_SERVER_HOST` at runtime, or else `apiBaseServerHost` from the build, the same as without the option. On a preset that embeds dictionaries (Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify, see [Deployment](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#serverless-and-edge)) the layer applies only with a host: the data is already in the bundle, and a copy in KV would be a network read for what memory holds.
- **Keys** are `i18n-micro:<buildId>~<dateBuild>~<fallbackLocale>~<host>:<locale>:<page>`, so two builds in a rolling deploy never read each other, and neither do two backends of one artifact. Each instance must come from one build (one artifact, or a pinned Nuxt [`buildId`](https://nuxt.com/docs/api/nuxt-config#buildid){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}); instances built separately simply do not share. With a pinned `buildId` and `dateBuild: 0`, two different builds do share keys. Only enabled locales are looked up, and page names over 200 characters skip the layer.
- **What is stored.** A dictionary is compared with the root one (`__root`) before it is written, and goes in only when it holds every root key and differs from the root. So a made-up page answered with the root adds no key, and neither does a 200 error body on a page. Each instance reads such a page from the source once. A host must answer unknown pages with the root, an empty object or a 404, and serve `__root`. A host without `__root`, or one that serves pages without the root keys, shares nothing. If the host answers `__root` itself with a well-formed error, that is stored: keep `cacheTtl` short when the backend can do that.
- **Expiry.** An entry expires `cacheTtl` seconds after it was written, or after one day when `cacheTtl` is `0`, so keys of old builds cannot pile up. A value can stay in an instance's own cache for another `cacheTtl`, and in the render's chunk cache for one more: backend changes show within three times `cacheTtl`. Drivers without expiry (`fs`) keep old keys until you remove them.
- **When the storage fails** the page does not. A read may take 1 second, which covers a connection handshake and a Cloudflare KV key that is cold at that location. After a failure the limit is 250 ms until the store answers again. Three failures in a row close the layer for 5 seconds. While it is closed, and while a read has just failed, nothing is written. A failed write closes nothing, so a read-only replica keeps serving reads. A store whose answers take longer than these limits counts as failing: a miss, and the dictionary comes from its source. With ioredis that starts near 400 ms per command, because its handshake takes three round trips. The module logs one warning per minute; ioredis prints its own errors on top of that. A value that is not a dictionary counts as a miss and is overwritten. An unknown mount name warns once on first use; the app then runs without the layer.
- **When the source fails** nothing keeps the failure. A failed fetch or an unreadable file reaches no cache, this one or the instance's own, and the next request reads again. See [Deployment](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#when-a-dictionary-cannot-be-read).
- **Off in dev and in prerender**, which read their files and must not need your production Redis.
- **Invalidation.** There is no purge call: a new build uses new keys. To refresh a running build at once, remove the `i18n-micro:` keys from the storage and restart the instances. `clearCache` and HMR only touch process state.
- Runtime changes (`$mergeTranslations`, `$defineI18nRoute`) stay in the render or the browser that made them and are never written to the storage.

## Payload size

The build warns when the payload output passes `translationPayloads.warnFileCount` (500 files) or `warnSizeBytes` (10 MB). When it does:

- move page-only keys out of the root files;
- link routes that show the same keys (`routesLocaleLinks`);
- on serverless or Edge, use `translationPayloads.mode: 'source'` so the server bundle embeds compact sources instead of every page × locale ([Deployment](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#serverless-and-edge)). An Edge build warns on its own past the platform's limit ([Bundle limits](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#bundle-limits-on-edge));
- enable `nitro.compressPublicAssets` for `.gz` / `.br` copies of the static payloads.

## Measuring

The repository tracks what the playground ships with `pnpm run budget:payload`; the current numbers:

Measured on `playground` across `/`, `/de`:

| Measurement                      | Size     |
| -------------------------------- | -------- |
| Translation sources on disk      | 7.8 MB   |
| Served as separate payload files | 23.9 MB  |
| Largest inline `__NUXT_DATA__`   | 0.4 KB   |
| Client assets                    | 624.4 KB |

The playground is a test bench with generated dictionaries of up to 100k keys, so these are not figures to expect from a real
application — they are a fixed point to measure against. The budget fails when they grow unexpectedly,
which is how an accidental change to what the payload carries gets noticed.

Run the benchmark suite yourself with `pnpm test:performance`; how it works is in the [benchmark methodology](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/performance-methodology).

# Performance Test Results

## Project Information

- **[plain-nuxt](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/tree/main/scripts/perf-fixtures/plain-nuxt){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}**: ./scripts/perf-fixtures/plain-nuxt
- **[i18n-micro](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/tree/main/scripts/perf-fixtures/i18n-micro){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}**: ./scripts/perf-fixtures/i18n-micro
- **[i18n](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/tree/main/scripts/perf-fixtures/i18n){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}**: ./scripts/perf-fixtures/i18n
- **CLI**: `pnpm test:performance`

### Description

Compares **plain Nuxt**, **i18n-micro**, and **`@nuxtjs/i18n`** under one shared dictionary profile via `untestutils/perf`.

Focus: build time, peak RSS, deployable **code vs translations (asset) vs total**, and load (Artillery).

### Methodology notes

- Metrics are **means of 3 consecutive runs per fixture** (not interleaved).
- **Artifact**: Nitro node-server `.output/server/index.mjs` after forced `nuxi build`; `nuxt-i18n-micro` is the **built module dist** (not `dev:prepare` jiti stub). See [benchmark methodology](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/performance-methodology).
- **Translations** = `bundle.asset` (locale JSON, `chunks/raw/`, matching locale chunks via `isTranslationFile`).
- **Code** excludes source maps (`*.map`): the fixtures link the module from the repo, so Nitro writes full maps for it and none for npm dependencies.
- **plain-nuxt** serves the same leaf volume as static JSON — I/O-heavy under load, not “i18n overhead”.
- Load profile `--load full`: warm 6s\@6 + main 60s\@60 uncapped (historical).
- Cool-downs `--cool fast` (see methodology doc).
- Each of the `runs` builds is **forced** (no warm-cache zeroing of build time).
- Artillery **Error rate** in tables is HTTP-status errors from the load metrics. Charts also plot `vusers.failed` (client timeouts under saturation); those can be high while HTTP error rate stays 0%.

### Runs

All metrics below are **means across 3 runs**.

---

| Pages           | **2** (`index`, `page`)                                                                  |
| Index tree      | depth **5**, branch **7** → **16,807** leaf keys / locale                                |
| Secondary pages | depth **5**, branch **6** → **7,776** leaf keys / page / locale                          |
| Goal            | Default CLI profile (`--locales 4 --keys 10000`); raise knobs for regression-radar loads |

Dictionaries come from `scripts/perf-fixtures/perf-shared/runtime.json` (written by the CLI) so all three fixtures stay aligned.

## Notes

- Shared profile: 4 locales × 2 pages × \~16.8k index leaves.
- Load: programmatic Artillery only — warm **6s\@6** + main **60s\@60**, uncapped VU (historical YAML methodology). Paths from runtime profile — see `scripts/src/perf/load.ts`.
- Cool-downs: 2s post-build, 3s between runs, 5s between fixtures. Builds are forced each run so means are not diluted by cache hits.
- Re-run day-to-day: `pnpm test:performance` (`--load short --cool fast`).
- Regenerate this page: `pnpm -C scripts cli performance --load full --only all --runs 3`.
- Flags: `--locales N --keys K --only all|micro|i18n|plain --runs N --skip-load --cool fast|strict`.


# Runtime overrides

Runtime overrides let one build artifact run with different locale settings per environment or tenant, without rebuilding. You can change the default locale, the fallback locale, which locales are disabled, the SEO origin (`metaBaseUrl`) and, in a build with locale domains, each locale's `baseUrl`. Routing, redirects, rendering and server helpers use the overridden values, and so does the browser on a server-rendered page.

## Set overrides with environment variables

```bash
NUXT_I18N_DEFAULT_LOCALE=de \
NUXT_I18N_FALLBACK_LOCALE=en \
NUXT_I18N_DISABLED_LOCALES=fr,it \
node .output/server/index.mjs
```

| Variable                                                                             | Alias                                       |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------- |
| `NUXT_I18N_DEFAULT_LOCALE`                                                           | `NUXT_PUBLIC_I18N_RUNTIME_DEFAULT_LOCALE`   |
| `NUXT_I18N_FALLBACK_LOCALE`                                                          | `NUXT_PUBLIC_I18N_RUNTIME_FALLBACK_LOCALE`  |
| `NUXT_I18N_DISABLED_LOCALES` (comma-separated)                                       | `NUXT_PUBLIC_I18N_RUNTIME_DISABLED_LOCALES` |
| `NUXT_I18N_META_BASE_URL`                                                            | `NUXT_PUBLIC_I18N_RUNTIME_META_BASE_URL`    |
| `NUXT_I18N_LOCALE_BASE_URLS` (`de=https://de.example.com,fr=https://fr.example.com`) | `NUXT_PUBLIC_I18N_RUNTIME_LOCALE_BASE_URLS` |

The server reads them once at start; restart to apply a change. On a server-rendered page the browser gets the resolved values from the server. With `ssr: false` there is no server render and the browser has no environment: only `runtimeConfig.public.i18nRuntime` applies there, and the browser logs the warnings below.

## Set overrides in runtimeConfig

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  runtimeConfig: {
    public: {
      i18nRuntime: {
        defaultLocale: 'de',
        fallbackLocale: 'en',
        disabledLocales: ['fr'],
        metaBaseUrl: 'https://staging.example.com',
        // a string as in the variable, or an object
        localeBaseUrls: { de: 'https://de.staging.example.com' },
      },
    },
  },
})
```

A value set in `runtimeConfig.public.i18nRuntime` wins over the `NUXT_I18N_*` variable for the same field.

Not to be confused with the build-time `DEFAULT_LOCALE` variable, which replaces `defaultLocale` while building and needs no runtime support.

## What can and cannot change

| Setting             | At runtime                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultLocale`     | Yes under `prefix` and `no_prefix`. Under `prefix_except_default` and `prefix_and_default` it is fixed at build (its pages are the unprefixed routes); an override is ignored with a warning.                                                                                                                                          |
| `fallbackLocale`    | Yes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `disabledLocales`   | Adds to the locales disabled at build; never re-enables one. The build default cannot be disabled under `prefix_except_default` / `prefix_and_default`.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `strategy`          | No. A runtime strategy is ignored with a warning; build one artifact per strategy.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `metaBaseUrl`       | Yes: canonical and hreflang take it in place of the build value. On a host of a locale domain the host's own origin still applies.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `locales[].baseUrl` | Only in a build that already has locale domains (some `locales[].baseUrl` at build): the path strategy for domains is chosen at build. Without them the override is ignored with a warning. A code that is no locale, or a value that is not an absolute URL, is ignored with a warning. A locale with no domain at build can get one. |

Invalid values never break the app. Each case logs one warning per server process:

- disabling every locale is ignored;
- a `defaultLocale` that is not enabled falls back to the first enabled locale;
- a `fallbackLocale` that is not enabled keeps the build value if it is enabled, otherwise there is no fallback.

## Read the effective config

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const { $getI18nConfig } = useNuxtApp()
const config = $getI18nConfig() // build config with overrides applied
</script>
```

Treat it as read-only: on the server it is shared by every request and frozen in development; the browser copy is not frozen. Importing the config from `#build/i18n.strategy.mjs` gives the build values without overrides.

## Origins at runtime

One build can serve staging and production on different hosts:

```bash
NUXT_I18N_LOCALE_BASE_URLS=en=https://staging.example.com,de=https://staging.example.de \
NUXT_I18N_META_BASE_URL=https://staging.example.com \
node .output/server/index.mjs
```

The hosts of the build then are unknown hosts: they get the build config, as any other host. `metaBaseUrl` (the origin of an unknown host's canonical and hreflang) does not move with them: set `NUXT_I18N_META_BASE_URL` too when the default locale's domain moves. The browser of a server-rendered page gets the changed origins with the page.

`nuxt generate` per host (`NUXT_I18N_DOMAIN`) is build time: the prerendered pages keep the origins of the build, and runtime `baseUrl`s do not reach them.

## Disabled locales and static files

A runtime-disabled locale answers 404 on its routes and payload route, but its payload files are still in `.output/public/_locales/` and a static file server returns them. When those files must not be reachable, disable the locale at build time with `disabled: true`.
