# SEO

With `meta: true` (the default) every localized page gets `<html lang dir>`, a canonical link, `hreflang` alternates, `x-default` and Open Graph locale tags. You need this page when you want to set the public origin, tune which locales appear in the tags, or override them for one page. Most sites only need a `site.url` or `metaBaseUrl` and correct `iso` codes.

## Minimal setup

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US', dir: 'ltr' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE', dir: 'ltr' },
      { code: 'ar', iso: 'ar-SA', dir: 'rtl' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    metaBaseUrl: 'https://example.com',
  },
})
```

`/de/about` then renders:

```html
<html lang="de-DE" dir="ltr">
<link rel="canonical" href="https://example.com/de/about">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en-US" href="https://example.com/about">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de-DE" href="https://example.com/de/about">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="ar-SA" href="https://example.com/ar/about">
<link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://example.com/about">
<meta property="og:locale" content="de_DE">
<meta property="og:url" content="https://example.com/de/about">
<meta property="og:locale:alternate" content="en_US">
<meta property="og:locale:alternate" content="ar_SA">
```

## Text direction

`<html dir>` comes from the locale's `dir`. Without one, a language written right to left gets `rtl`, read from `iso` (or `code`): Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu and a few others, and any tag with an RTL script such as `az-Arab`. Every other locale gets no `dir` attribute, which browsers read as `ltr`.

::warning
**`dir: 'auto'` costs parse time on large pages** — `auto` on `<html>` makes the browser work out the direction from the content while it parses. In Chromium that cost grows faster than the page: about 100 ms at 5,000 elements and 1 s at 20,000. Use it only for a small page whose language you cannot know.
::

## Which tags you get

- **hreflang**: one tag per locale that serves the page, value `iso` (or `code` when `iso` is missing), its URL with the same query as the canonical. A page restricted with [Page config](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/per-component-translations) or `routeLocales` lists only its locales. [`hreflangBaseLanguage: true`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#hreflangbaselanguage) also adds the bare language (`es-ES` → `es`) for the first regional locale.
- **x-default**: the default locale's URL, only when the default locale serves the page.
- **og\:locale**: derived from `iso` (`en-US` → `en_US`). Set `og` on the locale when the mapping is not direct, for example `{ code: 'zh', iso: 'zh-Hans', og: 'zh_CN' }`; without either, no `og:locale` is written and dev mode warns.
- **canonical / og\:url**: the current URL without query parameters, except those in [`canonicalQueryWhitelist`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#canonicalquerywhitelist) (default `page`, `sort`, `filter`, `search`, `q`, `query`, `tag`).

By strategy:

| Strategy                                                | hreflang and x-default           | canonical, og\:url, og\:locale, html attrs |
| ------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `prefix`, `prefix_except_default`, `prefix_and_default` | yes                              | yes                                        |
| `no_prefix`                                             | no (one URL serves every locale) | yes                                        |

## Set the public origin

Absolute URLs use the first of:

1. [`metaBaseUrl`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#metabaseurl);
2. `site.url` from `nuxt-site-config` (installed by `@nuxtjs/seo`);
3. the request origin, with `app.baseURL` appended.

Pin one of the first two.

::warning
The request-origin fallback reads `X-Forwarded-Host` and `X-Forwarded-Proto`, because [`metaTrustForwardedHost`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#metatrustforwardedhost) and `metaTrustForwardedProto` default to `true`. That is only safe behind a proxy that overwrites those headers; otherwise a client can choose the host in your canonical links, and a cache can pass that page on.

If the app is reachable directly, pin `metaBaseUrl`: unlike setting both options to `false`, it also ignores a forged `Host`. See [Behind a proxy or CDN](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment#behind-a-proxy-or-cdn).
::

The fallback is useful for one deployment answering several domains: `https://site-a.com/en/about` and `https://site-b.com/en/about` each get their own origin.

With `baseUrl` on the locales, a known host uses its own `baseUrl`, over `metaBaseUrl` and `site.url`, so canonical and `og:url` stay on that domain and `hreflang` points each locale at its domain. Any other host uses `metaBaseUrl`, else the default locale's `baseUrl`, else `site.url`, so a spoofed `Host` cannot reach your tags. If none of those is set, the request-origin fallback stays, and the build warns. See [Layers and domains](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/layers#multiple-domains).

## Leave locales or pages out

```ts
i18n: {
  locales: [
    { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
    { code: 'ru', iso: 'ru-RU', seo: false }, // routable, but not in hreflang / og:locale:alternate
    { code: 'fr', iso: 'fr-FR', disabled: true }, // no routes, no switching, no tags
  ],
}
```

If the default locale has `seo: false`, no `x-default` is written. To turn the tags off for one page, use `disableMeta` in [Page config](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/per-component-translations#turn-off-seo-tags), or [`routeDisableMeta`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#routedisablemeta) in the config.

## Override tags on one page

For CMS content where only some translations exist, or URLs come from an API, replace the generated tags with [`useI18nHead`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/composables/useI18nHead):

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const { data: article } = await useFetch('/api/articles/hello')
// article.value.urls = { en: 'https://example.com/blog/hello', de: 'https://example.com/de/artikel/hallo' }

useI18nHead(() => ({
  meta: [{ property: 'og:title', content: article.value?.title ?? '' }],
  replace: {
    hreflang: Object.entries(article.value?.urls ?? {}).map(([locale, href]) => ({ rel: 'alternate', hreflang: locale, href })),
    ogAlternates: Object.keys(article.value?.urls ?? {}),
  },
}))
</script>
```

`replace` can also set or remove `canonical`, `xDefault`, `ogLocale` and `ogUrl`; `disable` drops whole groups (`'hreflang'`, `'x-default'`, `'canonical'`, `'og'`, `'og-alternates'`, `'html'`). Pass a getter so values recompute after a locale switch. For per-locale slugs, set `$setI18nRouteParams` first ([Localized paths](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-locale-routes#per-locale-slugs)) and the generated alternates already use them.

## Trailing slash

`$localePath`, `$switchLocalePath`, the route object of `$switchLocaleRoute`, `<i18n-link>`, `<i18n-switcher>`, locale redirects and the SEO URLs follow one slash rule: `experimental.defaults.nuxtLink.trailingSlash` by default, or [`trailingSlash`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options) in the i18n config when i18n paths should differ.

## Nuxt SEO

[`@nuxtjs/seo`](https://nuxtseo.com/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} (sitemap, robots, schema.org) works with this module through `nuxt-site-config` 4+. List `nuxt-i18n-micro` first so site config can read the locales, and set `site.url` once — it also feeds the tags above.

```ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro', '@nuxtjs/seo'],
  site: { url: 'https://example.com', name: 'My Site' },
  i18n: {
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE' },
    ],
  },
})
```

A translated site name and description come from the `nuxtSiteConfig.name` / `nuxtSiteConfig.description` keys in your locale files. The error `Plugin nuxt-seo:defaults depends on nuxt-site-config:i18n but they are not registered` means `@nuxtjs/seo` is older than 3; upgrade it ([#133](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/issues/133){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}).

# Server routes and API

Server handlers in `server/api/` and `server/routes/` can translate strings and read the request's locale with two auto-imported helpers. Use them for API responses, emails, feeds or anything rendered outside a Vue page. They read the same translation files as your pages and detect the locale from the request.

## Translate in a handler

```ts
// server/api/greeting.get.ts
export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const t = await useTranslationServerMiddleware(event)
  return { message: t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) }
})
```

```bash
curl 'http://localhost:3000/api/greeting?locale=de'
# {"message":"Hallo, Ada!"}
```

`useTranslationServerMiddleware(event, defaultLocale?, locale?)` is async and returns `t(key, params?, defaultValue?)`. `t` returns the string, interpolates `{name}` params, and returns a non-empty `defaultValue`, otherwise the key, when the key is missing.

`t` also carries the page's plural, format and lookup helpers, with the same rules (the build's `plural`, `numberFormats`, `datetimeFormats`, `timeZone`, each locale's `iso`):

```ts
const t = await useTranslationServerMiddleware(event)
t.tc('apples', 5) // '5 apples', as $tc
t.tn(1234.5, 'currency') // a named number format, as $tn
t.td(new Date(), 'short') // a named date format, as $td
t.tdr(Date.now() - 86_400_000) // '1 day ago', as $tdr
t.has('apples') // true when the locale defines the key, as $has
```

`t` sees the `index` chunk only: the root files (`locales/<locale>.json`) plus `locales/pages/index/` when it exists (root files only with `disablePageLocales`). Keys of other pages are not loaded. For those, load the chunk yourself:

```ts
const { data } = await loadTranslationsFromServer('de', 'about') // Translations object of the about page
```

## Read the request locale

```ts
// server/api/locale.get.ts
export default defineEventHandler((event) => {
  const { current, isDefault, locale } = useLocaleServerMiddleware(event)
  return { current, isDefault, dir: locale?.dir ?? 'ltr' }
})
```

`useLocaleServerMiddleware(event, defaultLocale?, locale?)` is synchronous and returns:

```ts
interface LocaleInfo {
  current: string // detected locale code
  default: string // defaultLocale, runtime overrides included (fixed at build under prefix_except_default / prefix_and_default)
  fallback: string // fallbackLocale, else the default
  available: string[] // enabled locale codes
  locale: Locale | null // the config entry of `current`
  isDefault: boolean
  isFallback: boolean
}
```

## How the locale is chosen

Both helpers use the same order on every server route, `/api` or not:

1. `?locale=` query (first value when repeated);
2. a `[locale]` route param, or a locale prefix in the path (`/de/...`);
3. the locale cookie, when [`localeCookie`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#localecookie) is set (`hash-locale` under `hashMode`);
4. `Accept-Language`, when `autoDetectLanguage` is on (q-values respected);
5. `defaultLocale`.

Invalid and disabled codes are skipped at every step. This is the API order; a page render ignores `?locale=` under the prefix strategies. Both orders are compared on [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection).

## Force a locale

Pass the third argument to skip detection, for example in a job that sends mail in the user's language:

```ts
export default defineEventHandler(async (event) => {
  const user = await getUser(event) // your code
  const t = await useTranslationServerMiddleware(event, undefined, user.locale)
  return sendMail(user.email, t('mail.welcome.subject'))
})
```

The second argument replaces `defaultLocale` for this call's detection, so it has no effect when a locale is forced. Dictionaries are cached per request and per locale, and across requests in the server's translation cache, so calling a helper several times is cheap.

## Server components

A server component (`.server.vue`, `<NuxtIsland>`) renders from its own URL, `/__nuxt_island/...`, so it does not see the page's URL, and Nuxt passes it only its props. Pass the locale as a `locale` prop. It then renders in that locale, and a switch fetches it again, since the props are part of the island's URL and cache key. The name is reserved: any enabled locale code in a prop called `locale` sets the render's locale, so give a prop that means something else, such as a number format, another name:

```vue
<!-- components/Greeting.server.vue -->
<template><p>{{ $t('greeting') }}</p></template>
<script setup lang="ts">
defineProps<{ locale?: string }>()
</script>
```

```vue
<template>
  <Greeting :locale="$getLocale()" />
  <NuxtIsland name="Greeting" :props="{ locale: $getLocale() }" />
</template>
```

Without the prop it renders in the locale of the cookie, else the default locale, whatever the URL says, and it does not follow a switch. Its `$t` sees the `index` chunk: the root files plus `locales/pages/index/`.

# Storybook

Storybook for Nuxt (`@nuxtjs/storybook`) runs your components with the Nuxt app, but without the Nitro server that normally serves translation payloads. To make `$t` work in stories, write the payloads Storybook would fetch into a static folder before it starts. A complete project is in [s00d/nuxtjs-storybook-i18n-micro](https://github.com/s00d/nuxtjs-storybook-i18n-micro){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## Nuxt config

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro', '@nuxtjs/storybook'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US', displayName: 'English' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE', displayName: 'Deutsch' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
  },
})
```

## Write the payloads

The browser loads `/_locales/<page>/<locale>/data.json`. Stories have no page route, so they load the `index` payload. Build one per locale that holds every page's keys plus the root keys:

```ts
// .storybook/main.ts
import fs from 'node:fs'
import path from 'node:path'
import type { StorybookConfig } from '@storybook-vue/nuxt'
import { deepMergeTranslationsRecursive } from '@i18n-micro/utils/deep-merge'

type Tree = Record<string, unknown>

const localesDir = path.join(__dirname, '../locales')
const outDir = path.join(__dirname, '../storybook_locales/_locales/index')

const readJson = (file: string): Tree => JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf-8'))

/** Every `<locale>.json` below `dir`, deep-merged. */
function collect(dir: string, locale: string): Tree {
  if (!fs.existsSync(dir)) return {}
  return fs.readdirSync(dir, { withFileTypes: true }).reduce<Tree>((acc, entry) => {
    const full = path.join(dir, entry.name)
    if (entry.isDirectory()) return deepMergeTranslationsRecursive(acc, collect(full, locale))
    return entry.name === `${locale}.json` ? deepMergeTranslationsRecursive(acc, readJson(full)) : acc
  }, {})
}

for (const file of fs.readdirSync(localesDir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.json'))) {
  const locale = path.basename(file, '.json')
  // root keys first, page keys win (as in the module's build)
  const merged = deepMergeTranslationsRecursive(readJson(path.join(localesDir, file)), collect(path.join(localesDir, 'pages'), locale))
  fs.mkdirSync(path.join(outDir, locale), { recursive: true })
  fs.writeFileSync(path.join(outDir, locale, 'data.json'), JSON.stringify(merged))
}

const config: StorybookConfig = {
  stories: ['../components/**/*.stories.@(ts|tsx|mdx)'],
  staticDirs: ['../storybook_locales'], // serves /_locales/index/<locale>/data.json
  framework: { name: '@storybook-vue/nuxt', options: {} },
}

export default config
```

`deepMergeTranslationsRecursive` comes from `@i18n-micro/utils` (add it to your dev dependencies); it merges nested keys at any depth, like the module's own build. Add `storybook_locales/` to `.gitignore`.

## Related

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Testing your app" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/testing"}

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Translation files" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations"}

  :::card
  ---

  target: _blank
  title: "@nuxtjs/storybook"
  to: https://storybook.nuxtjs.org/getting-started/setup

# Routing strategies

The `strategy` option decides whether a locale appears in the URL and for which locales. Pick it once, before you publish URLs: changing it later changes every link. The module then generates the localized routes at build time, and `$localePath`, `<i18n-link>` and the switcher read them.

## The four strategies

![The /about page in en (default) and de under each strategy; the same URLs are listed in the text below](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/diagrams/strategies.svg)

**Type** `Strategies` · **Default** `'prefix_except_default'`

URL routing strategy for locale prefixes.

- `'no_prefix'` — no locale in URL; locale stored in cookie.
- `'prefix_except_default'` — prefix all locales except the default.
- `'prefix'` — always prefix, including the default locale.
- `'prefix_and_default'` — like `prefix`, but the default locale is also accessible without prefix.

URLs for an `about` page with `defaultLocale: 'en'` and locales `en`, `de`:

| Strategy                          | English                  | German      | Not served                           |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `prefix_except_default` (default) | `/about`                 | `/de/about` | `/en` and `/en/about` are a 404      |
| `prefix`                          | `/en/about`              | `/de/about` | `/about` redirects to a prefixed URL |
| `prefix_and_default`              | `/about` and `/en/about` | `/de/about` | —                                    |
| `no_prefix`                       | `/about`                 | `/about`    | the locale is not in the URL         |

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    strategy: 'prefix',
  },
})
```

The strategy is fixed at build: a runtime override of it is ignored with a warning ([Runtime overrides](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/runtime-overrides)).

## Which one to choose

- **`prefix_except_default`**: most sites. Existing unprefixed URLs keep working for the default language.
- **`prefix`**: every language is equal; `/` always leads to a prefixed home.
- **`prefix_and_default`**: you need `/en/...` and the unprefixed URLs both to work, for example while moving from one to the other. Unprefixed URLs are never redirected.
- **`no_prefix`**: apps behind a login, or one URL per page for every language. The locale comes from a cookie or `?locale=`. Search engines see one language per URL, so no `hreflang` alternates are emitted.

How the locale is picked for a URL, and when a visitor is redirected, is on [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection).

## Generated routes

At build time every page gets the route records its strategy needs. Each record carries `meta.i18n = { name, locales }`: the page it shows and the locales it serves. Links, switches and redirects are all answered from those records, so a URL the module hands out is always one the router serves.

Locales that share the page's path share one record, `/:locale(de|fr)/about`. A locale with its own path gets its own record, named `localized-<page>-<locale>`:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts: German has its own path for the about page
i18n: {
  globalLocaleRoutes: { about: { de: '/ueber-uns' } },
}
// prefix_except_default, locales en (default), de, fr:
// about                 /about
// localized-about       /:locale(fr)/about
// localized-about-de    /:locale(de)/ueber-uns
```

Custom paths, per-page locale lists and excluding a page from localization are on [Localized paths](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-locale-routes) and [Page config](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/per-component-translations). The `localized-` prefix is [`localizedRouteNamePrefix`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#localizedroutenameprefix).

::warning
**Route names are generated** — Do not hard-code `localized-…` names in `router.push({ name })`. Pass the page's own name to `$localeRoute` or `<i18n-link>`; they pick the right record.
::

## Linking to a page in a locale

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
const { localePath, localeRoute, switchLocalePath } = useI18n()

localePath({ name: 'about' }) // '/de/ueber-uns' while the page is German
localePath({ name: 'about' }, 'en') // '/about'
localePath('/about', 'de') // '/de/ueber-uns': a path is read as the page it shows
localeRoute({ name: 'products-id', params: { id: '42' } }, 'de') // resolved route: name, params, fullPath
switchLocalePath('fr') // the current page in French
</script>

<template>
  <i18n-link :to="{ name: 'about' }">{{ $t('nav.about') }}</i18n-link>
  <NuxtLink :to="$switchLocalePath('de')">Deutsch</NuxtLink>
</template>
```

- Named routes and paths both work. A path is matched against the generated routes, so any locale's form of it is accepted.
- A locale that does not serve the page (see `locales` in [Page config](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/per-component-translations)) links to that locale's home instead of a missing page.
- Per-locale params (a translated slug) go through `$setI18nRouteParams`, see [Localized paths](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/custom-locale-routes).

Signatures are in [Methods](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/methods).

## `no_prefix` details

- [`localeCookie`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#localecookie) defaults to `'user-locale'` under `no_prefix`, so the choice survives a reload.
- `$switchLocale('de')` loads the German dictionary and replaces the current history entry; the URL does not change.
- Custom per-locale paths still work: with `globalLocaleRoutes: { about: { de: '/ueber-uns' } }`, German readers get `/ueber-uns`. That URL always renders German, whatever the visitor prefers, and a page restricted to some locales renders in one of them. A path several locales share (`en` and `de` both on `/page/:id`) renders the preference when it is one of them. The preference itself stays: the next page returns to it.
- [`noPrefixRedirect: true`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#noprefixredirect) redirects the original path of a page with a custom path in the default locale: to the custom path of the visitor's locale, the default locale's otherwise (`/about` → `/about-us` when `en` has `/about-us`, → `/ueber-uns` with cookie `de`). A locale with no custom path of its own stays on the original path and renders there. Pages with params are not redirected.

## Apps without `pages/`

With `pages: false` there are no page routes to localize. Use root translation files only (`disablePageLocales: true`); detection, the cookie and `$switchLocale` still work. The `pages-false` variant of `test/fixtures/basic` in the repository is a working setup.

:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Excluding paths" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/excluding-static-files"}

# Testing your app

Components that call `useI18n()` need an i18n instance in unit tests. `@i18n-micro/test-utils` gives you a fake `useI18n()` with real translation, plural and formatting logic, so you can mount a component with your own dictionaries and no Nuxt server. For routing and redirects, run the real module end to end with `@nuxt/test-utils`.

This page is about testing your application. How this repository tests the module itself is on [Testing the module](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/contributing/testing).

## Install

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add -D @i18n-micro/test-utils @nuxt/test-utils vitest @vue/test-utils happy-dom
```

```bash [npm]
npm install -D @i18n-micro/test-utils @nuxt/test-utils vitest @vue/test-utils happy-dom
```
::

## Mock useI18n

```ts
// tests/unit-setup.ts
import { setupNuxtI18nMock } from '@i18n-micro/test-utils'
import { mockNuxtImport } from '@nuxt/test-utils/runtime'
import { beforeEach, vi } from 'vitest'

export const { i18n, useI18n, setTranslationsFromJson } = setupNuxtI18nMock({
  spy: vi.fn, // every method becomes a vi.fn, so you can assert calls
  beforeEach, // reset state and reseed `translations` before each test
  translations: { welcome: 'Welcome' },
})

mockNuxtImport('useI18n', () => useI18n)
```

```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineVitestConfig } from '@nuxt/test-utils/config'

export default defineVitestConfig({
  test: {
    environment: 'nuxt',
    setupFiles: ['./tests/unit-setup.ts'],
  },
})
```

Keep `mockNuxtImport` in the setup file: `@nuxt/test-utils` has to transform it. `setupNuxtI18nMock` uses a private translation cache, so parallel test files do not share state.

## Write a test

```vue
<!-- components/Greeting.vue -->
<script setup lang="ts">
const { $t } = useI18n()
</script>

<template>
  <p>{{ $t('welcome') }}</p>
</template>
```

```ts
// tests/greeting.spec.ts
import { mountSuspended } from '@nuxt/test-utils/runtime'
import { expect, it } from 'vitest'
import Greeting from '~/components/Greeting.vue'
import de from '~/locales/de.json'
import { i18n, setTranslationsFromJson } from './unit-setup'

it('renders the German greeting', async () => {
  await setTranslationsFromJson('de', de)
  i18n.setLocale('de')

  const wrapper = await mountSuspended(Greeting)
  expect(wrapper.text()).toBe('Willkommen') // de.json: { "welcome": "Willkommen" }
})
```

The fake exposes the same methods as the real `useI18n()` (`$t`, `$tc`, `$tn`, `$td`, `$has`, `$localePath`, …, with and without `$`) plus setters for tests: `setLocale`, `setLocales`, `setDefaultLocale`, `setRouteName`, `setTranslationsFromJson`, `loadPageTranslations`, `mergeTranslations`, `setMissingHandler`.

`$localePath` and `$switchLocalePath` are stubs that prefix the path according to the `strategy` option (no real router). Test real links and redirects end to end.

## Lower-level helpers

| Helper                                    | Use it for                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createIsolatedFakeI18n(options)`         | An isolated fake without the Nuxt `useI18n` wiring, e.g. for plain `@vue/test-utils` `mount` with `global.mocks`. |
| `createFakeI18n(options)`                 | A fake on the shared module cache (call `resetI18n()` in `beforeEach`), or isolated with `isolated: true`.        |
| `createI18nTestContext(options)`          | The context behind both, when you need several fakes.                                                             |
| `t`, `tc`, `ts`, `tn`, `td`, `tdr`, `has` | Direct calls on the shared context, for testing plain functions.                                                  |

The mock is a `BaseI18n`: `t`, `tc`, `tn`, `td`, `tdr` and `has` are the real ones, on real dictionaries, so a test sees what the app shows.

The factory helpers above accept `locale`, `defaultLocale`, `locales`, `routeName`, `strategy`, `translations` and `messages` (dictionaries per locale). A complete example project lives in [`packages/test-utils/example`](https://github.com/s00d/nuxt-i18n-micro/tree/main/packages/test-utils/example){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## End-to-end tests

Routing, redirects, SEO tags and payload loading need the real module. Start your app with `@nuxt/test-utils/e2e`:

```ts
// tests/e2e/locales.test.ts
import { $fetch, fetch, setup } from '@nuxt/test-utils/e2e'
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'

describe('locales', async () => {
  await setup({ server: true })

  it('serves the German page', async () => {
    expect(await $fetch('/de')).toContain('lang="de-DE"')
  })

  it('redirects / for a German browser', async () => {
    const res = await fetch('/', { headers: { 'accept-language': 'de' }, redirect: 'manual' })
    expect(res.headers.get('location')).toBe('/de')
  })
})
```

The second test assumes `prefix` (or `prefix_except_default` with another default locale); see [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/locale-detection) for when `/` redirects.

# Translation files

Translations are plain JSON files: one root file per locale for shared keys, and one file per page and locale for that page's keys. Read this when you add pages, share keys between them or set up fallbacks. You learn which file a key must go in, what a page can see, and when each file is loaded.

## Layout

```text
locales/
├── en.json                 # root: menus, footer, buttons
├── de.json
└── pages/
    ├── index/              # pages/index.vue
    │   ├── en.json
    │   └── de.json
    ├── about/              # pages/about.vue
    │   ├── en.json
    │   └── de.json
    └── products-id/        # pages/products/[id].vue
        ├── en.json
        └── de.json
```

- The folder under `locales/pages/` is the Nuxt **route name** of the page: `pages/products/[id].vue` is `products-id`, `pages/blog/[slug]/comments.vue` is `blog-slug-comments`.
- Keys can nest to any depth; `$t('auth.form.login')` reads `{ "auth": { "form": { "login": … } } }`.
- `translationDir` moves the folder (`'locales'` by default, relative to the project root, also under the Nuxt 4 `app/` layout).
- Missing files are created as `{}` when Nuxt resolves the pages, unless [`disableWatcher`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#disablewatcher) is set.

## What a page sees

![Lookup order for a key on /about in de: pages/about/de.json, de.json, pages/about/en.json, en.json. They merge into one about/de/data.json that $t reads](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/diagrams/page-dictionary.svg)

A page's dictionary is its root file merged with its page file, deeply (every level). The page file wins on a clash:

```json
// locales/en.json
{ "title": "My shop", "nav": { "home": "Home", "cart": "Cart" } }
```

```json
// locales/pages/about/en.json
{ "title": "About us", "nav": { "cart": "Basket" } }
```

```ts
// on /about
t('title') // 'About us'
t('nav.home') // 'Home'   (root)
t('nav.cart') // 'Basket' (page wins)
// on any other page
t('title') // 'My shop'
```

A page without its own folder gets the root dictionary alone. Keys of other pages are not visible.

### Fallback locales

A key missing in the active locale is taken from its fallback locale before the key itself is shown:

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE' },
      { code: 'de-at', iso: 'de-AT', fallbackLocale: 'de' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    fallbackLocale: 'en', // global, for every locale
  },
})
```

- A locale's own `fallbackLocale` is followed to its end: `de-at` → `de` → `en`.
- The global `fallbackLocale` is the weakest layer, under every chain.
- Each locale in the chain adds its root file, then its page file, from the weakest fallback up to the active locale. So the active locale's root file beats a fallback locale's page file.

Without a fallback, a missing key renders as the key (`'nav.home'`) and logs a warning in the browser console in dev ([`missingWarn`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#missingwarn)).

### Parameters

`{name}` takes `params.name`; `{0}`, `{1}` take the items of an array:

```json [locales/en.json]
{ "welcome": "Welcome, {name}!", "pair": "{0} and {1}" }
```

`$t('welcome', { name: 'Ada' })` reads `Welcome, Ada!` and `$t('pair', ['Ann', 'Bob'])` reads `Ann and Bob`. A placeholder with no param stays as written.

### Linked messages

With [`linkedMessages: true`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#linkedmessages) a message can reuse another one, with the vue-i18n syntax:

```json [locales/en.json]
{
  "brand": "Acme",
  "title": "Welcome to @:brand",
  "shout": "@.upper:brand",
  "intro": "@.capitalize:{'nav.home'}.",
  "greet": "Hi @:withName",
  "withName": "{name}!",
  "nav": { "home": "home" }
}
```

`title` reads `Welcome to Acme`, `shout` reads `ACME`, `intro` reads `Home.` and `$t('greet', { name: 'Ada' })` reads `Hi Ada!`.

- `@:key` inserts the text of `key`; `@.upper:`, `@.lower:` and `@.capitalize:` change its case, by the locale's `iso` (so `@.upper:` of `i` is `İ` in Turkish).
- A bare key runs to a space or one of `{ } @ % | ( )`, dots and other punctuation included: `@:nav.home`. A key followed by `.`, `,` or `!` goes in a literal: `@:{'nav.home'}.`.
- Links are resolved when the dictionaries are built (and when a server merges them in `mode: 'source'` or in dev), in the page's whole dictionary: its root keys, its fallback locales. `$t` reads plain text, so this costs nothing at runtime. `{name}` params in a linked text stay, and `$t` interpolates them.
- A link to a missing key, to an object, or in a cycle leaves the whole message as written, and the build warns once. So does an unknown modifier. Dynamic keys (`@:{name}`) and the old `@:(key)` form are not links.
- Messages added at runtime (`$mergeTranslations`, `$setTranslation`, the `i18n:register` hook, inline `$defineI18nRoute` locales) are not resolved.
- It is off by default: `@:` may already be plain text in your messages.

## Sharing and other sources

| Need                                 | Option                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Only root files, no `pages/` folders | [`disablePageLocales: true`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#disablepagelocales)                                                                        |
| Two pages read one page folder       | [`routesLocaleLinks`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#routeslocalelinks): `{ 'about-us': 'about' }`                                                     |
| Shared root files in another folder  | [`additionalTranslationDirs`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#additionaltranslationdirs): `['common']` (the main `translationDir` wins)                 |
| Keys shipped by a Nuxt module        | the module adds its absolute folder to `additionalTranslationDirs`, see [for module authors](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#additionaltranslationdirs) |
| Keys from a Nuxt layer               | Layers' files merge, the project's own files win. See [Layers](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/layers)                                                               |
| Keys added at runtime                | the [`i18n:register`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/events) hook, `$mergeTranslations`, `$setTranslation`                                                            |
| Keys inline in a page component      | `$defineI18nRoute({ locales: { en: { … } } })`, see [Page config](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/per-component-translations)                                        |

## How a page loads its dictionary

![Locale JSON files are built into a payload tree, stored in public/ on Node or in server assets on Edge, read by a server loader, then used by $t on the server and fetched for $t in the browser](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/diagrams/translation-pipeline.svg)

The module builds one payload per page and locale: `/{apiBaseUrl}/{page}/{locale}/data.json` (`/_locales/about/de/data.json` by default).

1. **Server render.** Nitro detects the locale and the page loads its payload from the server loader directly, with no HTTP request. The dictionary is not written into the HTML payload, so pages stay small.
2. **Hydration.** The browser fetches the same payload. The server already emitted a `<link rel="preload">` for it, so the fetch starts with the HTML.
3. **Navigation.** The next page's payload replaces the dictionary. The leaving page's keys still resolve until it is gone (end of the page transition, or `page:finish`), so a fading-out page does not flash raw keys. A chunk that fails to load (network error, 4xx or 5xx, a body that is not an object) leaves the current dictionary in place, and the next navigation loads it again. A failed locale switch is the same: `$switchLocale` resolves `false`, and calling it again, or clicking the switcher again, retries. Under the prefix strategies the URL has already moved by then, so `lang` and `$getLocale()` name the URL's locale while the old texts stay on screen.
4. **Cache.** Loaded payloads are cached on the server and in the browser; [Performance](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/performance) has the size and TTL knobs.

`translationPayloads.mode` decides how payloads are built. `'premerged'` (default) writes every page × locale file at build time. `'source'` keeps the source files and merges per request, which is smaller for large catalogs on Edge targets. Both give the same dictionaries. Where the files end up for each deploy target is on [Deployment](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/deployment).

## Editing in development

`nuxt dev` reads the files live. Saving a translation file refreshes the open page's dictionary in place: no reload, removed keys disappear, and a change to a root file reaches every page. A broken JSON file logs a warning with its path and is treated as empty. Set [`hmr: false`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/module-options#hmr) to refresh by hand instead.
