# Astro

`@i18n-micro/astro` translates Astro pages on the server: a middleware picks the locale from the URL and puts a per-request instance in `Astro.locals`, and `useI18n(Astro)` reads it. Use it in an Astro site that needs locale-prefixed URLs (`/about`, `/fr/about`) and shared JSON dictionaries. You get `.astro` components, a home-page redirect to the visitor's language, `hreflang` tags, and props for [islands](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/astro-islands).

## Install

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @i18n-micro/astro
```

```bash [npm]
npm install @i18n-micro/astro
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @i18n-micro/astro
```
::

Peer dependencies: `astro` `^5.0.0 || ^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0`. Optional, only for [islands](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/astro-islands): `vue` `^3.3.0`, `react` `^16.8.0 || ^17.0.0 || ^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`, `preact` `^10.0.0 || ^11.0.0`, `svelte` `^4.0.0 || ^5.0.0`.

## Setup

Add the integration. It bundles your dictionaries into the server and installs the middleware, so no `src/middleware.ts` is needed:

```ts
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config'
import node from '@astrojs/node'
import { i18nIntegration } from '@i18n-micro/astro'

export default defineConfig({
  output: 'server',
  adapter: node({ mode: 'standalone' }),
  integrations: [
    i18nIntegration({
      locale: 'en',
      fallbackLocale: 'en',
      locales: [
        { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US', displayName: 'English' },
        { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE', displayName: 'Deutsch' },
        { code: 'fr', iso: 'fr-FR', displayName: 'Français' },
      ],
      translationDir: 'src/locales',
    }),
  ],
})
```

The dictionaries become code at build time: the server reads no disk, so it runs on the edge (Cloudflare, Vercel Edge) too. In `astro dev` an edit to a file applies on the next request.

### Integration options

| Option               | Default         | Notes                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `locale`             | required        | Default locale.                                                                                                                                              |
| `fallbackLocale`     | `locale`        |                                                                                                                                                              |
| `locales`            | `[]`            | Full `Locale` objects. A `disabled` one is no URL's locale and no redirect target. `iso` is the tag plurals go by when the code is not one (`ua` → `uk-UA`). |
| `translationDir`     | none            | Folder bundled into the server, relative to the project root.                                                                                                |
| `disablePageLocales` | `false`         | Page files count as root translations.                                                                                                                       |
| `autoDetect`         | `true`          | Home-page redirect, see [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#locale-detection).                                                        |
| `redirectToDefault`  | `false`         | `/` also redirects when nothing prefers another locale.                                                                                                      |
| `localeCookie`       | `'i18n-locale'` | `null` disables the cookie.                                                                                                                                  |
| `missingWarn`        | `false`         |                                                                                                                                                              |
| `middleware`         | `true`          | `false`: write the middleware yourself, see below.                                                                                                           |

The runtime settings are published in `virtual:i18n-micro/config` (`config.base` is Astro's `base`, `config.localeCodes` the enabled codes), the dictionaries in `virtual:i18n-micro/messages`.

### Your own middleware

A plural rule, a missing-key handler and a router adapter cannot cross from the config process to the server bundle. For those, pass `middleware: false` and write `src/middleware.ts`. Astro's `i18n` config is then set for you with `routing: 'manual'`, so `Astro.currentLocale` and `astro:i18n` work. Astro does not allow that setting without a `src/middleware.ts`, so with the integration's own middleware they do not.

```ts
// src/middleware.ts
import { config } from 'virtual:i18n-micro/config'
import { messages } from 'virtual:i18n-micro/messages'
import { createAstroRouterAdapter, createI18n, createI18nMiddleware, localeIsoMap } from '@i18n-micro/astro'

const i18n = createI18n({
  locale: config.defaultLocale,
  fallbackLocale: config.fallbackLocale,
  localeIso: localeIsoMap(config.locales),
  messages: messages.root,
  routeMessages: messages.routes,
  plural: myPluralRule,
})

export const onRequest = createI18nMiddleware({
  i18n,
  defaultLocale: config.defaultLocale,
  locales: config.localeCodes,
  localeObjects: config.locales,
  autoDetect: config.autoDetect,
  redirectToDefault: config.redirectToDefault,
  localeCookie: config.localeCookie,
  base: config.base,
  routingStrategy: createAstroRouterAdapter(config.locales, config.defaultLocale),
})
```

To read the folder at runtime instead, `loadTranslationsFromDir` and `loadTranslationsIntoI18n` are in `@i18n-micro/astro/node` (Node only).

### Middleware options

| Option              | Default                 | Notes                                                                                                                     |
| ------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `i18n`              | required                | Global instance; each request gets `i18n.fork(locale)`, which costs the same however many dictionaries there are.         |
| `defaultLocale`     | required                |                                                                                                                           |
| `locales`           | required                | Locale codes.                                                                                                             |
| `localeObjects`     | `locales` as `{ code }` | Full `Locale` objects for components and SEO.                                                                             |
| `autoDetect`        | `true`                  | Home-page redirect, see [Locale detection](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#locale-detection).                     |
| `redirectToDefault` | `false`                 | `/` also redirects when nothing prefers another locale, to the default locale's home as the routing strategy resolves it. |
| `localeCookie`      | `'i18n-locale'`         | `null` disables the cookie.                                                                                               |
| `routingStrategy`   | prefix except default   | Router adapter. Methods it leaves out come from the default adapter.                                                      |
| `base`              | none                    | Astro's `base`: `config.base`.                                                                                            |

Page files (`src/locales/pages/blog/post/de.json`) are the route `blog-post`: the page path joined with `-`.

## Translate

```astro
---
// src/pages/index.astro
import { useI18n } from '@i18n-micro/astro'
import I18nT from '@i18n-micro/astro/i18n-t'

const { t, tc, locale } = useI18n(Astro)
---

<h1>{t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' })}</h1>
<p>{tc('apples', 3)}</p>
<I18nT keypath="welcome" tag="p" />
<p>{locale}</p>
```

`useI18n(Astro)` returns `locale`, `defaultLocale`, `locales`, `t`, `ts`, `tc`, `tn`, `td`, `tdr`, `has`, `getRoute`, `getRouteName(path?)`, `getLocaleFromPath(path?)`, `switchLocalePath(locale)`, `localizePath(path, locale?)`, `getBasePath(url?)`, `getI18n`, `addTranslations`, `addRouteTranslations`, `mergeTranslations` and `clearCache`. It throws when the middleware did not run. Helpers `getI18n`, `getLocale`, `getDefaultLocale` and `getLocales` read the same `Astro.locals`.

The route name comes from the route without its locale: `/fr/blog/post` → `blog-post`, and every URL of `src/pages/blog/[slug].astro` → `blog-slug`, so one folder `locales/pages/blog-slug/` serves them all. `[...path]` is `path`. Under Astro's `base` the helpers take and return URLs of the site: `switchLocalePath` and `localizePath` include it, `getBasePath` does not, because `Astro.rewrite` takes the path without it.

### Components

Import them from `@i18n-micro/astro/<name>` (or `@i18n-micro/astro/components/<name>.astro`):

| Component       | Props                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `i18n-t`        | `keypath`, `params`, `plural`, `number`, `date`, `relativeDate`, `tag` (`span`, any tag), `html`, `hideIfEmpty`, `defaultValue`; other attributes pass through. With `html` the result of every branch is rendered as HTML and `params` are escaped. There are no slots |
| `i18n-link`     | `href`, `locale` (target locale, default current), `class`; other attributes pass through. External URLs, `#hash` and `?query` stay as written; a route keeps its query, hash and trailing slash                                                                        |
| `i18n-switcher` | `class`, `activeClass` (`'active'`), `customLabels`; renders links to the current page in each enabled locale, with its query                                                                                                                                           |
| `i18n-group`    | none that change output: a `<div>` around its slot, no prefix                                                                                                                                                                                                           |

## Locale-prefixed routes

Keep one page per route in `src/pages/` and add thin rewrite stubs under `src/pages/[locale]/`:

```text
src/pages/
  index.astro
  about.astro
  [locale]/
    index.astro
    about.astro
```

```astro
---
// src/pages/[locale]/about.astro
import { prepareLocaleRewrite } from '@i18n-micro/astro'

const target = prepareLocaleRewrite(Astro)
if (target instanceof Response) return target
return Astro.rewrite(target)
---
```

`prepareLocaleRewrite` returns a `404` response for an unknown `:locale`, otherwise sets the locale on `Astro.locals` and returns the path without the prefix. The middleware keeps a locale already in `locals`, so the rewritten page renders in it. `getLocaleRewritePath(Astro)` returns only the path, when you validate the locale yourself.

## Locale detection

The URL decides the page's locale:

1. A locale prefix (`/fr/about` → `fr`; `/en/about` is `en` too).
2. Otherwise what the router adapter's `getLocaleFromPath` returns, if it is not the default.
3. Otherwise the default locale. `/about` is always the default locale's page, whatever the cookie says.

`autoDetect` is a redirect hint on the home page only:

- A request for `/` whose cookie or `Accept-Language` prefers another locale gets a `302` to that locale's home (`/de`). q-weights are honoured; `de-DE` matches a `de` locale, and `de` matches a `de-DE` one.
- With `redirectToDefault`, `/` always redirects: to the preferred locale's home, else the default locale's.
- The `/` response carries `Vary: Cookie, Accept-Language` (`Accept-Language` only when `localeCookie` is `null`).
- Prerendered pages never redirect.

`detectLocale(pathname, cookies, headers, defaultLocale, locales, localeCookie?, routingStrategy?, autoDetect?)` returns the same preferred locale for your own logic.

The cookie remembers a choice. A page view that comes from a same-origin page of another locale is a visitor switching, whatever link took them there: the HTML response sets the cookie to the new locale, and `/` does not redirect, so a switcher reaches the default locale's home. An endpoint, an image, a 404, a form post and a prefetch change nothing. "Same origin" is what the browser says in `Sec-Fetch-Site`; without that header the `Referer`'s host is compared with the request's, so behind a proxy set Astro's `security.allowedDomains`.

A [server island](https://docs.astro.build/en/guides/server-islands/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} or an action has no locale in its URL. It is rendered for the page that asked, read from the `Referer`, whose path is all that counts, so a proxy in front of the server changes nothing, and it never redirects. Its response carries `Vary: Referer`. Without a `Referer` (a `no-referrer` policy) it is in the default locale, and on a dynamic page its route comes from the URL, so page dictionaries do not reach it.

## Router adapter

`createAstroRouterAdapter(locales, defaultLocale)` prefixes every locale except the default. An Astro adapter needs only `getCurrentPath`; the other members are optional and fall back to the default adapter: `getRouteName(path, locales, routePattern?)`, `getLocaleFromPath`, `switchLocalePath`, `localizePath`, `removeLocaleFromPath`, `resolvePath` (home redirect target), `push`, `replace`, `getRoute`. Write your own for subdomain or suffix URLs and pass it to `createI18nMiddleware`.

## SEO

```astro
---
// src/layouts/Layout.astro
import { useLocaleHead } from '@i18n-micro/astro'

const head = useLocaleHead(Astro, { baseUrl: 'https://example.com' })
---

<html lang={head.htmlAttrs.lang} dir={head.htmlAttrs.dir}>
  <head>
    {head.link.map((l) => <link rel={l.rel} href={l.href} hreflang={l.hreflang} />)}
    {head.meta.map((m) => <meta property={m.property} content={m.content} />)}
  </head>
  <body><slot /></body>
</html>
```

It returns `htmlAttrs` (`lang` from `iso`, `dir`), a canonical link (path without query), `hreflang` alternates for every enabled locale with `seo !== false` plus `x-default`, `og:locale`, `og:locale:alternate` and `og:url`. Options: `baseUrl` (`site` from the Astro config, else root-relative URLs), `addDirAttribute` (`true`), `addSeoAttributes` (`true`), `hreflangBaseLanguage` (`false`).

# DevTools UI

`@i18n-micro/devtools-ui` is the translation editor from the Nuxt DevTools tab, packaged as a web component with a Vite plugin. Add it to a Vue, React, Preact, Solid or Astro project to browse and edit the JSON files in your translation folder from the browser during development. Nuxt apps already have it in [Nuxt DevTools](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/devtools).

![The DevTools UI: a file tree and an editor with the default-locale text next to each key](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/devtools/02-translations-editor-dark.webp){height="852" width="1392"}

## Install

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add -D @i18n-micro/devtools-ui
```

```bash [npm]
npm install -D @i18n-micro/devtools-ui
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add -D @i18n-micro/devtools-ui
```
::

No peer dependencies.

## Setup

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import { i18nDevToolsPlugin } from '@i18n-micro/devtools-ui/vite'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [i18nDevToolsPlugin({ translationDir: 'src/locales' })],
})
```

| Option           | Default                               | Notes                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `translationDir` | `'src/locales'`                       | Folder with the JSON files, relative to the Vite root.                                                           |
| `base`           | `'/__i18n_api'`                       | Base path of the API endpoints.                                                                                  |
| `injectButton`   | `true`                                | Add a floating button to pages served through Vite's `index.html` transform. Astro has no such pages: see below. |
| `defaultLocale`  | first locale file in `translationDir` | Reported by `/config`.                                                                                           |
| `fallbackLocale` | `defaultLocale`                       | Reported by `/config`.                                                                                           |

The plugin runs on the dev server only (`apply: 'serve'`); a production build contains nothing from it. The button opens `/__i18n_devtools.html`, which reads and saves files through the plugin's endpoints:

| Endpoint                  | Does                                                                                                                             |
| ------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET <base>/translations` | every dictionary under `translationDir`, by relative path                                                                        |
| `POST <base>/save`        | body `{ file, content }`; overwrites an existing `.json` inside `translationDir`, 403 for anything else. It never creates a file |
| `GET <base>/config`       | `{ defaultLocale, fallbackLocale, locales, translationDir }`; `locales` come from the root files in `translationDir`             |

The endpoints answer the devtools page only: a request from another origin or host is a `403`, and `/save` takes `application/json` only (`415`). The page hears about file changes over Vite's HMR socket.

In Astro, add the integration instead of the plugin. It adds an app to the dev toolbar:

```ts
// astro.config.mjs
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config'
import { i18nDevToolsIntegration } from '@i18n-micro/devtools-ui/vite'

export default defineConfig({
  integrations: [i18nDevToolsIntegration({ translationDir: 'src/locales' })],
})
```

Saving only writes the file. An app that imports the JSON through Vite gets it through HMR; for edits applied to the running instance directly, use a bridge.

## Bridge to a live instance

To embed the editor in your own page and have edits applied to the running instance at once, create a bridge from an adapter and pass it to the `<i18n-devtools-ui>` element:

```ts
import { createBridge, register } from '@i18n-micro/devtools-ui'
import { i18n, locales } from './i18n' // a runtime, React, Preact or Solid instance

register() // defines <i18n-devtools-ui> once

const bridge = createBridge({
  adapter: {
    getRouteCache: () => Object.fromEntries(i18n.storage.translations),
    addTranslations: (locale, content, merge) => i18n.addTranslations(locale, content, merge),
    addRouteTranslations: (locale, route, content, merge) => i18n.addRouteTranslations(locale, route, content, merge),
    subscribe: (cb) => i18n.subscribe(cb),
    getCurrentLocale: () => i18n.locale,
  },
  locales,
  defaultLocale: 'en',
  translationDir: 'src/locales',
})

const el = document.createElement('i18n-devtools-ui') as HTMLElement & { bridge: typeof bridge }
el.bridge = bridge
document.body.append(el)
```

`getRouteCache` must return the dictionaries keyed `locale:route` (`en:index`, `en:blog-post`), which is what `i18n.storage.translations` holds. For a Vue instance use `i18n.global.getRouteCache()` and `i18n.global.subscribeToChanges(cb)`.

`saveTranslation` updates the instance first, then POSTs to `<base>/save`. When there is no endpoint (a static preview build) or the dev server cannot be reached, the edit is kept in `localStorage`; any other save error restores the previous dictionary and throws.

## API

| Export                                                                | Entry                                             |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| `i18nDevToolsPlugin(options)`, `i18nDevToolsIntegration(options)`     | `@i18n-micro/devtools-ui/vite`                    |
| `register()`, `I18nDevToolsElement`                                   | `@i18n-micro/devtools-ui`                         |
| `createBridge(options)`, types `BridgeAdapter`, `CreateBridgeOptions` | `@i18n-micro/devtools-ui` (also `/bridge/create`) |
| type `I18nDevToolsBridge`                                             | `@i18n-micro/devtools-ui` (also `/bridge`)        |
| `createRpcClient`, `setupRpcHost`                                     | `@i18n-micro/devtools-ui`                         |

Full signatures: [package reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages/devtools-ui).

# Frameworks

The `@i18n-micro/*` packages bring the translation core of Nuxt I18n Micro to Vue, React, Preact, Solid, Astro, VitePress and plain JavaScript. Use them when your app is not a Nuxt app, or when a script or server outside Nuxt needs the same translation files. Every package shares one instance model, one router adapter contract and the same four components, described once on this page.

## Packages

| Stack                                                                                                                                                            | Package                       | Router entry               |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| [Vue 3 SPA](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/vue-package)                                                                                     | `@i18n-micro/vue`             | `@i18n-micro/vue/router`   |
| [React](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/react-package)                                                                                       | `@i18n-micro/react`           | `@i18n-micro/react/router` |
| [Preact](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/react-package#preact)                                                                               | `@i18n-micro/preact`          | —                          |
| [SolidJS](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/solid-package)                                                                                     | `@i18n-micro/solid`           | `@i18n-micro/solid/router` |
| [Astro](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/astro-package): SSR and [islands](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/astro-islands) | `@i18n-micro/astro`           | —                          |
| [VitePress](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/vitepress-package)                                                                               | `@i18n-micro/vitepress`       | —                          |
| [Browser or edge](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/runtime-package), no framework                                                             | `@i18n-micro/runtime`         | —                          |
| [Node.js](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/nodejs-package) server, CLI                                                                        | `@i18n-micro/node`            | —                          |
| [Typed keys](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/types-generator), Vite or Nuxt                                                                  | `@i18n-micro/types-generator` | —                          |
| [Translation editor](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/devtools-ui-package) in dev                                                             | `@i18n-micro/devtools-ui`     | —                          |

The router entry is a separate import, so an app without a router never bundles one.

`@i18n-micro/core`, `@i18n-micro/types` and `@i18n-micro/utils` are installed with these packages; you rarely import them directly. Signatures of every export are on the generated [package reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages).

Each package has a playground under `packages/<name>/playground` in the repository.

## The instance

`createI18n(options)` returns one instance that holds the dictionaries, the current locale and the current route. The options are the same in every package:

| Option            | Type                                                       | Default         | Notes                                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`          | `string`                                                   | required        | Active locale.                                                                                                             |
| `fallbackLocale`  | `string`                                                   | `locale`        | Looked up when a key is missing in `locale`.                                                                               |
| `messages`        | `Record<locale, Translations>`                             | `{}`            | Root dictionaries (`'index'` route).                                                                                       |
| `routeMessages`   | `Record<route, Record<locale, Translations>>`              | `{}`            | Route dictionaries. Runtime, React, Preact, Node and VitePress only.                                                       |
| `plural`          | `PluralFunc`                                               | `defaultPlural` | Custom plural rule.                                                                                                        |
| `missingWarn`     | `boolean`                                                  | `true`          | Dev-only `console.warn` in the browser for a missing key.                                                                  |
| `missingHandler`  | `(locale, key, routeName) => void`                         | —               | Called instead of the warning.                                                                                             |
| `numberFormats`   | `Record<locale, Record<name, Intl.NumberFormatOptions>>`   | —               | Named formats: `tn(9.5, 'currency')`.                                                                                      |
| `datetimeFormats` | `Record<locale, Record<name, Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions>>` | —               | Named formats: `td(date, 'short')`.                                                                                        |
| `timeZone`        | `string`                                                   | runtime's zone  | IANA zone for `td` dates; it does not affect `tdr`. Set it so server and browser render one date.                          |
| `now`             | `() => number`                                             | `Date.now`      | The clock of `tdr`. Hand hydration the server's time so both render one text.                                              |
| `localeIso`       | `Record<code, string>`                                     | —               | BCP 47 tag used for plural rules (`ua` → `uk-UA`). React, Preact and Solid take it from `iso` in the provider's `locales`. |

The dictionaries live in `i18n.storage.translations`, a `Map` keyed `locale:route` (`en:index`, `en:about`).

A key is looked up in the current route's dictionary, then in the root dictionary, first for `locale`, then for `fallbackLocale`. A missing key returns the key itself (or the `defaultValue` you pass).

```ts
i18n.addTranslations('en', { nav: { home: 'Home' } }) // root, deep-merged
i18n.addRouteTranslations('en', 'about', { title: 'About us' }) // route chunk
i18n.addTranslations('en', { nav: { home: 'Start' } }, false) // replace instead of merge
i18n.setRoute('about')
i18n.t('title') // 'About us'
i18n.t('nav.home') // 'Start' (root key, still visible on the route)
```

### Translate and format

| Method                                       | Returns                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `t(key, params?, defaultValue?, routeName?)` | The value (string, number, object) with `{param}` interpolated.                                    |
| `ts(...)`                                    | Same as `t`, as a string.                                                                          |
| `tc(key, count | params, defaultValue?)`     | Plural form.                                                                                       |
| `tn(value, options | name)`                  | `Intl.NumberFormat` in the active locale.                                                          |
| `td(value, options | name)`                  | `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.                                                                             |
| `tdr(value, options?)`                       | Relative time (`3 days ago`).                                                                      |
| `has(key, routeName?)`                       | `true` when the active locale has the key (route or root dictionary; the fallback is not checked). |

`defaultPlural` splits the value on `|` and picks the form at index `count`, clamped to the last one; a negative, fractional or `NaN` count picks the last form.

A custom `plural` receives `(key, count, params, locale, getter)`. Read the value through `getter(key)`; do not split the key:

```ts
import type { PluralFunc } from '@i18n-micro/vue'

const plural: PluralFunc = (key, count, params, _locale, getter) => {
  const value = getter(key)
  if (typeof value !== 'string') return null
  const forms = value.split('|').map((form) => form.trim())
  return (count === 1 ? forms[0] : forms[1] ?? forms[0])!.replace('{count}', String(count))
}
```

## Router adapter

The SPA packages do not depend on a router. A router adapter (`I18nRoutingStrategy`) tells them how to read the current path, navigate and build a localized path. The built-in adapters prefix every locale except `defaultLocale` (`/about`, `/de/about`).

| Member                     | Required | Used by                                                                               |
| -------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `getCurrentPath(): string` | yes      | active link check (by page, query and hash do not count), `switchLocale` (keeps them) |
| `push({ path }): void`     | yes      | `switchLocale`, `<I18nLink>` without `linkComponent`, `<I18nSwitcher>`                |
| `replace({ path }): void`  | yes      | —                                                                                     |
| `resolvePath(to, locale)`  | no       | `localePath`, `localeRoute`, `<I18nLink>`; without it paths are returned as is        |
| `linkComponent`            | no       | `<I18nLink>` renders it (e.g. `RouterLink`) instead of `<a>`                          |
| `getRoute()`               | no       | `{ fullPath, query }` for SEO helpers                                                 |

`push` and `replace` are required in Vue, React, Preact and Solid. Astro has its own, server-side adapter with optional `push`/`replace` (see [Astro](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/astro-package#router-adapter)).

A minimal adapter for any history-based router:

```ts
import type { I18nRoutingStrategy } from '@i18n-micro/react'

const locales = ['en', 'de']
const stripLocale = (path: string) => path.replace(/^\/(en|de)(?=\/|$)/, '') || '/'

export const historyAdapter: I18nRoutingStrategy = {
  getCurrentPath: () => window.location.pathname + window.location.search + window.location.hash,
  push: ({ path }) => window.history.pushState({}, '', path),
  replace: ({ path }) => window.history.replaceState({}, '', path),
  resolvePath: (to, locale) => {
    const path = stripLocale(typeof to === 'string' ? to : to.path || '/')
    return locale === 'en' ? path : `/${locale}${path === '/' ? '' : path}`
  },
}
```

## Components

Vue, React, Preact and Solid ship the same four components. Their props match; React, Preact and Solid pass other props through to the root element.

### `<I18nT>`

| Prop               | Type                     | Notes                                                                                     |
| ------------------ | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `keypath`          | `string`                 | required                                                                                  |
| `params`           | `object`                 | interpolation values                                                                      |
| `plural`           | `number | string`        | renders `tc(keypath, count)`                                                              |
| `number`           | `number | string`        | passes `tn(number)` as `{number}`                                                         |
| `date`             | `Date | string | number` | passes `td(date)` as `{date}`                                                             |
| `relativeDate`     | `Date | string | number` | passes `tdr(relativeDate)` as `{relativeDate}`                                            |
| `tag`              | `string`                 | wrapper element, default `span`                                                           |
| `html`             | `boolean`                | render the translation as HTML; it must be trusted, params are escaped                    |
| `defaultValue`     | `string`                 | stands in for a missing key, and is rendered bare when `hideIfEmpty` hides an empty value |
| `hideIfEmpty`      | `boolean`                | render nothing for an empty translation                                                   |
| `customPluralRule` | `PluralFunc`             | plural rule for this element                                                              |

Only one formatting prop applies, checked in this order: `number`, `date`, `relativeDate`, `plural`.

#### Rich text

A `{placeholder}` can hold an element. In Vue it is a named slot; in React, Preact and Solid the `components` prop gives elements, or functions returning one, by name. Either way it beats a param of the same name, works in every branch, and survives a locale that reorders the placeholders.

```tsx
// { "terms": "I accept the {link} of {company}" }
<I18nT keypath="terms" params={{ company: 'ACME' }} components={{ link: <a href="/terms">terms</a> }} />
```

In Solid pass a function when a placeholder repeats: one node stands in one place. `children` replace the text, as a function they get `{ translation }`, like Vue's default slot. `html` ignores all of these.

### `<I18nLink>`

| Prop          | Type                | Notes                                                                                             |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `to`          | `string | { path }` | localized through the adapter's `resolvePath`                                                     |
| `activeStyle` | style object        | merged over `style` on the current page; React, Preact and Solid also apply it to a section above |
| `localeRoute` | function            | overrides `resolvePath` for this link                                                             |

External URLs (`https://`, `mailto:`, `tel:`) render as `<a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">`; a `target` or `rel` of your own wins. `onClick` always runs. A modified click, another mouse button or a `target` stays with the browser.

### `<I18nSwitcher>`

A dropdown of enabled locales (`disabled: true` locales are hidden) with inline default styles. Its items are links, with `lang`, `hreflang` and `dir` from the locale. By default, clicking one sets the locale and calls the adapter's `push` with the localized current path; a `switchLocale` prop replaces that action. With a `localeRoute` and no router, the browser follows the link. Escape or a click outside closes it.

| Prop                                                                                                                                                                          | Notes                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `locales`, `currentLocale`, `getLocaleName`                                                                                                                                   | override the provided values |
| `switchLocale(code)`                                                                                                                                                          | replaces the built-in switch |
| `localeRoute`                                                                                                                                                                 | replaces `resolvePath`       |
| `customLabels`                                                                                                                                                                | `{ de: 'DE' }`               |
| `customWrapperStyle`, `customButtonStyle`, `customDropdownStyle`, `customItemStyle`, `customLinkStyle`, `customActiveLinkStyle`, `customDisabledLinkStyle`, `customIconStyle` | style overrides              |

### `<I18nGroup>`

A `<div class="i18n-group">` that hands a prefixed `t` to its children. It does **not** prefix `<I18nT>` or `t()` calls inside it; only the `t` it passes down is prefixed.

| Prop         | Notes                      |
| ------------ | -------------------------- |
| `prefix`     | required, e.g. `'profile'` |
| `groupClass` | extra class on the wrapper |

The prefixed `t` comes through a scoped slot in Vue (`v-slot="{ t }"`) and a render-prop child in React, Preact and Solid (`{({ t }) => …}`).

## Typed keys

`t()` accepts any string. To get autocomplete for your keys, generate a declaration with the [types generator](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/integrations/types-generator). Keys are suggested, not enforced, and params are not typed.

## Compared with the Nuxt module

The packages have no file-based routing, no server middleware and no translation loader: you decide when to load JSON (`import`, `fetch`, or `@i18n-micro/node` on the server) and which router adapter to use. Locale detection, SEO meta and route generation are Nuxt features; Astro has its own middleware for detection and `useLocaleHead` for SEO.

# Node.js

`@i18n-micro/node` is the [runtime](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/runtime-package) instance plus a loader that reads a translation folder from disk. Use it in an Express or Fastify server, a CLI, an email or PDF generator, or any script that needs the same JSON files as your Nuxt app. You load the files once and translate per request without sharing mutable state between requests.

## Install

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @i18n-micro/node @i18n-micro/utils
```

```bash [npm]
npm install @i18n-micro/node @i18n-micro/utils
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @i18n-micro/node @i18n-micro/utils
```
::

No peer dependencies; Node.js `>=20`. `@i18n-micro/utils` is only needed for the `Accept-Language` helper below.

## Setup

The loader reads the [Nuxt folder layout](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/translations): `locales/en.json` is a root dictionary, `locales/pages/blog/post/en.json` belongs to the route `blog-post`.

```ts
import { createI18n } from '@i18n-micro/node'

const i18n = createI18n({ locale: 'en', fallbackLocale: 'en', translationDir: './locales' })
await i18n.loadTranslations()

i18n.t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) // 'Hello, Ada!'
i18n.t('title', undefined, undefined, 'blog-post') // from locales/pages/blog/post/en.json
```

Options are the runtime ones (see [the instance](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#the-instance)) plus `translationDir` and `disablePageLocales` (treat `pages/**` files as root dictionaries). `i18n.reload()` clears every dictionary and reads the folder again, for a file watcher in development.

`loadTranslations(dir, disablePageLocales?)` is also exported on its own and returns `{ root, routes }`:

```ts
import { loadTranslations } from '@i18n-micro/node'

const { root, routes } = await loadTranslations('./locales')
// root:   { en: {...}, de: {...} }
// routes: { 'blog-post': { en: {...}, de: {...} } }
```

## Per request

An instance holds one locale and one route. Switching `i18n.locale` on a shared instance inside a request handler races with concurrent requests. `run` gives a request its own:

```ts
const i18n = createI18n({ locale: 'en', fallbackLocale: 'en', translationDir: './locales' })
await i18n.loadTranslations()

// `() => next()`: `run` hands its callback the fork, and Express reads an argument of `next` as an error
app.use((req, res, next) => i18n.run(pickLocale(req), () => next()))

app.get('/', (req, res) => {
  res.send(i18n.t('greeting')) // the request's locale, in everything it awaits
})
```

Inside `run` the shared instance reads and sets the request's locale and route (`AsyncLocalStorage`); the fork starts on the current route, and `i18n.setRoute(...)` inside the callback changes that request's route. The callback also gets the request's fork: dictionaries written to it stay in the request, dictionaries written to the shared instance reach everyone.

Without `AsyncLocalStorage`, `i18n.fork(locale)` returns the same kind of instance to pass around.

`reload()` reads the directory again; the old dictionaries answer until the new ones are in.

## Pick the locale

`detectLocaleFromAcceptLanguage(header, locales)` honours `q` weights and matches `de-DE` to a `de` locale (and `de` to `de-DE`). It returns `null` when nothing matches.

```ts
import express from 'express'
import { detectLocaleFromAcceptLanguage } from '@i18n-micro/utils/accept-language'

const app = express()

app.get('/hello', (req, res) => {
  const locale = detectLocaleFromAcceptLanguage(req.headers['accept-language'], locales) ?? 'en'
  const i18n = byLocale.get(locale)!
  res.json({ message: i18n.t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) })
})
```

For URL prefix, cookie and header together, `resolveLocale({ defaultLocale, validLocales, url, cookie, acceptLanguage, autoDetectLanguage: true })` from `@i18n-micro/utils/resolve-locale` applies the module's precedence: URL, then cookie, then `Accept-Language`, then the default. Invalid values are skipped.

Inside a Nuxt app you do not need this package on the server: use the module's [server-side translations](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/guide/server-side-translations).

## API

| Export                                                                                       | Notes                                                                     |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createI18n(options)`, `I18n`                                                                | runtime instance + `translationDir`, `loadTranslations(dir?)`, `reload()` |
| `loadTranslations(dir, disablePageLocales?)`                                                 | `{ root, routes }`                                                        |
| `loadRootTranslations(dir, disablePageLocales?)`                                             | `root` only                                                               |
| `FormatService`, `interpolate`                                                               | from core                                                                 |
| Types: `I18nOptions`, `LoadedTranslations`, `Translations`, `Locale`, `PluralFunc`, `Params` |                                                                           |

Instance methods are listed on [Runtime](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/runtime-package#api). Full signatures: [package reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages/node).

# React and Preact

`@i18n-micro/react` and `@i18n-micro/preact` wrap the framework-agnostic [runtime](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/runtime-package) in a provider, a `useI18n()` hook and four components. Use them in a React or Preact app that is not built with Nuxt. Both packages have the same API; the [Preact](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#preact) block lists the few differences, and the shared model is in [Frameworks](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/).

## Install

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @i18n-micro/react
```

```bash [npm]
npm install @i18n-micro/react
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @i18n-micro/react
```
::

Peer dependencies: `react` `^18.0.0 || ^19.0.0`; `react-dom` (optional, for rendering); `react-router-dom` `^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0` (optional, only for `@i18n-micro/react/router`). Tested on React 19.3 and 18.3, React Router 7.18 and 6.30.

## Setup

```tsx
// src/main.tsx
import { createRoot } from 'react-dom/client'
import { createI18n, I18nProvider } from '@i18n-micro/react'
import App from './App'
import en from './locales/en.json'

const locales = [
  { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US', displayName: 'English' },
  { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE', displayName: 'Deutsch' },
]

const i18n = createI18n({ locale: 'en', fallbackLocale: 'en', messages: { en } })

createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
  <I18nProvider i18n={i18n} locales={locales} defaultLocale="en">
    <App />
  </I18nProvider>,
)
```

::warning
Create the instance once, at module level or in a `useState` initializer, never in a component body.
::

`<I18nProvider>` takes `i18n`, `locales`, `defaultLocale` and `routingStrategy`:

- An omitted prop keeps the value of an outer provider, the instance included.
- With no instance at all, it builds one from the `createI18n` options next to them, so the props stay plain data: `<I18nProvider locale="de" messages={messages}>`.
- A new `locale` prop builds a new instance with the `messages` of that render. Such an instance lives in the component: if something above it suspends during mount, React throws it away, with whatever was added to it.

All `createI18n` options, including `routeMessages`, are in [the instance](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#the-instance).

## Translate

```tsx
import { useI18n } from '@i18n-micro/react'

export function Greeting() {
  const { t, tc, tn } = useI18n()
  return (
    <>
      <h1>{t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' })}</h1> {/* Hello, Ada! */}
      <p>{tc('apples', 3)}</p> {/* 3 apples */}
      <p>{tn(1234.5)}</p>
    </>
  )
}
```

`useI18n()` returns:

| Group            | Members                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Translate        | `t`, `ts`, `tc`, `tn`, `td`, `tdr`, `has`                                                                                         |
| Locale and route | `locale`, `fallbackLocale`, `currentRoute`, `setLocale`, `setRoute`, `getRoute`, `getLocales`, `defaultLocale()`, `getLocaleName` |
| Routing          | `switchLocale`, `localePath`, `localeRoute`                                                                                       |
| Dictionaries     | `addTranslations`, `addRouteTranslations`, `clearCache`                                                                           |

- The component re-renders when the locale, the route or a readable dictionary changes, and when the provider gets a new `locales` or `routingStrategy` object. A dictionary of a locale that is neither active nor fallback renders nothing.
- `t` and the other translation methods change only with the store, so they are safe in `memo` and effect deps.

`useT` is one string as a value. The component renders only when that string changes, whatever happens to the provider's other props; `<I18nT>` does not depend on them either:

```tsx
const title = useT('page.title')
```

Load more dictionaries at any time:

```tsx
const { addTranslations, addRouteTranslations, setRoute } = useI18n()

useEffect(() => {
  import('./locales/de.json').then((m) => addTranslations('de', m.default))
  addRouteTranslations('en', 'about', { title: 'About us' })
  setRoute('about') // t('title') now reads the 'about' dictionary first
}, [])
```

The instance itself also has `loadFromUrl(url, { locale, routeName })` for JSON over `fetch`.

## Switch locale

```tsx
const { setLocale, switchLocale } = useI18n()

setLocale('de') // only the locale
switchLocale('de') // the locale, then the adapter's push to the localized current path
```

Switching does not load anything; add the locale's dictionary first. A store write is synchronous for React, even inside `startTransition`, so a component that suspends on a missing dictionary would show its fallback. `useLocaleSwitch` loads first and keeps the old UI until the dictionary is in:

```tsx
const [switchTo, pending] = useLocaleSwitch((locale) => i18n.loadFromUrl(`/locales/${locale}.json`, { locale }))

<button disabled={pending} onClick={() => switchTo('de')}>Deutsch</button>
```

The last call wins. A failed load rejects and leaves the locale as it was.

`<I18nGroup>` passes a prefixed `t` to a render-prop child. `<I18nT>` and `t()` inside it are not prefixed:

```tsx
<I18nGroup prefix="profile">{({ t }) => <h2>{t('title')}</h2> /* profile.title */}</I18nGroup>
```

## Routing

The React Router adapter lives in a subpath so the main entry never imports `react-router-dom`. It needs `useLocation()` and `useNavigate()`, so create it inside a component under the router:

```tsx
// src/App.tsx
import { useMemo } from 'react'
import { BrowserRouter, Route, Routes, useLocation, useNavigate } from 'react-router-dom'
import { I18nLink, I18nProvider, I18nSwitcher } from '@i18n-micro/react'
import { createReactRouterAdapter } from '@i18n-micro/react/router'
import { i18n, locales } from './i18n'
import { About, Home } from './pages'

function Localized() {
  const location = useLocation()
  const navigate = useNavigate()
  // memoized: a new object on every render re-renders every `useI18n()` consumer
  const routingStrategy = useMemo(() => createReactRouterAdapter(locales, 'en', location, navigate), [location, navigate])
  return (
    <I18nProvider i18n={i18n} locales={locales} defaultLocale="en" routingStrategy={routingStrategy}>
      <I18nLink to="/about">About</I18nLink>
      <I18nSwitcher />
      <Routes>
        <Route path="/:locale?" element={<Home />} />
        <Route path="/:locale?/about" element={<About />} />
      </Routes>
    </I18nProvider>
  )
}

export default function App() {
  return (
    <BrowserRouter>
      <Localized />
    </BrowserRouter>
  )
}
```

The adapter prefixes every locale except the default (`/about`, `/de/about`) and renders `<I18nLink>` as React Router's `<Link>`. Set the locale from the URL yourself (for example from `useParams().locale` in an effect). For any other router write an adapter with `getCurrentPath`, `push` and `replace` (all required) — see [Router adapter](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#router-adapter).

## SSR

`renderToString` works: `useI18n()` has a server snapshot. Create one instance per request and add its dictionaries before you render, so requests in different locales do not share state, or pass plain data to the provider.

### Hydration

Numbers, plurals and text hydrate as they are. A date depends on the time zone and a relative date on the clock: set `timeZone` on the server and in the browser, and for `tdr` hand the browser the server's time with `now`. `<I18nT>` with `date` or `relativeDate` sets `suppressHydrationWarning`, so a difference does not fail hydration, but the server's text stays until the text changes. That reaches one level only: `children` that wrap the translation in an element still fail on a difference, so give those the same `timeZone`.

### Server Components

The package marks its client code with `'use client'`. `@i18n-micro/react/server` has `createI18n` and an `I18nT` without hooks that takes the instance as a prop, so the text stays out of the client bundle. Under the `react-server` condition, as in the Next.js app router, the main entry resolves to it too, but TypeScript does not know that by default: import from `/server`. `@i18n-micro/react/client` always gives the client entry.

```tsx
// app/[locale]/layout.tsx: a server component
import { cache } from 'react'
import { createI18n, I18nT } from '@i18n-micro/react/server'
import { I18nProvider } from '@i18n-micro/react/client'
import { loadMessages } from './messages'

const getI18n = cache(async (locale: string) => createI18n({ locale, messages: await loadMessages(locale) }))

export default async function Layout({ params, children }) {
  const { locale } = await params
  const i18n = await getI18n(locale)
  return (
    <I18nProvider locale={locale} messages={{ [locale]: i18n.resolveTranslations() }}>
      <h1>
        <I18nT i18n={i18n} keypath="title" />
      </h1>
      {children}
    </I18nProvider>
  )
}
```

Rendered through `react-server-dom-webpack`; a Next.js app itself has not been run against this.

## API

| Export                                                                                                                                                            | Entry                      |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `createI18n`, `ReactI18n`, `I18nProvider`, `useI18n`, `useT`, `useLocaleSwitch`                                                                                   | `@i18n-micro/react`        |
| `I18nT`, `I18nLink`, `I18nSwitcher`, `I18nGroup`                                                                                                                  | `@i18n-micro/react`        |
| `I18nContext`, `I18nConfigContext`, `useI18nContext`, `useI18nLocales`, `useI18nDefaultLocale`, `useI18nRouter`                                                   | `@i18n-micro/react`        |
| `defaultPlural`, `FormatService`, `interpolate`                                                                                                                   | `@i18n-micro/react`        |
| Types: `I18nRoutingStrategy`, `ReactI18nOptions`, `I18nProviderProps`, `UseI18nReturn`, component props, `TranslationKey`, `Locale`, `Translations`, `PluralFunc` | `@i18n-micro/react`        |
| `createReactRouterAdapter`                                                                                                                                        | `@i18n-micro/react/router` |
| `createI18n`, `ReactI18n`, `I18nT` (takes `i18n`)                                                                                                                 | `@i18n-micro/react/server` |

Full signatures: [React reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages/react).

## Preact

`@i18n-micro/preact` is built from the same source, on Preact itself, without `preact/compat`: the same instance, provider, hooks and components. Differences:

|                   | React                                     | Preact                                                                        |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Peer dependency   | `react` (+ optional `react-router-dom`)   | `preact` `^10.0.0 || ^11.0.0`, tested on 10.29 and 11.1                       |
| Instance class    | `ReactI18n`                               | `PreactI18n`                                                                  |
| Router adapter    | `createReactRouterAdapter` from `/router` | `createBrowserHistoryAdapter(locales, defaultLocale, ssrUrl?)` from `/router` |
| Re-render         | `useSyncExternalStore`                    | a layout-effect subscription that re-checks the store                         |
| Server Components | `/server`, `/client`                      | none                                                                          |

`createBrowserHistoryAdapter` works with any History API router (wouter, preact-router): `push` and `replace` call `history.pushState` / `replaceState` and dispatch `popstate`, and `<I18nLink>` renders a plain `<a>` that navigates through `push`. A server has no address bar: pass the request's URL as `ssrUrl`, or links and the switcher render as on `/`. In a browser the address bar wins.

```tsx
// src/main.tsx
import { render } from 'preact'
import { createI18n, I18nProvider } from '@i18n-micro/preact'
import { createBrowserHistoryAdapter } from '@i18n-micro/preact/router'
import { App } from './App'
import en from './locales/en.json'

const locales = [
  { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US', displayName: 'English' },
  { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE', displayName: 'Deutsch' },
]
const i18n = createI18n({ locale: 'en', fallbackLocale: 'en', messages: { en } })

render(
  <I18nProvider i18n={i18n} locales={locales} defaultLocale="en" routingStrategy={createBrowserHistoryAdapter(locales, 'en')}>
    <App />
  </I18nProvider>,
  document.getElementById('app')!,
)
```

Full signatures: [Preact reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages/preact).

# Runtime

`@i18n-micro/runtime` is the framework-agnostic i18n instance: dictionaries, `t()`, plurals, `Intl` formatting and a change subscription, with no `fs` and no framework. Use it in plain TypeScript, a web worker, an edge function, or as the base of your own binding. The React, Preact, Node and Astro packages extend this same class.

## Install

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @i18n-micro/runtime
```

```bash [npm]
npm install @i18n-micro/runtime
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @i18n-micro/runtime
```
::

No peer dependencies. For translation files on disk use [`@i18n-micro/node`](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/nodejs-package).

## Setup

```ts
import { createI18n } from '@i18n-micro/runtime'

const i18n = createI18n({
  locale: 'en',
  fallbackLocale: 'en',
  messages: {
    en: { greeting: 'Hello, {name}!', apples: 'no apples | one apple | {count} apples' },
    de: { greeting: 'Hallo, {name}!' },
  },
  routeMessages: {
    about: { en: { title: 'About us' } },
  },
})
```

All options (`plural`, `missingWarn`, `missingHandler`, `numberFormats`, `datetimeFormats`) are listed in [the instance](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#the-instance).

## Translate

```ts
i18n.t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) // 'Hello, Ada!'
i18n.tc('apples', 5) // '5 apples'
i18n.tn(1234.5) // '1,234.5'

i18n.setRoute('about')
i18n.t('title') // 'About us' (route dictionary)
i18n.t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) // 'Hello, Ada!' (root, still visible)
```

Load more dictionaries later:

```ts
i18n.loadMessages({ fr: { greeting: 'Bonjour, {name} !' } }, { about: { fr: { title: 'À propos' } } })
i18n.addTranslations('fr', { nav: { home: 'Accueil' } }) // deep merge; pass false to replace

await i18n.loadFromUrl('/locales/fr.json', { locale: 'fr' })
await i18n.loadFromUrl('/locales/pages/about/fr.json', { locale: 'fr', routeName: 'about' })
await i18n.loadFromUrls([
  { url: '/locales/en.json', locale: 'en' },
  { url: '/locales/de.json', locale: 'de' },
])
```

`loadFromUrl` uses `fetch` (pass `init` for headers) and throws on a non-OK response. `loadFromUrls` loads one after another.

## Switch locale

```ts
i18n.locale = 'de'
i18n.t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) // 'Hallo, Ada!'
```

Locale, route and dictionary changes notify subscribers, which is how framework bindings re-render:

```ts
const stop = i18n.subscribe(() => {
  document.querySelector('#greeting')!.textContent = i18n.t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) as string
})
i18n.locale = 'fr'
stop()
```

`getSnapshot()` returns a string that changes on every notification (for `useSyncExternalStore`-style stores).

## Per request

The instance holds one locale and one route. On a server, do not switch a shared instance per request: two concurrent requests would see each other's locale. `i18n.fork(locale)` gives a request its own: own locale, fallback and route; the same dictionaries, formatters and rules. Forking costs the same however many dictionaries there are. A fork sees writes to its parent until its first own write, and its writes stay in it. [Node.js](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/nodejs-package#per-request) adds `run`.

## API

| Member                                                                                                   | Notes                                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `t`, `ts`, `tc`, `tn`, `td`, `tdr`, `has`                                                                | see [Translate and format](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#translate-and-format) |
| `locale`, `fallbackLocale`                                                                               | get/set                                                                                  |
| `currentRoute`, `setRoute(name)`, `getRoute()`                                                           | active route, default `'index'`                                                          |
| `loadMessages(messages?, routeMessages?)`                                                                | merge many locales and routes at once                                                    |
| `addTranslations(locale, tree, merge = true)`, `addRouteTranslations(locale, route, tree, merge = true)` |                                                                                          |
| `loadFromUrl(url, { locale?, routeName?, init? })`, `loadFromUrls(entries)`                              | `fetch` JSON                                                                             |
| `hasTranslation(key)`                                                                                    | active locale, any route (unlike `has`, which checks the active route and root)          |
| `setTranslation(key, value)`, `resolveTranslations()`                                                    | write one key; read the merged tree                                                      |
| `clear()`, `clearCache()`                                                                                | drop every dictionary                                                                    |
| `subscribe(cb)`, `getSnapshot()`                                                                         | change notifications                                                                     |
| `storage`                                                                                                | `{ translations: Map<'locale:route', Translations> }`                                    |

A code that is no language tag gets its plurals from `localeIso: { ua: 'uk-UA' }`; `localeIsoMap(locales)` builds that from the entries of a locale list that have an `iso`.

Module exports: `createI18n`, `I18n`, `fetchJsonTranslations`, `FormatService`, `interpolate`, `localeIsoMap` and the types `I18nOptions`, `LoadFromUrlOptions`, `LoadFromUrlEntry`, `TranslationStorage`, `Translations`, `Locale`, `PluralFunc`. Full signatures: [package reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages/runtime).

  :::card

  title: Frameworks

  :::

  :::card

  :::

# Solid

`@i18n-micro/solid` gives SolidJS apps a signal-backed i18n instance, a provider, `useI18n()` and four components. Use it in a Solid app that is not built with Nuxt. Reads of `t()` inside JSX or effects track the locale, the route and the dictionaries; the shared model is in [Frameworks](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/).

## Install

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add @i18n-micro/solid
```

```bash [npm]
npm install @i18n-micro/solid
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add @i18n-micro/solid
```
::

Peer dependencies: `solid-js` `^1.8.0`; `@solidjs/router` `^0.15.4 || ^1.0.0` (optional, only for `@i18n-micro/solid/router`). Solid 2 is not supported yet.

## Setup

```tsx
// src/index.tsx
import { render } from 'solid-js/web'
import { createI18n, I18nProvider } from '@i18n-micro/solid'
import App from './App'
import en from './locales/en.json'

const locales = [
  { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US', displayName: 'English' },
  { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE', displayName: 'Deutsch' },
]

const i18n = createI18n({ locale: 'en', fallbackLocale: 'en', messages: { en } })

render(
  () => (
    <I18nProvider i18n={i18n} locales={locales} defaultLocale="en">
      <App />
    </I18nProvider>
  ),
  document.getElementById('root')!,
)
```

`<I18nProvider>` takes `i18n`, `locales`, `defaultLocale` and `routingStrategy`; an omitted prop keeps the outer provider's value, the instance included. `getLocaleName()` and `<I18nSwitcher>` read `locales`; without them they have nothing to list. Options are in [the instance](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#the-instance). The instance is the [runtime](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/runtime-package)'s, with one signal over its store.

## Translate

```tsx
import { useI18n } from '@i18n-micro/solid'

export function Greeting() {
  const { t, tc, tn } = useI18n()
  return (
    <>
      <h1>{t('greeting', { name: 'Ada' }) as string}</h1> {/* Hello, Ada! */}
      <p>{tc('apples', 3)}</p> {/* 3 apples */}
      <p>{tn(1234.5)}</p>
    </>
  )
}
```

Call the methods inside JSX or an effect so Solid tracks them, `localePath` and `getLocale` too; a value read once in the component body does not update. On the instance, track with `i18n.locale` and `i18n.currentRoute`: `i18n.getLocale()` stays plain, because writes read it. Reading the locale wakes on the locale alone, so an effect that reads it and loads a dictionary runs once. Do not destructure props or keep `t('key')` results in plain variables.

`useI18n()` returns `t`, `ts`, `tc`, `tn`, `td`, `tdr`, `has`, `locale` (an accessor: `locale()`), `getLocale`, `getLocales`, `defaultLocale()`, `getLocaleName`, `switchLocale`, `localePath`, `localeRoute`, `setRoute`, `getRoute`, `addTranslations`, `addRouteTranslations`, `resolveTranslations`, `setTranslation`, `clearCache` and `instance`.

```ts
const { addTranslations, addRouteTranslations, setRoute } = useI18n()

addTranslations('de', (await import('./locales/de.json')).default)
addRouteTranslations('en', 'about', { title: 'About us' })
setRoute('about') // t('title') now reads the 'about' dictionary first
```

## Switch locale

```ts
const { instance, switchLocale } = useI18n()

instance.locale = 'de' // only the locale
switchLocale('de') // the locale, then the adapter's push to the localized current path
```

Switching does not load anything; add the locale's dictionary first.

`<I18nGroup>` passes a prefixed `t` to a function child. `<I18nT>` and `t()` inside it are not prefixed:

```tsx
<I18nGroup prefix="profile">{({ t }) => <h2>{t('title')}</h2> /* profile.title */}</I18nGroup>
```

## Routing

The `@solidjs/router` adapter lives in a subpath so the main entry never imports the router. Call it under the router, typically in the router's `root`, where `useNavigate` and `useLocation` work:

```tsx
// src/App.tsx
import { Route, Router, useLocation, useNavigate, type RouteSectionProps } from '@solidjs/router'
import { I18nLink, I18nProvider, I18nSwitcher } from '@i18n-micro/solid'
import { createSolidRouterAdapter } from '@i18n-micro/solid/router'
import { i18n, locales } from './i18n'
import { About, Home } from './pages'

function Root(props: RouteSectionProps) {
  const routingStrategy = createSolidRouterAdapter(locales, 'en', useNavigate(), useLocation())
  return (
    <I18nProvider i18n={i18n} locales={locales} defaultLocale="en" routingStrategy={routingStrategy}>
      <I18nLink to="/about">About</I18nLink>
      <I18nSwitcher />
      {props.children}
    </I18nProvider>
  )
}

export default function App() {
  return (
    <Router root={Root}>
      <Route path="/:locale?" component={Home} />
      <Route path="/:locale?/about" component={About} />
    </Router>
  )
}
```

The adapter prefixes every locale except the default (`/about`, `/de/about`), and renders `<I18nLink>` as the router's `<A>`. `getCurrentPath` reads the router's reactive location, so active links and the switcher follow it; a custom strategy gets the same by reading a signal there. Note the argument order: `(locales, defaultLocale, navigate, location)`. For other routers write an adapter with `getCurrentPath`, `push` and `replace` (all required) — see [Router adapter](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#router-adapter).

## SSR

For server rendering, build with `vite-plugin-solid`: the package's `solid` export condition hands it the source, so it compiles for the server. The prebuilt `dist` is for the browser only. The instance has no `destroy()`; create one per app, or one per request on the server, and let it be garbage-collected.

## API

| Export                                                                                                                                            | Entry                      |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| `createI18n`, `SolidI18n`, `I18nProvider`, `useI18n`                                                                                              | `@i18n-micro/solid`        |
| `I18nT`, `I18nLink`, `I18nSwitcher`, `I18nGroup`                                                                                                  | `@i18n-micro/solid`        |
| `I18nContext`, `useI18nContext`, `useI18nLocales`, `useI18nDefaultLocale`, `useI18nRouter`                                                        | `@i18n-micro/solid`        |
| `defaultPlural`, `FormatService`, `interpolate`                                                                                                   | `@i18n-micro/solid`        |
| Types: `I18nRoutingStrategy`, `SolidI18nOptions`, `I18nProviderProps`, `UseI18nOptions`, `TranslationKey`, `Locale`, `Translations`, `PluralFunc` | `@i18n-micro/solid`        |
| `createSolidRouterAdapter`                                                                                                                        | `@i18n-micro/solid/router` |

Full signatures: [package reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages/solid).

# Types generator

`@i18n-micro/types-generator` reads every JSON file in your translation folder and writes a declaration that lists all keys. Add it when you want your editor to suggest keys in `t()`, `$t()` and `<I18nT keypath>`. It works as a Nuxt module and as a Vite or Rollup plugin, and regenerates when a file changes.

## Install

::code-group
```bash [pnpm]
pnpm add -D @i18n-micro/types-generator
```

```bash [npm]
npm install -D @i18n-micro/types-generator
```

```bash [yarn]
yarn add -D @i18n-micro/types-generator
```
::

Peer dependency: `@nuxt/kit` `^3.18.0 || ^4.0.0`. Only the `/nuxt` entry imports it; in a Vite-only project the peer warning can be ignored.

## Nuxt

```ts
// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  modules: ['nuxt-i18n-micro', '@i18n-micro/types-generator/nuxt'],
  i18n: {
    locales: [
      { code: 'en', iso: 'en-US' },
      { code: 'de', iso: 'de-DE' },
    ],
    defaultLocale: 'en',
    translationDir: 'locales',
  },
})
```

The module writes `.nuxt/types/i18n-micro.d.ts` and Nuxt adds it to the type context; nothing to include by hand. It reads `i18nTypes.translationDir`, else where `nuxt-i18n-micro` reads translations: `translationDir` (from `i18n` or inline module options, default `'locales'`) in every layer, and `additionalTranslationDirs`. Editing a JSON file under that folder regenerates the types in `nuxi dev`. `i18nTypes.outputFile` is ignored in Nuxt (a warning says so).

## Vite

`I18nTypesPlugin` is a Vite plugin, which Rollup also takes. For another bundler, call `generateTypes` in a script.

```ts
// vite.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vite'
import vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue'
import { I18nTypesPlugin } from '@i18n-micro/types-generator'

export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [
    vue(),
    I18nTypesPlugin({
      srcDir: process.cwd(),
      translationDir: 'src/locales',
      outputFile: 'src/i18n-micro.d.ts',
    }),
  ],
})
```

| Option           | Required | Notes                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `srcDir`         | yes      | Base directory; `translationDir` is resolved against it.                                   |
| `translationDir` | yes      | Folder with the JSON files (subfolders such as `pages/` included), or an array of folders. |
| `outputFile`     | no       | Where to write the declaration; default `<srcDir>/i18n-micro.d.ts`.                        |

The plugin generates once at build start and, on the dev server, regenerates 300 ms after a change in the folder. Make sure your `tsconfig.json` `include` covers the output file.

## Use the keys

The generated file augments `DefineLocaleMessage` in `@i18n-micro/types`, which turns `TranslationKey` into your keys:

```ts
declare module '@i18n-micro/types' {
  export interface DefineLocaleMessage {
    nav: object
    'nav.home': string
    'profile.title': string
  }
}
```

The keys are the ones `t()` answers, objects too, from every locale and every page file, with the type of their JSON value. `TranslationKey` is the union of those keys plus any string, so you get autocomplete, not errors: a misspelled or dynamic key still compiles. Params and return values are not typed.

For dynamic keys under a known prefix, `ScopedKey<'prefix'>` narrows to the matching keys:

```ts
import type { ScopedKey } from '@i18n-micro/types'

const statusText = (status: string) => t(`status.${status}` as ScopedKey<'status'>)
```

`TranslationKey` and `ScopedKey` come from `@i18n-micro/types` (React, Preact and Solid re-export `TranslationKey`; Vue does not).

## API

| Export                                 | Entry                              | Notes                                   |
| -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `I18nTypesPlugin(options)`             | `@i18n-micro/types-generator`      | Vite and Rollup plugin                  |
| `generateTypes(options)`               | `@i18n-micro/types-generator`      | writes the file, returns its path       |
| `getTypesString(options)`              | `@i18n-micro/types-generator`      | returns the declaration without writing |
| `formatKeyProperty(key)`               | `@i18n-micro/types-generator`      | helper                                  |
| Nuxt module (`configKey: 'i18nTypes'`) | `@i18n-micro/types-generator/nuxt` | option `translationDir`                 |

Full signatures: [package reference](https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/api/packages/types-generator).

::card-group
:card{icon="i-lucide-book-open" title="Frameworks" to="https://s00d.github.io/nuxt-i18n-micro/#typed-keys"}
